column1: Kernel: allow building in git worktree
column58:
The kernel currently fails to fetch git information if the top-level directory is a git worktree, since it scans for the existence of {{.git/config}} and parses data from it.

Git worktrees are very useful, but in a worktree, {{.git}} is not a directory, but a file pointing to the actual repository.

Fix that detection by being smarter.

every time a new parameter is set it takes at least around 0.5 seconds to go through all signal changed signals.

I could easily reproduce it with setting an value 4 times, causing our parameter changed signal to be triggered 2-3 times, taking about 1.2-1.6 seconds to be processed in total, which causes everything else to freeze.
I propose to implement the feature to allow us to listen to only one parameter in the desktop, prefiltering the changes, until the dbus interface of setupd is implemented.

column1: Error log floods when window has no _NET_WM_ICON property
column58:
When opening a video that doesn't set the _NET_WM_ICON X11 window property (e.g. ffplay gst-launch-1.0), the log is flooded with error messages at ~100ms intervals.

A bit of useful copilot:

*Root Cause:*

Two issues combine to produce the flood:

1.Broken retry counter in retry_icon_fetch() — The retry counter at OpenWindowManager.cpp:559 uses static auto COUNTER = 0, which is shared across all windows and all calls. Once any previous window exhausts the 3 retries (COUNTER exceeds 3), the check COUNTER++ == 3 will never be true again for subsequent windows, causing the 100ms timer to fire indefinitely.

2. Missing icon treated as error — In read_raw_image(), when XGetWindowProperty returns type == None (property doesn't exist), it's logged at error level. This is an expected condition for apps that don't set _NET_WM_ICON.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

Run: ffplay <any-video-file>
Observe system journal or /var/log/syslog
Assigning an icon stops the flooding: 
{{xprop -id <WINDOW_ID> -f _NET_WM_ICON 32c -set _NET_WM_ICON '1,1,4294901760' }}


*Suggested Fix:*

Replace the static counter with a per-window counter
Downgrade the "type wrong" log to debug level when error == 0 && result == 0 && type == None, since this simply means the property doesn't exist

column1: Special keys | Generated key mappings in hwdb not applied directly at boot
column58:
It seems that the key mappings in the generated hwdb-file are not being applied at boot. They require an extra “udevadm trigger” to work. 

The generator does update the hwdb and does a “udevadm trigger” on the input device, however this does not seem to work when the service starts at boot.

If you add a manual “udevadm trigger” call after boot everything works. Also if you add a new key mapping in a new HWI-variable, and restart the “igel-special-function-key-generator.service” then everything works. 

So this seems to be a problem unique to the boot-order.

h3. Affected devices

This exclusively affects devices which have a HWI_KEY of type “hwdb”. The issue is then limited to the mute-mic key on the following devices:

column1: Shell injection in post-mount script and install trigger due to unquoted user-controlled values
column58:
Several places in builder.py interpolate user-controlled values from JSON config files ({{dirs.json}}, install.json, app.json) into shell scripts without shell escaping, allowing arbitrary command injection.

*Affected locations:*

# *Post-mount script generation* (lines ~1634-1640): {{full_path}}, {{permissions}}, {{user}}, and {{group}} from {{dirs.json}} are written unquoted into a bash script:

{code:python}post_mount_script += f'mkdir -p {full_path}\n'
post_mount_script += f'chmod {permissions} {full_path}\n'
post_mount_script += f'chown {user or ""}:{group or ""} {full_path}\n'{code}

# *Install trigger command* (line ~1653): {{app_name}} from app.json is interpolated unquoted into a shell command:

{code:python}install_trigger_command = str(self.config.app_helper_path) + f' trigger --action install --app {app_name} --type'{code}

While {{app_name}} is validated by {{app_name_is_compliant_to_rules()}} (alphanumeric + underscore only), the validation and the script generation are in separate modules and could diverge.

# *Strip commands* (line ~549): File paths are double-quoted but not properly escaped, leaving {{$()}}, backticks, and {{!}} as injection vectors:

{code:python}strip_commands += f'strip --strip-all --preserve-dates "{file_to_strip}"\n'{code}

*Fix:* Use {{shlex.quote()}} for all user-controlled values interpolated into shell scripts. The {{delayed_chown_fakeroot}} method was already fixed with this pattern and should serve as the reference:

{code:python}f"/bin/chown --no-dereference {shlex.quote(user + ':' + group)} {shlex.quote(str(path))}\n"{code}

Apply the same pattern to all three locations.

*Severity:* High
*Component:* Builder, Security
*Affected File:* builder.py

column1: ZIP Slip path traversal vulnerability in checker's partition extraction
column58:
In checker.py line 111, {{zipfile.extract()}} is called on {{.ipkg}} files without validating that ZIP entry names don't contain path traversal sequences like work:

{code:python}with zipfile.ZipFile(ipkg_package_file, 'r') as zip_file:
    for filename in zip_file.namelist():
        if Path(filename).suffix != '.igelfs':
            continue
        zip_file.extract(filename, self.tmp_dir){code}

A crafted {{.ipkg}} file with an entry named e.g. {{../../etc/cron.d/malicious.igelfs}} would be extracted outside the intended temp directory, allowing arbitrary file writes on the filesystem.

*Fix:* Validate that the resolved extraction path stays within {{self.tmp_dir}} before extracting:

{code:python}member_path = (self.tmp_dir / filename).resolve()
if not str(member_path).startswith(str(self.tmp_dir.resolve())):
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Checker', f'Path traversal detected in ZIP entry: {filename}')
    continue
zip_file.extract(filename, self.tmp_dir){code}

Note: Python 3.12+ added the {{filter}} parameter ({{extraction_filter='data'}}) to {{ZipFile.extract()}} which prevents this class of vulnerability natively. If the minimum Python version is raised to 3.12, that would be the preferred approach.

*Severity:* Critical
*Component:* Checker, Security
*Affected File:* checker.py

column1: New DHCP options for rmagent auto-registering break IGEL specific encapsulated options
column58:
Implemented evaluation of new DHCP options for rmagent auto-registering break IGEL specific encapsulated options which is made with DHCP option 43 introducing vendor space options (vendor specific encapsulation).

This is caused by '-' character in names of the new options:

* igelrmserver-port

column1: TEST
Dual Boot - adjust installer sequence: ensure IGEL OS partition is written before bootloader installation
column58:
The current installer workflow does not explicitly guarantee that the IGEL OS partition is fully written and verified before proceeding with bootloader installation.

This can lead to potential issues where the bootloader is installed without a properly prepared or validated OS partition.

We need to update the installation sequence to enforce correct ordering and ensure system integrity.

h3. *Expected Behavior*

* The IGEL OS partition must be:
** Fully written
** Verified 
* Only after successful completion should the installer proceed with bootloader installation.

h3. *Proposed Change*

* Modify installer workflow to:
*# Write IGEL OS partition
*# Validate successful write 
*# Proceed with bootloader installation only upon success
* Add error handling:
** If partition write fails → abort bootloader installation
** Provide clear error messaging/logging
column223:
* Bootloader installation does not start unless OS partition write is confirmed successful
* Installer logs clearly show partition write completion before bootloader step
* Failure in partition write prevents further installation steps
column244: The installation process has been updated to enforce the correct sequence of steps, reducing the risk of incomplete or inconsistent system setups.

column1: Inconsistent return type (None vs False) in __write_signature_to_partition error handling
column58:
In signer.py line ~694, the generic BaseException handler returns {{None}} while the TimeoutExpired handler returns {{False}}:

{noformat}except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as err:
    process.kill()
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Signer', f'Error writing signature: {err}')
    return False
except BaseException as err:
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Signer', f'Error writing signature: {err}')
    return None    # ← inconsistent with False above{noformat}

While callers currently use {{if not ...}} which treats both identically, the inconsistent return type violates the method's contract (docstring says "True if success, else false") and could cause subtle issues if callers ever check {{is False}} or {{is None}}.

*Fix:* Return {{False}} in both exception handlers.

column1: File handle leak in Extractor when redirectOut is configured and extraction fails
column58:
In extractor.py line ~91, when the redirectOut option is configured, a file handle is opened but not closed on the error path:

{noformat}stdout = Path(path).open('w', encoding='utf-8')
# ...
if process.returncode != 0:
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Extractor', f'Failed to run: {extract_command}')
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Extractor', 'Output: ' + process.stderr)
    return False   # ← file handle 'stdout' is never closed

if stdout != subprocess.DEVNULL:
    stdout.close(){noformat}

When extraction fails and redirectOut is set, the file handle is leaked. Over many failed extractions this could exhaust file descriptors.

*Fix:* Use a {{try/finally}} block or a context manager to ensure the file handle is always closed.

column1: Regex error message displays class descriptor instead of actual error text
column58:
In builder.py line ~332, the re.error exception is caught but the error message is read from the class attribute instead of the exception instance:

{noformat}except re.error:
    self.report.add(ReportType.Error, 'Builder', f'Failed to compile regex: {re.error.msg}'){noformat}

re.error.msg accesses the class-level method descriptor, not the actual error message of the caught exception. The error report will show something like <method 'msg' of 're.error'> instead of the actual regex compilation error.

*Fix:* Capture the exception instance: except re.error as e: and then use e.msg.

column1: Shell injection vulnerability in delayed_chown_fakeroot via unquoted user/group values
column58:
In builder.py line ~361, user and group values from app configuration files are injected unquoted into a shell script:

{noformat}f.write(f"/bin/chown --no-dereference {user or ''}:{group or ''} '{path}'\n"){noformat}

The user and group values originate from install.json, dirs.json, and input.json configuration files. A maliciously crafted owner field (e.g. {{'; rm -rf / #}}) could execute arbitrary commands during the fakeroot build step. The path is single-quoted but a path containing a single-quote would also break the quoting.

*Fix:* Use {{shlex.quote()}} for all three interpolated values (user, group, and path).

column1: chmod crashes with ValueError when restoring file permissions after stripping ELF binaries
subprocess_run returns None on FileNotFoundError causing AttributeError crash in all callers
column58:
In utils.py line ~174, when a command binary is not found, subprocess_run returns {{None}}:

{noformat}except FileNotFoundError:
    logger.error(f'FileNotFound: {command[0]}')
    return None{noformat}

Every caller in the codebase accesses process.returncode without checking for {{None}}. If any external tool (strip, {{fakeroot}}, {{parsebk}}, apt-get, {{mksquashfs}}, {{compress_igelfs}}, etc.) is not installed or not on PATH, the program crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'returncode' instead of producing a useful error message.

*Fix:* Return CompletedSubProcess(1, '', f'FileNotFound: {command[0]}') instead of {{None}} so callers handle it through the normal error-reporting path.

column1: rmagent | Ensure queued messages are sent before disconnect
column58:
When disconnecting from the UMS server, the rmagent must ensure that all queued messages are sent before closing the websocket connection connection.
Current implementation just ends the websocket process and sending of a queued message isn’t reliable. That can cause that the UMS will never get the response to its releasetc command and so the UMS will not remove the device from the database.
Solution:

* Signal to the websocket process that it has to disconnect
* Wait for the disconnect event from the websocket process
* Terminate the websocket process by sending SIGTERM

column1: Container with same name can be created if it has a different config
column58:
To reproduce:

* create two Compose configuration files which have the same container name but different images, e.g.:
{noformat}# alpine_latest.yml
services:
  alpine:
    container_name: alpine
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:latest
    command: [
      "sh",
      "-c",
      "sleep 5"
    ]
    network_mode: none
# alpine_old.yml
services:
  alpine:
    container_name: alpine
    image: docker.io/library/alpine:3.18
    command: [
      "sh",
      "-c",
      "sleep 5"
    ]
    network_mode: none{noformat}
* from the GUI, create a container using one of the configuration files
* afterwards, create a container using the other configuration file

Result: GUI will show two containers with the same name, but when trying to access the old one, it will not be possible. This can be done multiple times and will look similar to the following:

!bug.png|width=686,alt="bug.png"!

What happens behind the scenes is that podman-compose lets you create a new container with the same name - it silently removes the old container and creates the new one.

column1: Sidebar status dot and container state label are out of sync after Start/Stop/Restart
column58:
After performing a Start, Stop, or Restart action on a container, the sidebar status dot and the "State:" field on the container detail page are out of sync when the runtime-returned container name is not explicitly overridden with the GUI-registered name in _refresh_container_ui().

The current code works around this by silently forcing container_info.name to the GUI-registered name before calling _update_sidebar_row() and _add_container_page(). Without this override, the sidebar row lookup fails because it relies on the name used at registration time, causing the status dot to not update while the detail page reflects the correct state.

19/Mar/26 1:59 PM;712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a;[~accountid:712020:076bb861-e2c0-4f65-9b3c-0bb2cb01b538] With the help of [~accountid:712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57] and [~accountid:712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8]  (thanks!), we found out what is happening and what the problem is:

what happens:

* when the ZSTray.service is stopped (via {{systemctl --user stop ZSTray}} or via UI / tray icon), we saw that the {{graphical-session.target}} gets stopped
* stopping {{graphical-session.target}} leads to stopping of several other services, like our {{igel-windowmanager}} => no taskbar, no title bars etc.

Reason for stopping the {{graphical-session.target}} is the configuration of the service ZSTray.service. The service “wants” graphical-session.target.

!image-20260319-122825.png|width=512,alt="image-20260319-122825.png"!

The problem is that it is the only service who “wants” it. Because of that, when shutting down ZSTray, it will lead to shutdown of graphical-session.target, too. That’s really bad, because it (gracefully) closes many other services like our window manager.

!image-20260319-125310.png|width=512,alt="image-20260319-125310.png"!

[~accountid:712020:076bb861-e2c0-4f65-9b3c-0bb2cb01b538] The main question is why the ZSTray service “Wants” graphical-session.target. It is the only service in the system doing it. I would give that information to the app developers and ask them to change it.

==

We tried something on base_system side (adding “Wants=graphical-session.target” in our window manager service), which also worked. But that’s a risky change we do not want to add in the late phase right now.

==

[~accountid:712020:f528bc65-6fe5-4a0c-b88d-975084b91e75] [~accountid:712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57] FYI

19/Mar/26 3:57 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;anyway,
we should cover such cases in the base_system.
{{graphical-session.target}} should be active, we should pull this in.

Quote from [https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.special.html#graphical-session.target|https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.special.html#graphical-session.target] 

{quote}A target for a particular session (e. g. gnome-session.target) starts and stops "graphical-session.target" with "BindsTo=graphical-session.target".{quote}

-We could add this BindsTo=graphical-session.target to our igel-desktop.target for example.-
{{graphical-session.target}} needs some permanent {{WantedBy=}} or {{RequiredBy=}}, otherwise it will stop, when the last unit stops, which {{Wants=}} or {{Requires=}} {{graphical-session.target}}.
That’s because {{graphical-session.target}} has {{StopWhenUnneeded=yes}} .
And when {{graphical-session.target}} stops, also {{xdg-desktop-portal.service}} is stopped, because {{xdg-desktop-portal.service}} is {{PartOf=graphical-session.target}} .
And when {{xdg-desktop-portal.service}} stops, also {{igel-windowmanager.service}} is stopped, because {{igel-windowmanager.service}}  {{Requires=xdg-desktop-portal.service}} .
And we end up with no windowmanager.

So, I suggest to add {{Requires=graphical-session.target}} to {{igel-desktop.target}}

Risk is low, I would say.

column376:
23/Mar/26 11:49 AM;712020:9faabc93-72fc-451e-b514-dd2fd1240c23;Nevermind, I’ll do it via env variables.

Disabling DRI3 completely in the server config would make testing if DRI3 works better at a later point in time more difficult and has drawbacks when it comes to Vulkan and Xwayland on Wayland: Vulkan pretty much always needs DRI3 to be available, and Xwayland only offers hardware acceleration on Wayland if DRI3 is available.

Going with the environment variable makes the scheme more flexible - and by unsetting the variable that disables DRI3, individual applications can still be started with DRI3 support enabled.

column1: Container sidebar status dot not reflecting real container state after start/stop operations
column58: After a Start or Stop operation completes, the sidebar status dot is updated based on the triggered action rather than the actual container state fetched from the runtime. This can lead to the sidebar showing an incorrect state if the operation partially fails or if the container state differs from what was requested. The container detail page correctly shows the real state (via GetContainerInfo), but the sidebar dot is not kept in sync with it.

* OSVersion: base system 12.8 rc 11

* set System->Power Options->System-> Lid close action while -/not plugged in to “Suspend“
* Connect any number of external monitors to the laptop

### Expected Behavior

column1: IMH | closing encrypted LV immediately after importing .vmdk from .ova via nbdkit subprocess causes data loss
column58:
Calling close_crypt_lv() immediately after importing a disk image via subprocess pair with nbdkit and qemu-img convert causes data corruption.

When run remotely with debugger via vscode this does not occur.

Things I’ve tried that did not make a difference:

* Changing cache settings for qemu-img convert
* Pausing via sleep() before closing
* Calling sync() before closing
* Calling dmsetup suspend/resume before closing
* Using communicate instead of wait() for nbdkit subprocess
* Using psutil to terminate subprocess

Workaround is closing after import is done. Leaving the decrypted LV open does not affect normal usage, one problem is that the user can not delete the volume in the Igel storage pool without starting and stopping the VM first.

column1: Podman compose uses incompatible network mode when network is not specified explicitly
column58:

The problem is that this network seems to be a bridge network, thus failing when trying to start the container in rootless mode, due to the operating system missing the veth kernel module:

{noformat}$ podman start 12d0f5ab800b26958ef99e1ebc102fc96353d2aa8ca3c6b4b033f027420b3a81
WARN[0000] aardvark-dns binary not found, container dns will not be enabled 
Error: unable to start container "12d0f5ab800b26958ef99e1ebc102fc96353d2aa8ca3c6b4b033f027420b3a81": netavark: create veth pair: Netlink error: Operation not supported (os error 95){noformat}

Even though the podman configuration specifies that, by default, no network should be used, “podman compose” overrides that default by explicitly creating and specifying a network, as can be seen in the command above.

This can be “fixed” by explicitly specifying a network mode in the Compose configuration, e.g.:

{noformat}network_mode: none{noformat}

, or:

{noformat}network_mode: slirp4netns{noformat}

But since we don’t control the Compose configuration, we should find a way to override this default, so that customers who don’t explicitly specify a network mode are not affected.

column1: Unreliable evaluation of rmagent state during onboarding
column58:
Unreliable evaluation of the rmagent state during onboarding, this situation can occur in conjunction with a long response time from the UMS/ICG server or if the server is unreachable for some reasons (network or other outage) and the rmagent has to try then an alternative server. 

In that case the rmagent is blocked for the whole onboarding procedure and requesting of the rmagent state ends in a timeout error which isn’t properly handled and leads to this erroneously decision.

column1: Investigate incomplete silent uninstall behavior for IGEL Dual Boot installer (unins000.exe /verysilent /norestart)
column58:
Silent uninstall of the IGEL Dual Boot application using {{C:\Program Files\IGEL\DualBoot\unins000.exe /verysilent /norestart}} appears to remove the partition correctly, but does not complete a full uninstall. Residual artifacts remain, including the install directory, WMI entries, registry entries, and the application listing in Programs and Features.
By contrast, uninstall initiated from Programs and Features appears to invoke {{unins000.exe}} as well, but runs longer and completes a full cleanup.

We need to investigate why these two uninstall paths behave differently and determine how to support a fully clean unattended uninstall for enterprise automation tools such as SCCM and Intune.

*Background / Customer Need*
Customers need to remove the Dual Boot app through automated deployment and endpoint management tools, using silent options such as {{/verysilent /norestart}}. They cannot rely on manual removal through Programs and Features on each endpoint.
Current behavior makes the silent uninstall unsuitable for enterprise use because it leaves the system in a partially uninstalled state.

*Suggested Reproduction Steps*

# Install IGEL Dual Boot on a test machine.
# Run:
{{C:\Program Files\IGEL\DualBoot\unins000.exe /verysilent /norestart}}
# Verify:
#* Partition removal
#* Remaining install folder
#* Remaining WMI entries
#* Remaining registry entries
#* Remaining Programs and Features entry
# Reinstall if needed.
# Uninstall via Programs and Features.
# Compare:
#* Child processes
#* Command-line arguments
#* Execution duration
#* Cleanup steps performed
#* Resulting system state
column223:
* Root cause of incomplete silent uninstall is identified and documented
* Engineering confirms whether current behavior is a bug or unsupported scenario
* A supported unattended uninstall method is defined for SCCM/Intune use
* If bug confirmed, fix scope is identified
* Silent uninstall can achieve parity with Programs and Features uninstall, or a documented equivalent enterprise-safe uninstall method is provided
* Validation steps exist to confirm no residual WMI, registry, install folder, or Programs and Features entries remain after automated uninstall

column1: OS12 device shows as connected when postconnect/updatedeviceinfo times out
column58:
When an *OS12 device* connects, the system may show the device as *connected* even if the {{postconnect/updatedeviceinfo}} request *times out*.

In this scenario, the device connection process is not fully completed because the {{updatedeviceinfo}} call fails due to a timeout. However, the device state in the system is still reported as *connected*, which can lead to an *incorrect connection status*.

This may cause confusion or inconsistent device state handling, since the device appears connected even though the post-connection update step did not finish successfully.

*Expected behavior*
If {{postconnect/updatedeviceinfo}} times out, the device should either:

* not be marked as connected, or
* the failure should be clearly reflected in the device state.

*Actual behavior*
The device is shown as *connected* despite the {{postconnect/updatedeviceinfo}} timeout.

column1: Elo touchscreen | elo-monitor-config does not work due to inconsistensies with x11/setup get_drm names
column58:
Our {{elo-monitor-config}} script is not working correctly when more than one monitor is used in the setup. It ends up exiting early with {{"Could not calibrate touch on Error as it is not available"}} messages in the logs. This is due to inconsistencies in which get_drm names are used, setup vs x11. For example: dp1 vs DisplayPort-0

It seems like it was expected that {{CONN_ORDER}} follows the setup naming convention, i.e. dpX - but the {{/usr/libexec/igel-system-tray/get_connector_order}} script returns X11 names. In order to not change too much of the logic, we can add a simple loop which converts the names to setup names as the script expects. 

h3. Details

{{get_drm conv [setup|xrandr|x11|kernel] <name> [setup|xrandr|x11|kernel] : converts connector names}}

* Converts the name from the first given format to the second
* The second one can be omitted, and then {{x11}} will be converted into {{setup}}, and {{setup}} into {{x11}}
* So doing {{get_drm conv setup dp1}} will result in {{DisplayPort-0}} but {{get_drm conv setup DisplayPort-0}} will result in an empty output, since the {{setup}} indicates “from setup to x11”

*Code snippet:*

{noformat}else
    i="${CONN_ORDER#    }"
    i="${i#   }"
    i="${i#  }"
    i="${i# }"
    i="${i%%* }"
    x11PortName=`get_drm conv setup $i`
    if [ "$x11PortName" != "" ]; then
        CONN_ORDER="${CONN_ORDER/ $i / }"
    else
        # use screen number 1
        x11PortName="$(xrandr --current --verbose | tac \
                   | sed -n "/IGEL_OUTPUT_ORDINAL:[ \t]\{1,\}1/,/^[^ \t]\{1,\} / s/^\([^ \t]\{1,\}\) .*/\1/ p")"
        i=`get_drm conv x11 $x11PortName`
        if [ "$i" != "" ]; then
            CONN_ORDER="${CONN_ORDER/ $i / }"
        fi
    fi
fi{noformat}

* {{CONN_ORDER}} uses the x11 name format: {{DisplayPort-0}}
* The last {{i="${i%%* }"}} will remove everything, leaving an empty string behind → it should be {{i="${i%% *}"}} to get the first connector
* {{get_drm conv setup $i}} transforms a setup name ({{dp1}}) to an x11 name ({{DisplayPort-0}}), but since we are already using the x11 name, the output of this command is empty
* {{get_drm conv x11 $x11PortName}}will transform an x11 name ({{DisplayPort-0}}) to a setup name ({{dp1}}), but {{CONN_ORDER}} uses the x11 names → inconsistent

*Problem:*

{{CONN_ORDER}} is in X11 format which causes the inconsistencies further down the script. Least-intervention-solution is to convert this to setup names.

column1: Remove registry flag after enabling Controlled Folder Access to prevent duplicate execution errors
column58:
During the IGEL installation process, Controlled Folder Access (CFA) is enabled to protect C:\Program Files\IGEL. The process works as intended by checking for Microsoft Defender presence, ensuring no third-party antivirus is active, and confirming Defender Antivirus is enabled. A registry flag is set during installation to indicate that CFA should be applied.

*Current Behavior:*

CFA is enabled successfully after installation.

The registry flag indicating CFA execution remains in the system.

If the installation process or related scripts run again, CFA tries to apply a second time, which can generate errors.

*Expected Behavior:*

After CFA is successfully enabled, the registry flag should be deleted.

This ensures CFA is applied only once and prevents errors from re-execution.
column223: IGEL now ensures that Controlled Folder Access (CFA) protection for C:\Program Files\IGEL is applied only once during installation. After CFA is enabled, the temporary registry flag used to trigger CFA is automatically removed, preventing errors if installation scripts run again.
column244: IGEL now safely enables CFA on compatible systems, automatically cleans up the trigger registry flag, prevents errors on re-runs, and skips CFA on systems that don’t meet prerequisites.
column303:
# CFA Enablement Check:

Install IGEL on a system meeting all CFA prerequisites (Defender enabled, no third-party antivirus).

Confirm CFA is successfully enabled for C:\Program Files\IGEL.

# Registry Flag Removal:

After CFA is applied, verify that the registry flag used to trigger CFA is deleted.

# No Duplicate Execution Errors:

Re-run the installation or CFA script.

Confirm that no errors occur related to CFA being applied a second time.

# Conditional Skip:

On systems not meeting CFA prerequisites (e.g., third-party antivirus present), confirm that CFA is skipped and no registry flag is set.

column1: OpenGLEnabled registry setting ignored/missleading -> requires wfclient.ini override
column58:
The OpenGLEnabled parameter defined in wfclient.config.param does not match the actual runtime behavior in IGEL OS 12.

Although the registry shows:

{{OpenGLEnabled=false}}

OpenGL remains enabled at runtime due to the Citrix default value (true). As a result, modifying the registry key has no effect on the ICA session behavior.

Currently, in order to force the use of H264 and be able to check the relevant logs with {{tail -f /var/log/user/ctxh264.log}}, we need to manually add *OpenGLEnabled=False* in {{/userhome/.ICAClient/wfclient.ini}} under {{[Thinwire3.0]}}.

To effectively disable OpenGL and force H264 usage, it is currently required to manually override the parameter in:

{{/userhome/.ICAClient/wfclient.ini}}

by adding under [Thinwire3.0] : 


{{OpenGLEnabled=False}}

*Current configuration*

wfclient.config.param

{noformat}<OpenGLEnabled>
    value=<false>
    type=<bool>
    runtime=<true>
    cwaparam=<OpenGLEnabled>
    cwadefault=<false>
    displayname[en_us]=<OpenGLEnabled>
    tooltip[en_us]=<Improves the performance of graphics usage by supporting OpenGL library>
</OpenGLEnabled>{noformat}

*Observed Behavior*

* Registry reports OpenGLEnabled=false
* Citrix runtime behavior still enables OpenGL
* Registry modification does not affect session behavior
* Disabling OpenGL requires manual wfclient.ini modification

*Expected Behavior*

One of the following should apply:

The registry value {{OpenGLEnabled=false }}should correctly disable OpenGL at runtime.

or

The configuration should reflect the real Citrix default by setting:

{{cwadefault=<true>}}

to avoid a mismatch between registry state and runtime behavior.

20/Mar/26 1:28 PM;712020:eb11546b-6213-4618-8a1d-69eff0c6a0f2;From my perspective, two issues require investigation.

* Why are read-write (rw) partitions deleted during multistage? This contradicts the architecture's intent.
** During multistage, all rw partitions must be preserved for later use, even if the attached app is removed. Due to the fact that if the updated do so, it will remove user configuration and other important information from the user. 
** Free space removal should occur only on read-only (ro) partitions. If removing all ro partitions leaves insufficient free space, multistage must be canceled before starting. 
* Additionally, the rw partition Python handlers should not be invoked.

----

Possible solutions:

* Identify where rw partitions are deleted and prevent their removal.
* To avoid adverse effects on rw partition creation, modify the rw Python scripts to block rw partition regeneration during multistage.

column1: igel-shutdown-dialog: dangling processes if called multiple times
column58:
We see a problem of dangling igel-shutdown-dialog processes, if it is triggered multiple times.

Each time, calling /bin/igel-shutdown-dialog,  a new process is spawned.
But if there is already one shutdown-dialog open, no new special-notification will be created by igel-notify, and the next processes will never terminate.
Only the first process will be exited.

Probably to be solved inside igel-notify.
Here:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-notify/browse/igel-shutdown-dialog/src/igel-shutdown-dialog.cpp#241|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-notify/browse/igel-shutdown-dialog/src/igel-shutdown-dialog.cpp#241]
if {{client.showNotification(notification, closeCallback);}} does not return the dbus-object-path of the special notification, but only empty string, something went wrong and we need to quit.

column1: igelpkg: Handle excludes of folders in install.json correctly
column58:
h3. Impact

The bug affects the installation process. It does not handle folder exclusions in the {{install.json}} file correctly. Users may find that certain folders are not ignored during installation as expected. This occurs when a user wants to create a folder listed in the ignore list via a {{dirs.json}} as a persistent folder. The {{igelpkg}} complains that this folder already exists in the Debian archive file.

h3. Expected behaviour

The system should ignore paths specified in the {{exclude}} entry of {{install.json}}. If a path ends with “/“, it should be trimmed for proper exclusion.

h3. Actual behaviour

Currently, the regex mechanism fails to ignore a folder path in the {{exclude}} entry if it ends with “/“ during installation.

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Create an {{install.json}} file.
* Add an {{exclude}} entry with a folder path that ends with “/“.
* Attempt to install using this {{install.json}}.
* Observe that the folder is not ignored.

h3. Environment

N/A

h3. Workarounds

N/A

h3. Other information

Examples of the {{install.json}} file:

{code:json}# Fail
[
  {
    "source": ".*",
    "excludes": [
      "/usr/share/doc/",
    ]
  },
  ...
]

# Good
[
  {
    "source": ".*",
    "excludes": [
      "/usr/share/doc",
    ]
  },
  ...
]{code}

12/Mar/26 5:11 PM;712020:3f68fc46-4312-421c-883d-b96b5bc1e2bb;General icon analysis and solution tries:

Apparently the applications have a couple of bugs that play together:
In these scenarios we are loading the icon from the X11 Atom  {{_NET_WM_ICON}}
When they are loaded at first they get the RDP web access icon. This icon has the issue, that it tells us it has the following sizes 16, 32, 64, 128 pixels, but in reality the 128 is just pixelporridge and causes the graphic glitches seen in this screenshot. (128 is always fetched, as it is the preferred size)
At some point this icon data gets updated, but doesn't respect the protocol and does not publicize the changes. This seems to be random.
after this happens we get the correct icon. This icon is always at the size 32 (as far as I have observed).
I implemented a different (older) way to fetch icons by getting it through {{WM_HINTS}} this did not solve the problem. This solution seems to also not work for Citrix, but I will retest it once I have access to a machine/account with this problem.
Conclusion:
updating the rdp icons in an interval may be the only way to get an correct icon

Possible solutions to be implemented in combination:
- Limiting the icon size to 32 pixels → removes glitches, but shows the rdp web access icon
- Set a timed fetch for the icons, once there is an update (has only the 32x32 size available), we update it once

I think if we should use {{wnck}} in the future, as xfce uses it and works perfectly fine. I think we could dodge a lot of icon issues here.

column1: Avoid stale websocket tunnel connection to the local service
column58: While tunneling VNC or telnet through a websocket connection to the UMS, the rmagent is first connecting the local service and then it is establishing a websocket connection to the UMS/ICG server. A such order can provoke a stale connection to the local service, when connection to the UMS side wasn’t established at the first try. To avoid this situation, the rmagent must first establish the remote connection of the tunnel and then the local connection.

* Rely on enterprise GPU security features

column1: Chromium: possibly corrupt profile when starting Chromium multiple times
column58:
If Chromium is started while it is already starting but no window is opened yet, it opens multiple windows and a dialog pops up: “profile error occurred“.

We need to detect if chromium is already running but no window is running yet and only remove singletons etc if that is not the case.

Sadly, there is no proper way to check for that. We might either check for the wrapper process (python3 /services/chromium/bin/chromium-wrapper /services/chromium/usr/bin/chromium-browser_orig) or rely on a file that could be created when starting Chromium (MUST be removed when closing…might cause issues).

The chromium-wrapper.py contains the part to be edited:

{code:python}# remove SingletonLock files if no other instance of Chromium is running
if not _other_windows_running():
    clear_singletons(PROFILE_PATH){code}

column1: Cntlm service starts before network is online in certain scenarios
column58:

column1: Citrix Cloud SSO authentication fails with IGEL config (AuthManConfig.xml) but works with Citrix default config

h3. Issue description : 

When using the default Citrix configuration (usecitrixconfig) without any modifications, Citrix Cloud authentication via SSO works as expected:

* Citrix session opens correctly.
* Cloud credentials prompt appears ([ipgtest.de|http://ipgtest.de]).
* Store enumeration and app launch work as expected.

However, when using our custom configuration (modified AuthManConfig.xml), authentication does not complete.

h3. Behavior with IGEL Configuration:

* The session starts but hangs at process:
** {{citrix-WebKitWebProcess}}
* The process does not proceed to credential prompt or successful enumeration.
* After 60 seconds, storebrowse times out:
** {{Timeout after 60s: storebrowse.ctx --enumerate --icons best https://ipgdev.cloud.com/citrix/store/discovery}}
* A hard reset is triggered, killing all Citrix-related processes.
* Second attempt also times out during enumeration.
* Final result:
** {{Failed with result 'exit-code'}}

h3. Relevant Log Extract:

{{ERROR [_run_storebrowse_once:121] Timeout after 60s: /services/cwa/opt/Citrix/ICAClient/util/storebrowse.ctx --enumerate --icons best https://ipgdev.cloud.com/citrix/store/discovery}}
{{ERROR [main:177] Second attempt timed out during enumeration. Hard reset: killing all Citrix-related processes.}}
{{ERROR [storebrowse_with_auth:284] Error: storebrowse [...] returns -9}}
{{igel-appwrap-cwa-cwa1.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'}}

Added the following files for comparison:

* Default AuthManConfig.xml (working).
* IGEL  AuthManConfig.xml (non-working).

Expected Behavior:
IGEL configuration should allow Citrix Cloud SSO authentication to proceed identically to the default configuration, including successful store enumeration and application launch.

Actual Result:
Authentication hangs at {{citrix-WebKitWebProcess}}, store enumeration times out twice, Citrix processes are killed, and the service exits with result {{'exit-code'}}.

With {{app.cwa.authman.authmanlite.gnomekeyringdisabled}} set to {{false}}, {{app.cwa.configuration.ssoigelwebkit}} enabled, {{app.cwa.authman.fido2enabled}} enabled, when connecting to Citrix Cloud i always enter in a login loop and get the “Response for Secondary Token is not 200/400/404” error message.

!image-20260226-140539.png|width=767,alt="image-20260226-140539.png"!



Tested on : 

* base_system-12.8.0-1.rc.6+DEV (same with 12.7.4 DEV)

Replaced the AuthManConfig.xml with the Citrix default one in {{/services/cwa/opt/Citrix/ICAClient/config/}} and Citrix Cloud connection worked as expected while having {{app.cwa.configuration.login.use_igel_uidialoglib }}enabled.

First, I aligned the AuthManConfig.xml on the non-working system with the working configuration. I also tested the Citrix-documented parameters (validated separately on Ubuntu), including:

{noformat}<key>SharedAuthContextEnabled</key>

<key>FIDO2Enabled</key>

column1: Touchpad | Ordering between igel-touchpad.service and igel-synclient-config.service causes issues
column58:
h3. Background

Touchpad configuration is handled by two systemd services:

* {{igel-touchpad.service}}
* {{igel-synclient-config.service}}

When working on: [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13910|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13910|smart-link] I implemented a fix which changed the systemd services to a different target, and some of the “After” dependencies. Originally, there was an ordering between the the services in {{igel-touchpad.service}} there was an {{After=igel-synclient-config.service}} - this was removed in the new solution because it was causing issues. There don’t seem to be any actual dependency between the two scripts, but it might be safer to include an ordering. 

h3. Issue

When adding another {{After=igel-synclient-config.service}} in the {{igel-touchpad.service}} service, the configurations in {{igel-touchpad.service}} no longer take an effect. Either it’s started too early and something is overwriting them again (e.g. mutter) or something else is going on.

h3. Task

Investigate why introducing ordering between these two services isn’t possible.

column1: IGEL@IGEL - Bluetooth Tray App - Cannot switch between High-Fidelity and Hands-Free mode
column58:
I would like to use my HUAWEI Freeclip 2 bluetooth headphone with IGEL OS while traveling.


Most of the time, in the tray app the device is stuck in “High-Fidelity mode” without the option to change to “Hands-free mode” → no microphone.



I need to run “igel-sound-control” from the debugtools app to switch between profiles.

Then the headset works without any issues.



Would be nice to know why igel-sound-control manages to change the bluetooth profiles, while the tray app is locked in one mode and does not allow to switch.

!only_headset.png|width=1021,alt="only_headset.png"!



!only_headphone.png|width=1021,alt="only_headphone.png"!
column362:
23/Feb/26 3:42 PM;712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a;[~accountid:712020:0a53f544-6c21-42a8-a85f-f6e0aad28b0a] To your question:

{quote}Would be nice to know why igel-sound-control manages to change the bluetooth profiles, while the tray app is locked in one mode and does not allow to switch.{quote}

The output profile selector is disabled, when there is an active input stream and when the device is of type Bluetooth. It was introduced here: [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/pull-requests/626/commits/93e3eae5393fd37f5420491b3e68d3dde3def76e#frontend%2Faudio%2Fsrc%2Fcomponents%2Funits%2FProfileSelector.tsx?t=59|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/pull-requests/626/commits/93e3eae5393fd37f5420491b3e68d3dde3def76e#frontend%2Faudio%2Fsrc%2Fcomponents%2Funits%2FProfileSelector.tsx?t=59]

From the corresponding ticket [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-9835|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-9835|smart-link] : 

“Because of bluetooth limitations the audio output profile of a bluetooth device can not be changed if an input stream for that device is active.”

==

We must check if that requirement is still needed, why igel-sound-control works and why the input stream seems to be active in your case.

column1: Modern Desktop | mutter sometimes segfaults when selecting a window that has already been closed in the task switcher
column58:
This is essentially a continuation of [LX8-13383|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13383].

If a window is selected in the task switcher that has already been closed, mutter sometimes segfaults.

Coredump attached, debugging logging not enabled yet. I’ll provide debug logs if necessary once I reboot my machine.

The issue can be reproduced by:

* start app launcher
* on the terminal, execute {{sleep 10; pkill applauncher}}
* press Ctrl-Alt-Tab to bring up the task switcher, keep Ctrl-Alt pressed
* select the app launcher, release Ctrl-Alt => app launcher will be put into foreground
* press Ctrl-Alt-Tab again, keep it pressed
* wait for app launcher to be killed
* select app launcher icon, release Ctrl-Alt => segfault

I’m not sure if that’s 100 % reproducible, sometimes mutter didn’t crash, but most often it did. It especially didn’t crash when the window selected was not the top-most one, I believe.

*I also believe that mutter crashes if a different window is selected.* I’ve noticed this issue when using the task switcher while a zoom meeting ended - Zoom is prone to create a lot of short-lived windows and might aggravate such situations.

Root cause is probably this new function in the AMD DRM driver, which was not available in the 6.12 kernel.

{noformat}dm_helpers_probe_acpi_edid{noformat}

[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXK/repos/linux-5.x.y.igel/browse/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/amdgpu_dm/amdgpu_dm_helpers.c?at=refs%2Fheads%2F12.08.xxx#931|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXK/repos/linux-5.x.y.igel/browse/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/amdgpu_dm/amdgpu_dm_helpers.c?at=refs%2Fheads%2F12.08.xxx#931]

If the AMD driver supports this, EDID data is pulled from an ACPI table in the BIOS.

It seems like there are plans to generalize this for all drivers and move it out of the AMD driver:
[https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2401.3/08783.html|https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2401.3/08783.html|smart-link]

column1: Evidian: unexpectedly brings up a citrix login prompt
column58:
Steps to reproduce:

# Configure a Citrix session with an autostart resource and EVIDIAN_CTX name
# Configure Evidian app to start the Citrix session with cwa_bypass mode
# Tap the badge to login
## Expected result: the autostart resource is started w/o any prompts
## Observed result: a Citrix login prompt is displayed.

-Initial analysis shows that although this does happen when the user has no roaming session, the root cause is that rsUserAuth binary doesn’t pass the password and no session is started. Looks like an Evidian binary bug.-

The above is a bug, but it is not the cause of the customer issue. The customer confirmed that their password doesn’t have any weird characters. They also claim that the normal CWA session starts as expected. Only the ‘cwa_bypass’ mode fails with the unexpected prompt.

From my prior tests, one combination of username and domain formats which works for the normal CWA sesssion and doesn’t work for storebrowse is when username is in the UPN format and the domain is missing. In this case storefront considers storebrowse login insecure and forces a step-up authentication. The normal CWA session uses the UIDialogLib which simulates interactive authentication and satisfies the security requirements of the storefront server.

But this doesn’t match the customer’s logs. They don’t have the UPN format enabled and the binary ‘should’ pass the sAMAccountName and NetBIOS domain to the hua binary and eventually to the evidian_trg_start.py script.

The logs from the original issue report.

[^igel-logs-2026-02-16.zip]

[^rsUserAuth_16887.log]

The logs with Evidian loglevel set to ‘details’ (debug).

[^rsUserAuth_16778.log]

[^igel-logs-2026-02-17.zip]

Comparing the rsUserAuth binary logs to what I have, there are two differences. 

# The customer’s EAM server sends the domain in the NetBIOS format
# The customer’s EAM server doesn’t require the badge PIN to create a new roaming session, it required the user password instead.

I’ve reconfigured our server to match these two feature, but still failed to reproduce the issue.

20/Feb/26 10:29 AM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;h2. Summary:

This issue is caused by *multiple detection of the lightdm-igel-greeter* window which provokes
WindowRaiser::enter_screenlock_state multiple times (in my case 3 times - which is the number of monitors I have).
This lead to 3 calls to Keyhandler::disable_hotkeys which will set the hotkeys_disabled_count to 3.
But in the other hand when the greeter is destroyed we get *only one destroy notification* to lightdm-igel-greeter so we call Keyhandler::enable_hotkeys only once
which leaves the counter at 2.
When the hotkeys are triggered the  Keyhandler will think that the hotkeys are disabled because the *hotkeys_disabled_count is at 2 an not at 0 (hotkeys enabled).*
And that's why restarting the window manager solves the issue because it rests the counter to 0. 

h2. Solution:

I have changed our logic in the *WindowRaiser* to make sure that we provoke the *enter_screenlock_state only once,* we have done that by adding *a bool that marks if we are in screen_lock state or not.*

column1: VM proxmox and Horizon hang at firstboot_wizard first screen.
column58:
The actual error occurs when the setup assistant freezes unexpectedly in the Proxmox and Horizon VMs.

Commit in use 150a4ff8f571 of stable/old/12.7

I replicated this issue with the following Proxmox configuration:

* 4.31 GB of RAM
* 8 GB of memory

!image-20260217-101625.png|width=1259,height=260!

After a valid OSC installation, the system boots normally and displays the first boot wizard tool.

However, it hangs, preventing the user from proceeding further with environment setup.

*Reason of setup wizard hang:*

After took a look of the reason. The first decision has to obtain a osc that install igel_development and igel_debug tools. 

* With that tools the issue did not happen.
* Then was not apps realeted, but when It is tried to install a older version of chromium the issue happens
* The reason behind it is that the system in the early first boot wizard, tries to install a newest version of chromium. Not popping up the eula message and hanging

* License for the hw with a valid token for the repo present in the osc image as default repo
* App installed not the latest one.
* The first boot wizard will hang without showing the EULA message and then the process is stalling.

column1: IgelOS login screen: Focus issues
column58:
IgelOS-12.7.5 login screen behaves randomly different: 

* Sometimes keyboard focus is at username, sometimes anywhere else. 
I see it as a bug that it behaves differently, focus at username is fine for me.
* With earlier OS versions I was able to type <TAB> to get the focus to the username (if it is anywhere). With the current release, maybe the same with some releases before, a <TAB> causes the login screen to switch to smartcard login instead of moving the focus to username.
I see this as a bug because it’s unexpected for a user and completely superfluous, because a switch to smartcard login is done automatically if a smartcard is provided by the user.

The solution to the first point seems sufficient to me, as there is then no need to press the <TAB> key anyway.

Screenshots show the display directly after a reboot.

The screensaver-window will of course intersect with the taskbar-rectangle, but it shall not be moved away from the taskbar.

How to detect the screensaver-window?

* detecting by window-title “screensaver” is easy with minimal code-changes and works (/) 
* detecting by {{igel-screenlock-layer-atom(INTEGER) = 9}}
value 9 is {{IGELScreenLockLayer_ScreenSaver}}, see [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/libxigelscreenlock/browse/include/igelscreenlock.h#26|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/libxigelscreenlock/browse/include/igelscreenlock.h#26]
This is set here: [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-x11-tools/browse/screensaver.c#238|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-x11-tools/browse/screensaver.c#238]
** this detection should also work
** could be more fail-proof, if someone changes the window-title
here: [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-x11-tools/browse/screensaver.c#128|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-x11-tools/browse/screensaver.c#128]
but that probably won't happen.
** would require some more code-changes (restructuring)



The screensaver-window has following properties:

{quote}_GTK_EDGE_CONSTRAINTS(CARDINAL) = 170
_NET_WM_STATE(ATOM) = _NET_WM_STATE_SKIP_PAGER, _NET_WM_STATE_SKIP_TASKBAR
_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS(ATOM) = _NET_WM_ACTION_CHANGE_DESKTOP, _NET_WM_ACTION_ABOVE, _NET_WM_ACTION_BELOW
igel-screenlock-layer-atom(INTEGER) = 9
_SCREENSAVER_ID(STRING) = "8472 (user@???)"
_SCREENSAVER_VERSION(STRING) = "IGELScreenSaver-1.0"
WM_NAME(STRING) = "screensaver"
WM_CLASS(STRING) = "screensaverd", "ScreenSaverD"
WM_HINTS(WM_HINTS):
                Client accepts input or input focus: False{quote}

column1: stable/os12 | System Boot Failure Related to Partition Integrity Problems (partition failures)
column58:
Current builds from stable/os12 (2026-02-05) are unable to be installed and cause all sorts of issues.

In OSC: mouse/touchpad unusable, install fails

In lxos: installs okay, but gets stuck in a Setup Assistant loop, many errors in the journal about failing partitions and device mappers

Has been seen on LG and Lenovo laptops, but the issue is probably a general one. 

The picture is an except from the journal in the rescue shell during the Setup Assistant after lxos update.

column1: igel-desktop: turning off taskbar-autohide-feature does not set wm-struts immediately
column58:
h3. bug description

Struts in window manager are not set when auto-hide taskbar feature is turned off.

h3. bug reproduction

* turn on taskbar-autohide
Setup → User Interface → Desktop → Taskbar → Taskbar auto hide
* this removes the reserved area for the taskbar in the wm-struts, sets it to zero (/)
* turn off taskbar-autohide feature
* struts are not set to the size and position of the taskbar-UI (x)
the reserved area stays zero
* interacting with the UI (click on taskbar, open start-menu)
anything which triggers update of ui-areas from frontend to backend,
this then triggers also an update of the reserved-taskbar-area, the struts get set then.

h3. technical remarks

I assume, there is just a little signal-connection missing.
When the setupd-subscriber notifies about the changed taskbarautohide-parameter, the igel-desktop-code needs to evaluate this and set the struts accordingly.

something like this:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/shared-desktop-params/SharedDesktopParams.cpp#140-146|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/shared-desktop-params/SharedDesktopParams.cpp#140-146]

But be careful to not break the autohide-feature.

In the SharedDesktopParams.cpp,

* on {{ui_areas_changed}}, we get the new taskbar-area and can set the correct struts, fine
* but  {{on_parameters_changed}}, we do not get the new taskbar-area.
That’s the problem here, I think.
Could the backend somehow enforce an update from the frontend? Is that a good approach?

column1: Realtek 8852be driver registry options no longer being applied

Affected scripts:

* “/etc/igel/module_options/configure_rtw89"
* “/etc/modprobe.d/rtw89-install.conf”

column1: CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor runs in RFM mode on IGEL OS 12.7.5+ – kernel backend not supported
column58:
Starting with *IGEL OS 12.7.5 (tested RC4)*, the *CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor* permanently runs in *Reduced Functionality Mode (RFM)*.

TP available in app releases and use by customer BoA.

!image-20260130-120814.png|width=501,alt="image-20260130-120814.png"!



The sensor service starts correctly as root, but reports the following reason {{falconctl -g --rfm-stat}}:

{quote}_“the kernel backend does not support the running kernel”_{quote}



Checked Kernel Flag´s, but looked good under first impresion.







With *IGEL OS 12.7.4*, the Falcon Sensor works correctly with the same configuration and *does not enter RFM* → Shows USER Mode

!image-20260130-123348.png|width=504,alt="image-20260130-123348.png"!







----

h3. *Observed Behavior*

* {{falconctl -g --rfm-state}} → {{true}}
* {{falconctl -g --rfm-reason}} → _the kernel backend does not support the running kernel_
* No Falcon kernel module loaded
* Backend does not switch to eBPF despite kernel flags being set
* Issue reproducible on multiple systems and by multiple persons
* Also on 12.9 tested by Daniel
* Works on 12.7.4
* Works on 12.7.5.tp.2
* Works with 12.8.0.rc4

column363:
30/Jan/26 3:35 PM;712020:ee35277e-d3b2-4b5d-8963-7393d33cf7fc;The issue is that we have changed the binary paths in our system. In newer versions we link {{/sbin}} to {{/usr/sbin}}. The igelpkgd detects via the dbus sender path for the dbus invocation id via polkit. We therefore get the PID for the D-Bus sender and then use {{/proc/<PID>/exe}} to detect the binary path, which points to {{/usr/sbin/igel-rmagent}}, where the binary is located. However, this does not match the igelpkgd path, which used to be {{/sbin/igel-rmagent}}.

It will be changed so that the igelpkg will check whether the binary path matches either {{/sbin/igel-rmagent}} or {{/usr/sbin/igel-rmagent}}.

[~accountid:712020:eb11546b-6213-4618-8a1d-69eff0c6a0f2] I know there is also code in the update that uses this mechanism to detect binary paths and perform comparisons. This is not an issue for the comparison with the igelpkgd binary, because the binary is located in {{/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libexec/igelpkgd}}. Are there any other code parts which could fail?

See the {{trust_sender}} function: [trust_sender function|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel_update/browse/src/lxos/libpolkit/update_polkit.c#111]

11/Feb/26 2:20 PM;712020:3f68fc46-4312-421c-883d-b96b5bc1e2bb;*Solution*
There were a couple of issues here:
- the icon positioning
- undefined behaviors if the icon position could not be retrieved
For the first part it is needed to position the xembed icon on the same monitor as the icon is on the taskbar. So when spanning multiple monitors, it needs to be on the most right or most bottom monitor the taskbar is located.
To achieve this, the entire ui-rectangle of the taskbar is fetched, of which the lowest right corner is taken to create a rectangle. This rectangle allows it to fetch the monitor it is located at. Which is the same monitor the actual (frontend) icons are located.
On this monitor the icons are placed as in before.
When the original application now fetches the monitor, on which the icon is positioned, it returns the correct monitor.
For the second issues part I fixed some bugs, but there are still some issues present, when a different screen for the taskbar is defined than the primary monitor. There will a ticket for it.

column1: igel-desktop: crash on boot (BadDrawable)
column58:
h3. Bug Description / Reproduction


* After a boot the igel-desktop crashes (see crash log below).
* The desktop automatically recovers after this and is then in a stable state.
* It doesn’t happen on successive restarts of the service, only on the first boot.


h3. Technical Details

{noformat}(mutter:8651): Gdk-WARNING **: 15:47:04.643: The program 'mutter' received an X Window System error.                                                                                                                                                                                    │
This probably reflects a bug in the program.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            │
The error was 'BadDrawable (invalid Pixmap or Window parameter)'.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       │
  (Details: serial 1242 error_code 9 request_code 144 (DAMAGE) minor_code 1)                                                                                                                                                                                                            │
  (Note to programmers: normally, X errors are reported asynchronously;                                                                                                                                                                                                                 │
   that is, you will receive the error a while after causing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        │
   To debug your program, run it with the GDK_SYNCHRONIZE environment                                                                                                                                                                                                                   │
   variable to change this behavior. You can then get a meaningful                                                                                                                                                                                                                      │
   backtrace from your debugger if you break on the gdk_x_error() function.)   {noformat}


This is probably due to registering a non window/drawable for damage watching in:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/tray-panel-port/Dock.cpp#198|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/tray-panel-port/Dock.cpp#198]


h3. Remarks

* can be reproduced with current stable/old/12.8 / base-system-12.8.0-rc.3


h3. Tasks

* Investigate why the igel-system-tray tries to dock a non window with name igel-system-tray
* Properly check if the given window XID points to a valid drawable / window before adding damage watch
* Check order of plugin registration and docking of windows during boot process

We now listen directly to DestroyNotify via our x_event_filter to remove docked trayicon windows and have checks in place to prevent these windows from registering XDamage ids for monitoring their drawables for damage / changes.

IconContainer and IconSocket now check their plug window is valid before doing any operations on the plug windows XID.

The bug causes the rmagent to request downgrades of locally installed apps after they have been upgraded. This affects IGEL@IGEL users who want to use the latest app releases.

column1: Chromium Incognito Mode (Forced) opens "newtab is blocked” instead of configured startup page
column58:
When Chromium is configured with Incognito Mode set to “Forced”, the browser no longer opens the configured startup page.
Instead, Chromium displays a “newtab is blocked” error page on launch.

The same configuration worked correctly in *chromium-142.0.7444+2*, where Chromium opened the URL defined in the startup/homepage settings even when Incognito Mode was forced.

h3. The issue is reproducible on:

* chromium-143.0.7499+1 and the latest 143 test and 144 RCs.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

* On IGEL OS 12.7.3, configure Chromium with:
** Setup → Apps → Chromium → Global Settings → Privacy → Incognito Mode → Allow incognito mode = Forced
** Setup → Apps → Chromium → Global Settings → General → Startup page set to a valid webpage (e.g. internal portal or citrix web store)
* Save the profile and apply it to the device.
* Launch Chromium.

h3. Expected Result

Chromium should open directly in Incognito mode and load the configured startup page, as it did in Chromium 142.

h3. Actual Result

Chromium launches in Incognito mode but displays a “newtab is blocked” error page instead of loading the configured URL.

column1: IGELmaker4: resigner not working on Debian Trixie host
column58:
Building the firmware on a Debian Trixie host currently fails due to resigner failing:



{noformat}* Installing modules ...

openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.3.0' not found (required by openssl)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.5.0' not found (required by openssl)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.4.0' not found (required by openssl)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.2.0' not found (required by openssl)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.3.0' not found (required by /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.3)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.4.0' not found (required by /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.3)
openssl: /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/lib/libcrypto.so.3: version `OPENSSL_3.2.0' not found (required by /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.3)
Error (get_shim_public_key): Could not extract public IGEL key from /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelmaker4/modules/focal/igel/shim-efi-bin/arch/amd64/microsoft-signed/20250221/bootx64.efi
Error (verify_signature_of_file): No public key present to check signature with.

ERROR: Install function of module bookworm/debian/igel/admin/grub-efi-amd64-bin-lx-os failed.{noformat}

This is due to the bookworm-based copy of {{libcrypto.so.3}} that we ship in the {{lib}} directory and that is preloaded via {{LD_LIBRARY_PATH}} in {{bin/buildigel}}.

In order to fix this, we can just drop this copy. OpenSSL is forward-compatible enough for the bookworm-based {{resigner}} binary to still work with the OpenSSL libraries that are part of trixie.

Going forward, we will completely drop {{resigner}} from IGELmaker and use the system version. Both users and builders will need to install the igelfs-utils-builderkit package corresponding to the Debian codename they are using as their build host.

column1: IMH- Nic Issue
column58:
I received following bug email internally from Landon Winburn:

I built a Windows XP machine using virtio drivers for the disk and nic. I captured this image and then deployed to a new machine. When the new machine booted the VM it went through a bunch of hardware detection. Upon investigation the nic was set to a realtek model instead of virtio like the source was set to which is not optimal.

!image-20260123-102813.png|width=313,alt="image-20260123-102813.png"!
column362:
29/Jan/26 11:22 AM;712020:4ac96b3e-d13a-4582-8a4c-3e4504f31c66;I was researching about the issue and I found the following: Windows XP is predecessor of the virtualization. Virsh/Libvirt are planned to provide the best option for xp and the rtl driver is what they chose. Final user can change and try other option but this is the default option for windows xp.

My intention is to test this scenario in debian as well, looking for what is given as default. I am not convinced that changing the default for the XP template would be a good fix, consider that the community has chosen to have this nic as default, and they are foreseen issues that we are not. 

In any case, going to investigate further.

Windows XP exists pre virtualization technology, in the template for the xp in the Community code for libvirt the default network card is the one selected and mentioned in the bug.
In the newer versions of xp one could use a newer card, so selecting a 1Gb network may work but there is no guarantee. 

I would say this is not a bug but the actual support for XP, when one does not know which version one is using.

column369:
25/Mar/26 10:21 AM;712020:66c61fac-739d-4add-aa6a-c5a5c1b514a6;This is not an XP specific problem. The NIC settings are overwritten in VMConfig.update_from_registry(), which also changes the NIC type. I think this is also a design question: At the moment, any NICs present are _replaced_ by the settings in the registry.

Solutions I can think of:

* Replace NICs defined in the imported file with registry values (current implementation, overwrites)
* Keep any defined NICs and add the ones defined in the registry. In this case we may have to change the virtual network for the imported NICs if that network is not defined on the machine that imports. Problem: maximum number of NIC settings
* Use pre-defined NICs but change network, MAC settings to those from registry. Problem: How to map pre-configured NIC to which registry settings ? What do we do if the number of configured NICs is different in the imported file and the registry ?

My currently best suggestion: Add warning if exporting more than NUM_NICS interfaces. On importing, take the settings from the imported file in the order they are defined, replace with registry settings in order. If not set, connect to “isolated” network. Error out when using more than NUM_NICS.

That way we can keep model and MAC from the imported values. We could set the MAC in the registry to the imported values if there is no existing entry. That way it is easier for the user to know which NIC is set to what.

column1: hashgen fails with partitions > 2GB
column58:
h3. Impact

The bug causes {{hashgen}} to fail when handling partitions greater than 2GB. This impacts users by preventing successful builds of large applications.

h3. Expected behaviour

The application should build successfully without any errors during the hashing process.

h3. Actual behaviour

The current behaviour results in an error when trying to read a partition greater than 2GB. The error log shows:

{noformat}hashgen -a sha512 -m 0x01012019 /work/git/lx-builderkit/igelpkg/tests/data/apps/test_bigapp/igelpkg.output/data_x64 -i 87b67513ce601894292e7f68bbf7d1d49d820d9282e5e2e511a1ab9323481f54abb15c04bc9ae552adc79aaac32e07445b3cc6e4a5f64f645fcc357fe0328ea8
Error [hashgen]: read(/work/git/lx-builderkit/igelpkg/tests/data/apps/test_bigapp/igelpkg.output/data_x64/bigfile_2G): No data available
Error [hashgen]: fsh_compute().{noformat}

h3. Steps to reproduce

The situation:

* on 12.7:
qt window flag "tool"
The window has _NET_WM_ACTION_FULLSCREEN in the _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS
and can go into fullscreen. It's allowed. (/)
* on 12.8:
qt window flag "tool"
The window does *NOT* have _NET_WM_ACTION_FULLSCREEN in the _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS
and can not got into fullscreen. Not allowed. (x)

{quote}_NET_WM_ACTION_FULLSCREEN indicates that the window may be brought to fullscreen state.{quote}


Why the difference on 12.7 and 12.8 ?

From the docu [https://doc.qt.io/archives/qtforpython-5/PySide2/QtCore/Qt.html#PySide2.QtCore.PySide2.QtCore.Qt.WindowType|https://doc.qt.io/archives/qtforpython-5/PySide2/QtCore/Qt.html#PySide2.QtCore.PySide2.QtCore.Qt.WindowType] :

{quote}On X11, the result of the flag is dependent on the window manager and its ability to understand Motif and/or NETWM hints. Most existing modern window managers can handle this.

Some of these flags depend on whether the underlying window manager supports them.{quote}

Maybe another reason for the difference: our patched xf-windowmanager in 12.7.
xfwm patches somehow about fullscreen:

* [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/xfwm/browse/debian/patches/IGEL-fullscreen.diff|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/xfwm/browse/debian/patches/IGEL-fullscreen.diff]

In general, the description for Qt Window Types: [https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qt.html#WindowType-enum|https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qt.html#WindowType-enum]
I read it like type "tool" is not supposed to be used for fullscreen applications, my opinion.

But anyway.
I attached my updated minimal-example-script.
Could be tested by [~accountid:712020:725616c0-4ddd-4ec8-8be6-5dac31847bca] 
It simply checks which windowmanager is running and sets the window-flag accordingly.

if (check_if_process_running("mutter")):

column1: igel-desktop: Taskbar above some RDP full-screen windows
column58:
Using RDP-Web-Access to to show seamless remote apps: “Normal” application windows like Firefox can be switched to fullscreen without problems. But windows no listed in taskbar are still covered with taskbar when showing fullscreen.

Easy to reproduce: Start Calculator remote app and then press on your keyboard ctrl-alt-del. A new fullscreen window appears. That window is not full visible, because taskbar is still on top of that. In OS12.7.5 such window is visible completely in fullscreen.

column376:
02/Apr/26 10:20 AM;712020:9faabc93-72fc-451e-b514-dd2fd1240c23;[~accountid:712020:f2524417-3808-4ec8-a0ad-3b2596a88014] we are likely dealing with multiple issues here, especially if both Intel and AMD chipsets are affected.

The issue that disabling PSR fixed is a GPU freeze, not a full system freeze. This GPU freeze is special in that the mouse pointer can still be seen moving, but nothing else on the screen updates and - more importantly - it can be worked around by going to the rescue shell via Ctrl-Alt-F11, logging in and killing the window manager via {{pkill mutter}}.

If the machine is “more dead” than that, i.e., totally frozen, then we have a different issue with a totally unknown cause.

column1: no taskbar in screenlock while a full-screen application is open
column58:
When a fullscreen application is open (i.e. avd login) and the screenlock appears after i.e. 5 minutes. Then the taskbar does not appear in the screenlock.

Therefor the user is not able to logout or shutdown the pc.

*reproduction steps*

* configure local user
* configure hotkey for screenlock (User Interface > Screenlock/Screensaver) , e.g. Win + l
* open terminal, enter full-screen mode (F11 or context menu)

*tasks*

* taskbar should be visible in screen-lock mode, also when there is a full-screen application running

column1: igel-desktop: app-switcher does not receive mouse-clicks
column58:
The new app-switcher in our igel-mutter-plugin can only be used with keyboard,
but not with mouse.
While the app-switcher is open (you need to hold the hotkey in order to keep app-switcher open),
you can not use the mouse to select an entry in the list of windows in the app-switcher-UI.

* press configured app-switcher hotkey (probably CTRL + ALT + Tab)
* keep keys press to keep the app-switcher-UI open (CTRL + ALT)
* move mouse over the UI
* click on one window you want to switch to
* nothing happens (x)

Analysis so far:

* hotkey-press triggers start of app-switcher, backend tells frontend to show it
* frontend sends new ui-areas to backend
* *new ‘apps-switcher’ ui-area has size and position 0x0 , FAIL* (x)
*Why? That’s the root-cause, I think. We have to get the correct size and position!*
*[InputManager] [ui_areas_handler]: visible uiArea 'apps-switcher' wants input grabbed: false, left/right: 0/0 top/bottom: 0/0*
* we grab global input while the app-switcher is open, correct.
This is not done because the ui-areas has {{prevent_focus_grab = false}},
but because the app-switcher-plugin-code simply calls {{input_manager_interface->grab_focus();}}
* mouse click gets catched by our input-manager correctly:
[InputManager] [on_button_event]: CLUTTER_BUTTON_PRESS event on input-actor '0x55ae9482bb60' for area 'input_grab_actor'
* button-press-event hit-detection does not find the app-switcher ui-area,
because the size is 0x0 and position is 0x0
[InputManager] [should_activate_window_under_mouse_event]: The button press did not hit internal UI but the input stays grabbed because auto_ungrab is not active
[InputManager] [on_button_event]: event did not hit internal UI. no ui area
* therefore, button-press gets not forwarded to the webview
column362:

column1: NCP7 App Firewall active and DNS blocked after first connection and reboot
column58:
Feedback from Client:

+*NCP7 with OS12 Summary*+ 

+Initial Tests+

The UMS profile “StBV-NCP7-OS12” was created. Mainly, paths were adjusted and the current NCP7 app was added.

After installing the NCP7 profile and without having established the VPN connection even once, the thin client works as usual.

As soon as the NCP connection has been successfully established for the first time and the current ncpphone.cnf has been downloaded from the management server, after an IGEL OS reboot the firewall becomes active and DNS is also blocked.
As a result, no new VPN connection can be established anymore.

+Workaround+:

* Start the terminal.
* Test DNS with nslookup [http://www.google.com|http://www.google.com|smart-link]  → error
* From the start menu, run “Reset NCP Settings”.

This deletes all ncpphone* files from the cfg directory and copies vorlage.cnf to ncpphone.cnf.

When the NCP app is started now, the log repeatedly shows:
"Firewall: Removed Rule=AR-VPN-IpSec-ng:999980"
(/services_rw/ncp/var/log/ncp/clnt/20XXXXXX-user-ncpclnt.log)

* The DNS test works again.
* The VPN connection can now be established successfully.
* The NCP7 license is installed correctly.

The VPN connection can be ended and restarted. This works until the next reboot, then the workaround must be repeated.

+Further Tests+

According to the NCP team from IT-DLZ (Mr. Faulian), this error does not occur under a normal Linux installation.

Tests with a VM running Ubuntu 24.04.03 + NCP 7.01 Build 31940 showed that no DNS/firewall issues occur after successful VPN connections.

However, in tests with a VM running IGEL OS 12.7.4 and the NCP App 7 BUILD 1.0 TP 1, the DNS/firewall problem could be reproduced.

So, actually without any firewall active I would guess that on the customer’s test machine the file /etc/resolv.conf differs in the situations where the VPN gateway can be reached and where it cannot be reached. column1: OpenSSH configuration not applied when server is disabled
column58:
We have a module called {{server_ssh}} that ships a configuration file being executed at boot, applying Setup configuration to both OpenSSH server and client configurations, c.f.: {{modules/misc/net/ssh_server/arch/all/data/root/config/bin/configure_ssh}}.



Unfortunately, quite some of these modifications, and especially all client modifications, are disabled if the server is disabled, because the script just exits in this case.

It shouldn’t do that, but instead apply all configuration independently of whether the OpenSSH server is enabled or not.

The server was enabled by default on OS 11, but this default was changed to disabled with OS 12, so we have a regression here.
column244: * Fixed applying OpenSSH client modifications on boot - settings in IGEL Setup should now be applied even if the OpenSSH server is disabled.
