column1: Certificates classified as "Browser" are added to the system certificate store
column58:
h3. Impact

The bug affects UMS admins who want to configure CA certificates for browser use only. Certificates classified as "Browser" are unintentionally added to the system certificate store, which poses a significant security risk.

h3. Expected behaviour

Certificates classified as "Browser" should not be added to the system certificate store.

h3. Actual behaviour

Currently, there is no option to configure certificates as “browser only.” Certificates marked as "Browser" are still added to the system store.

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Attempt to classify a CA certificate as “Browser.”
* Observe that the certificate is added to the system certificate store.

h3. Environment

N/A

h3. Workarounds

column1: Kiosk mode cannot be set properly in Horizon
column58:
To set kiosk mode in horizon the option --kioskLogin isn’t sufficient.

Additionally the options nonInteractive, once, nomenubar and fullscreen are also needed.

Only then the kiosk mode is fully working which means that no user interaction should be needed and in cases of error the client is expected to just quit and be able to be restarted.
Problem is that the fullscreen option isn’t available in current builds.
This option is affecting the client window not the size of the session window which can already be set in great detail.

The best way to fix this is setting --fullscreen and the above mentioned options when kiosk mode is switched on.
That way only one switch is needed and no cumbersome search to find the other options would be required.
column244:
When the kiosk mode is switched on now, the Horizon client options nonInteractive, once, fullscreen  and nomenubar are added automatically. Only then the expected non-interactive behavior of a kiosk mode is possible. This means the session should be directly started without any user interaction. The correct credentials need to be given here. Should there be error conditions which prevent the session to be established the session should just be closed without prompt. The general idea is to restart the session that after the down time of the service the session can resume automatically as soon as possible.

Added the Horizon option "Hide client after launching session"  to Horizon Client Global / Server Options This option existed only in the IGEL OS registry but under a different name app.horizon.vmware.view.use-single-window. Kiosk mode requires this option to be switched on (the default) or else the client will lose its non-interactive behavior and prompt the user on error conditions.
 
If you want to have the kiosk mode expanded to all monitors, set the Multimonitor full-screen mode to Display full-screen on all monitors.

column1: Audio output automatically changed to internal speaker when jack connected
column58:
Connect jack headphones to device (I’ve checked on Lenovo 13w 2-in-1 Gen 3, Lenovo ThinkPad L13 2-in-1 Gen 6 + work laptop; doesn’t seem to be hardware-dependent). _Make sure jack output is selected_ from the sound app tray. Change the input source, either from the jack mic or from the internal mic to the other one (jack mic ↔︎ internal mic). After the audio input change the audio output automatically gets changed to the internal speaker. This only happens if the jack output source is selected previously before any action takes place.

*Pipewire* audio is selected. Unchecking switch-on-connect and autoswitch-to-headset-profile params doesn’t make a difference in fixing the issue.

Checked on 12.8. The laptop used for work has 12.7.1 so I assume the OS version doesn’t matter.

Also checked on Ubuntu which uses pipewire by default and the audio output doesn’t automatically switch if the input is changed. Might be worth checking how this is behaves in Windows?

Changing from pipewire to pulseaudio in IGEL seems to fix the problem.

Not sure if pipewire (/jack headphones) should behave like this or not.

Please feel free to edit this ticket or even close if it proves to not actually be a bug.

27/Mar/26 3:00 PM;712020:fba16d47-bd02-47c3-8258-9a4e79978622;When the Pipewire is selected as audiobackend in the Igel Setup and when the audio jack headset is plugged in, you will be able to see in the tray app the profiles for each input and output.  

So, for the each input we have 2 profiles(one with the Speaker as output and one with the Heaphones as output): 

* Digital Microphone:-Play HiFi quality Music (HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI3, Mic1, Mic2, Speaker) 

                                         -Play HiFi quality Music (HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI3, Headphones, Mic1, Mic2) 



* Headphones: -Play HiFi quality Music (HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI3, Mic1, Mic2, Speaker) 

                               -Play HiFi quality Music (HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI3, Headphones, Mic1, Mic2) 

   These profiles are configured in alsa and can be based on the machine you are using. This is an example from the *HP EliteBook 630 G11.* The profiles can be different, but each output should have 2 profiles (one for headphones and one for speaker).

When the output is set to the Headphones, when changing the Input from the Headphones to the Digital Microphone, it automatically chooses the Play HiFi quality Music (HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI3, Mic1, Mic2, Speaker)  Profile, so that's why the output is automatically changing to the Speaker. 

The same is happening when changing the Input from Digital Microphone to the Headphones: it automatically chooses the profile with the Speaker as output. So, it seems to be a problem with the profile selection, because it automatically selects the one with Speaker as output when changing the mic. I looked into it and it doesn't seem to be a wireplumber logic problem.  

For now we don't have a solution for this and we are still working on it. We can say that it is a known issue fort the IGEL OS 12.8.

column58:

* Draws more attention than the instructional content
* Appears more actionable than any tour progression control

* The *“Cancel tour”* action should be visually de-emphasized
* Tour guidance and progression should be visually prioritized

column1: Cloud Services Tours rely on implicit UI interactions to progress (accessibility & usability issue)
column58:
Some steps in the Cloud Services Tours advance using an explicit *“Next”* button, while other steps implicitly require the user to interact with a UI element (for example, opening a dropdown) in order to progress.
This requirement is not clearly communicated to the user, resulting in inconsistent and unpredictable tour behavior.

This design causes accessibility and usability issues and increases the risk that tours become stuck or fail if the expected UI interaction is not performed or cannot be detected.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Sign in to [https://now-qas.igel.com/csm|https://now-qas.igel.com/csm] 
# Click on Tours
# Start a tour
# Progress through the steps
# Observe that:
#* Some steps show a *Next* button
#* Other steps do not show *Next* and instead require interacting with a specific UI element without clear instruction

*Actual Result*

* Tour progression depends on undocumented UI interactions
* Users may not know how to proceed
* Keyboard-only and screen reader users may be blocked
* Tours are more likely to fail if the expected interaction is missed

*Expected Result*

* Tour navigation behavior should be consistent across all steps
* Either:
** All steps provide a *Next* button
**or*
** Steps that require interaction clearly instruct the user and remain fully accessible
* Tours should not fail due to missed or inaccessible UI interactions

column1: Focused always on top window hides shutdown prompt and tray windows
column58:
If you have a window that you set as always on top (using context menu), and have that window focused, it will overlay the shutdown prompt when displayed and the tray windows (wifi, bluetooth) the always on top window will be above the newly opened tray window/ shutdown prompt.

Steps to reproduce:
- Open an app (terminal for example).
- Make the app window always on top using the context menu.
- Move that window to the buttom right (or where the tray windows will appear).
- Open a tray window (bluetooth, wifi… accessibility window does not have the issue).
the tray window will be hidden under the app window. (same be observed with the shutdown prompt). 

Hints: a similar issue was observed with the lock screen greeter [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/LX8/boards/179?selectedIssue=LX8-13311|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/LX8/boards/179?selectedIssue=LX8-13311|smart-link] .

14/Jan/26 8:29 AM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;h3. Summary: 

It seems when we set the *keep above from the gtk*, our mutter pluggin will consider that window to have the above set as true, meaning *meta_window_is_above returns true for that window.*
But somehow *mutter is not fully considering that window to be always on top.* The solution that I have found is to *call meta_window_make_above on windows that have the meta_window_is_above(current_window) set as true before focusing.*

PS: on some gtk window this issue is not observed for example on the floating notification because we calling set_override_redirect on them this means that our mutter window manager will not get any events related to that window see [https://docs.gtk.org/gdk3/method.Window.set_override_redirect.html|https://docs.gtk.org/gdk3/method.Window.set_override_redirect.html|smart-link]

column1: The Base System should make the parameter update.repository%.manager_is_app_proxy editable
column58:
Actually the parameter update.repository%.manager_is_app_proxy for base_system can not be edited in the ConfigDialog. Can this parameter be made editable.

Background:

Customers with multiple UMS Servers - possibly distributed over the continent - want the devices to prioritize the order of the Repositories depending on the location. This can be done by defining profiles with the URLs in the parameter update.repository%.url ordered with different priority for each region.

They can either define the parameter update.repository%.certificate to point to ‘/wfs/igel-rmagent/trust-store/2E2Ea67898C52…F6D8972F4AA.pem’ so that the device uses the correct certificate. But this is not optimal.

The other way would be to define update.repository%.manager_is_app_proxy=true. In this case - as far as I could see in my tests - the device uses a correct certificate to download the app, regardles if the value of update.repository%.certificate id not set or set to an empty string.

Actually, the UMS sends update.repository%.manager_is_app_proxy=true to the device for all repositories with URLs pointing to the UMS AppProxy. This actually works, but hides configuration options from the user.

column1: igelpkgctl local file install may fail with enabled discovery
column58:
Due to the current behavior of {{igelpkgctl install -f}} an installation with enabled discovery may fail.

* {{igelpkgctl}} may try to pull the app from remote even if the {{-f}} was provided
* DPU can’t currently handle community apps
* certificate for community app maybe not available on the device

With both enabled the customer may think he tries to install the app locally, but because the app is available on another device, the device will actually try to pull the app from another device that has the app and may fail.

IMHO i would expect {{-f}} only to consider the local file.

{{igelpkgctl install -f myapp.ipk}}

column1: CWA: node actions triggered by trivial changes in a disconnected session terminate connected resources of a different active session
column58:
When a citrix session is active (logged in) and a resource (an app, or a remote desktop, or several) is connected and running, execution of citrix-related node actions kills the resources, but does not disconnect the session. 

Tested under base system 12.7.4 and cwa 2505 build 1, 2505 build 2, and 2508 build 1

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Create two CWA sessions: Session A and Session B with minimal identical configuration
## Session type: StoreFront
## URL: https://lx2402.lx.test/citrix/store
## Auth method: IGEL login
# Start Sesssion A and log in with an lx.test account
## expected result: log in successful, resource icons appear on the desktop
## observed result: as expected
# Start any resource, e.g. Calculator
# Open IGEL setup
# Open the settings of the cwa Session B
# Under Authentication, change ‘Handling of domain in login window’ from ‘normal’ to ‘hidden’
# Save the settings
## expected result: the calculator app is uneffected
## observed result: the calculator app is closed by the execution of the node action
### Meantime, Session A is still active and the resource icons are still on the desktop
### For some reason that I don’t understand well, starting another app at this state doesn’t work reliably
### But starting a remote desktop (Windows Server 2022 on this server) does work reliably
### The remote desktop is also reliably killed by the same triggering of node actions (steps 4-7)
column362: 29/Jan/26 1:26 PM;712020:c2f113c7-926b-43c8-9951-8fd54c1ca916;I discussed with [~accountid:712020:cda1b85a-3c54-40c4-8658-a14992a8bc71] and [~accountid:712020:289f037f-8785-42c6-b39d-21c4f6346eef] that while the Citrix Application runs, the admin modifies registry entries in the ‘app.cwa.sessions%’ section. column1: igel-desktop: missing support of _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS (RDP)
column58:
Original description from Heiko:

{quote}wie gestern schon einmal angedeutet: Die Einträge im Kontextmenü sind alle enabled, obwohl per X11 anders gesetzt:
_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS(ATOM) = _NET_WM_ACTION_CLOSE, _NET_WM_ACTION_MINIMIZE, _NET_WM_ACTION_MOVE

Wenn ich beispielsweise auf "Maximize" klicke, wird das Fenster tatsächlich versucht zu maximieren. Danach ist die lokale Anzeige und die remote nicht mehr synchronisiert. Das eine ist ja die Anzeige im Kontextmenü (müsste ausgegraut sein) und das andere die ausgelöste Aktion. Ein Maximize sollte hier NICHT möglich sein.

"Always On Top" (_NET_WM_ACTION_ABOVE, _NET_WM_ACTION_BELOW) sind bei den Remote-Apps eigentlich immer NICHT gesetzt bei _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS, da solche Eigenschaften vom entfernten Server vorgegeben sind und ich als Client die nicht an den Server weitergeben kann. Wenn also lokal dieses "Always On Top" gesetzt ist, dann stimmt das Stacking der entfernten Fenster nicht mehr und es gibt Probleme mit dem Fokus und dergleichen.

Bitte setzt die _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS entsprechend um, ansonsten sind die Remote-Apps bei RDP nicht zu gebrauchen.{quote}



*tasks*

* support _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS by reading out given values and adjusting our app context menu 
** not allowed actions should be hidden or disabled

14/Jan/26 10:54 AM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;After clarifying the requirements with Heiko: 
- There is apps that cannot be maximized like the calculator but our context menu still tries to maximize these apps. 
- We are not supposed to be able to set the always above state for the window. Windows OS is the one setting that for the rdp windows we just need to listen to those state and show them in the context menu without the ability to change them.
column364:
15/Jan/26 7:37 AM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;h2. Observations: 

# *The internal state of the window in mutter does not consider/respect the* *_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS_* *set* *by the RDP client**_._* Meaning for the calculator the *_meta_**_window_can_maximize returns true* even though the xprop shows the only _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS_ to be set to_NET_WM_ACTION_CLOSE, _NET_WM_ACTION_MINIMIZE. (Also made sure that the id matches from the mutter part and the xprop part).
# I had a look into the mutter code base to see what they are doing with the _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS._ *It seems that mutter only sets those values never read from them* [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/mutter/browse/src/x11/window-x11.c#4378|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/mutter/browse/src/x11/window-x11.c#4378].

h3. Why Mutter does respect the set _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS and overrides them._

According to the *Extended Window Manager Hints (EWMH)* specification on x11 the Window [https://mail.gnome.org/archives/wm-spec-list/2001-October/msg00015.html|https://mail.gnome.org/archives/wm-spec-list/2001-October/msg00015.html|smart-link]  we have the following:

{noformat}Window Managers SHOULD ignore the value of _NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS when they initially manage a window. This value may be left over from a previous Window Manager with different policies.{noformat}

It seems that Mutter behavior aligns with the specification since it only read from this values and never read from them. The setting of this values is meant to reflect the internal status that mutter has for this window. *So setting those values ourselves does not seem to influence the Mutter internal state on the Window at all and the values will be overridden.* 

[~accountid:712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a] [~accountid:712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57] What do you think how should we proceed here?
column365:
15/Jan/26 7:49 AM;712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a;[~accountid:712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad] Not sure if I got it completely, but I see it like this:

* I assume there is a function {{canMaximize()}} in our backend which returns a boolean to the frontend / datacontext. Further I assume, that this function currently only relies on mutter API to get this state (probably: {{meta_window_can_maximize()}}). 
* I would adjust our {{canMaximize()}} to use the mutter API and also check the *_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS_* : return true only if the mutter API retruns true AND the maximize is within the *_NET_WM_ALLOWED_ACTIONS_*.

We can also discuss later after daily in more detail.

* Since Mutter does not read the xprops at all, the only way we found is to read the props ourselves. 
* The Challenge we found with that is that the xprops are not set on window creation for some reason and that we need to provoke a refocus after the window creation then read the xprop to find the set allowed actions by the rdp

h3. Solution:

# Add a function that enables us to detect rdp windows
# if rdp window is detected the maximize, minimize, always on top are disabled
# after 4 seconds (the least value that after it we can read the xprop) we provoke a refocus then read the xprop for the created rdp window and only the set allowed actions will be enbaled in the context menu. Also we sync here the is_above (always_on_top) property.

* Typo of “whitelist.conf” as “whitelist.powertop” for checking if a device is whitelisted for a specific quirk when laptop_mode is set to auto → this means that the laptop_mode is never enabled in the Laptop Mode Tools config
* The service “laptop-mode.service” is not restarted after adding lines to the Laptop Mode Tools configuration, thus it is never activated. This only happens in specific cases, hence why it does not always show up. If the powertop quirk is set to “Disable” but the laptop_mode should be active, then the laptop-mode service is properly restarted and everything works fine.

column1: kiosk-app: parameter not visible in UMS profile
column58:
h3. bug description

The parameter “Access only to initial folder” on {{Filesystem / Downloads}} page is not visible in UMS profiles.

[https://now.igel.com/now/cwf/agent/record/sn_customerservice_support_case/69b2c9eeebf1f610c837fe540bd0cd74|https://now.igel.com/now/cwf/agent/record/sn_customerservice_support_case/69b2c9eeebf1f610c837fe540bd0cd74]

h3. Analysis and possible solution

The given parameter differs from the others in the fact, that it is currently a base_system parameter. That’s the case because it is used internally by some base_system component. When creating an app profile, the corresponding base_system parameters are not loaded and thus not displayed.

We still need the decoupled way, meaning we should not make this parameter directly into an app parameter (because then an app parameter would control something in the base_system). One quick solution is to keep the base_system parameter, and add an another on app level which is in sync with the base_system parameter.

h3. tasks

* parameter handling
** create a new app parameter like {{app.igel_secure_kiosk.settings.access_only_default_folder}} 
** sync this new parameter to {{userinterface.gtk.filechooser.lock_to_startup_folder}} 
* translation improvements:
** “Access only to initial folder” should be changed to “Access only to default directory” (so that we use the same terms for the parameters on the setup page)

column58:

column1: Lenovo ThinkCentre Neo 50q Gen5 | Only left channel working on system; both channels working in igel-sound-control
column58:
When testing the audio in the Audio Tray App, only the left channel works (also the case when playing audio from e.g. firefox). When looking at alsamixer, there is no indication that the right channel is muted. 

When checking with igel-sound-control, both channels work as expected, but there are some inconsistencies when sliders are being adjusted. If the balance is pulled all the way to the right channel, then the entire speaker volume is zero. There’s also some glitching in alsamixer when this slider is adjusted, and for some moments the left and right channels have different volumes. 

h3. Setup

* Device: Lenovo ThinkCentre Neo 50q Gen 5
* Version: 12.7 or 12.8

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Test audio in Audio Tray App
* Test audio in igel-sound-control (in debugtools)

column1: Kernel build scripts pull in old kernel modules
column58:
The kernel build system currently pulls in modules from older initramfs builds if they exist, leading to version mismatches when upgrading the kernel version (i.e., 6.12.48 to 6.12.52 for instance).

This is caused by an oversight in {{IGEL/initramfs_modules_lxos}} that does not exclude the initramfs directories while searching for a specific module. Ironically, the other script, {{IGEL/initramfs_install}} does so.

Backport this change.

Also, at least one module was moved around by upstream (back in 2017…) and we should do the same.

column1: Restart igelpkgd on failure
column58:
h2. Impact

The igelpkgd service fail to restart automatically when they encounter issues. This impacts users by causing interruptions in notifications.

h2. Expected behaviour

The service should automatically restart upon failure. This ensures continuous notification delivery without manual intervention.

h2. Actual behaviour

Currently, the services do not restart automatically when they fail. Users experience downtime in notifications.

h2. Steps to reproduce

* Cause a failure in the igelpkgd service, e.g. {{kill -s SIGSEG $(pgrep igelpkgd)}}
* Observe that the service does not restart automatically. Can be checked by running the command {{systemctl status igel-packagemanager}}

column1: Restart igel-notify* on failure
column58:
h2. Impact

The igel-notifyd and igel-notify-ui services fail to restart automatically when they encounter issues. This impacts users by causing interruptions in notifications.

The services should automatically restart upon failure. This ensures continuous notification delivery without manual intervention.

Currently, the services do not restart automatically when they fail. Users experience downtime in notifications.

h2. Steps to reproduce

* Cause a failure in the igel-notifyd or igel-notify-ui service, e.g. {{kill -s SIGSEG <pid of igel-notifyd || igel-notify-ui>}}

{noformat}Restart=on-failure{noformat}

column1: igel-desktop: using window-decoration needs two clicks if internal-UI is open
column58:
* correct behavior:
** in IGEL OS 12.7, opening a tray app and then click on another window title bar (e.g. terminal) does two things:
*** closing the igel-system-tray-window (because of focus-out on outside click)
*** focus and trigger the appropriate action (e.g. close, maximize) directly, no other click needed
* bug with new mutter-plugin:
** in IGEL OS 12.8, with new mutter-plugin tray-apps, we need two clicks:
*** have one of the new igel-desktop-coded tray-apps open (a11y, time&date, language), or start-menu
*** first click on terminal title bar (window-decoration) closes the tray app and focus terminal
*** second click triggers the action (e.g. close or maximize)
*** the “old” igel-system-tray tray-apps do not have this problem, they still behave correct, as in 12.7

We see “{{activate_window_under_mouse_event}}” logs, but it seems that the window is not properly and directly focused (only on second click) ?

+Analysis so far:+

* when an internal WPEwebview-UI is open (start-menu, time&date, a11y, language-tray-app),
the {{input_grab_actor}} is active and the webview has focus
* first button event of type PRESS hits on the {{input_grab_actor}}
* button-press-event is piped through our hit-detection {{should_activate_window_under_mouse_event}}
** hit internal UI → focus stays grabbed
** hit outside of ui-area → unfocus webview, release grab_handle, activate window under event coordinates
* the button-event is not correctly propagated further (x)
** this can be seen with the tool “/usr/bin/xev” on a test-system
** the xev-window does not receive button-press (x)
** have xev-window open
** have e.g. language-tray open
** move mouse over the xev-window
** no input-events are logged by the xev-window, because input-events are handled by the active {{input_grab_actor}} (/)
** click inside xev-window, but not on its window-decoration
** language-tray closes, unset focus from webview, set {{input_grab_actor}} non-reactive (/)
** xev-window does not get button-press (x)
* the next button-event is of type RELEASE
** the {{input_grab_actor}} is no longer reactive, no hit-detection is performed (/)
** the xev-window gets the button-release (/)
* removing the focus from the webview causes some input-event handling in our InputManager, we see this in the igel-desktop log
* during the event-handling of the button-PRESS, many things happen before we  {{return CLUTTER_EVENT_PROPAGATE}}
** {{should_activate_window_under_mouse_event}}
*** causing {{ungrab_focus}}
**** causing some focus-event-handling in the InputManager
**** causing frontend to remove the ui-area, send update to backend
**** causing massive frontend-backend-communication
** {{activate_window_under_mouse_event}}
** event propagation does not result in the wanted behavior (x)
*** is the event already lost? or replaced?
because so many things happen between receiving the event on the {{input_grab_actor}} and propagating it further ?
* the window-decoration can be added to a window from client-side or from server-side
** server-side
*** mutter adds the window-decoration
*** terminal window for example
*** the window-decoration does not belong to the window’s input-region
*** the window-decoration does not get input-events
** client-side
*** the software, which created the window, also paints the window-decoration
*** firefox for example
*** the window-decoration does get some input-events but no button-click-events

Ideas:

* just for testing, wrap all the things, that are happening between receiving the event on the {{input_grab_actor}} and propagating it further,
in a glib signal timeout, to execute these things AFTER {{CLUTTER_EVENT_PROPAGATE}}
* do we need to “save” the button-press-event, and send it again (milliseconds) later?
Not sure if this is possible with meta/clutter API.
* maybe this is solved by this: [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11199?focusedCommentId=263582|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11199?focusedCommentId=263582] (X-input-region never set to None)
need to test.
* learn more about these functions:
[http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/method.Window.get_frame_type.html|http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/method.Window.get_frame_type.html]
[http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/method.Window.get_frame.html|http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/method.Window.get_frame.html]
Seems quite promising 
* detect click on window-decoration button:
[http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/signal.Display.grab-op-begin.html|http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/signal.Display.grab-op-begin.html]
[http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/enum.GrabOp.html|http://itga-devdocs.igel.local/manual/meta/enum.GrabOp.html] META_GRAB_OP_FRAME_BUTTON (see {{/usr/include/mutter-11/meta/common.h)}}
tested this successfully, but not sure if this leads us somewhere…

11/Dec/25 11:32 AM;712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8;Status update:

Inspecting the drag-drop data inside the drag-drop handler is not possible since there is no access to the GtkSelectionData, we can only allow dropping or block it completely we cannot differentiate dropped data type  on this level.

We can connect to the drag-data-received signal and inspect the data of the drop. Here I tried simply not propagating the drop by returning and finishing the drop with success == false. But the URL is still loaded in the webview.  Webkit2Gtk seems to have a default handler that handles calling a navigation action if a link is dropped. It looks like intercepting / overriding that default is not possible.

We might have to unset the whole webview widget from drag-and-drop to get rid of the default handling and then instate our own handling / rebuild dnd to get the behaviour we want.

 After talking to Andreas:

* Supply global drag & drop disable setter so consumer can set to not be a drag destination or source in libigelwebkit
* Modify igel-secure-kiosk to set those flags on the navigation bar webview
* As a follow up: unset the default handling of drag and drop events and rebuild drag and drop handling in libigelwebkit on the webview with only our handlers.

Nothing can be dropped on the toolbar but it is still possible to drag a button with icon from the toolbar onto the main webview.

There is a bug report for this:

[https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=200297|https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=200297|smart-link] 


To me it feels like the whole drag-and-drop behaviour handling is , badly documented (old code api examples, sometimes even wrong docs with swizzled expected true/false return values).

We will have to find another solution. A commenter on the webkit bug mentioned above uses javascript to block drag-and-drop.

The unset solution would’ve been nice as it could’ve worked on igel-secure-kiosk level without a libigelwebkit modification, but if we need javascript we have to modify libigelwebkit.

Idea:
We could go with unsetting the widget as a destination and modifying the frontend to stop drag and drop where we act as a source. Then we wouldn’t need a base_system / libigelwebkit change.

column1: RDP: incorrectly handles user logon name, if the UPN suffix is different from domain name
column58:
RDP client when presented with a user logon name and domain, where the suffix of the logon name is different from the domain, replaces the suffix with the domain name which can lead to logon failures

h3. Steps to reproduce:

# Create a new active directory user, e.g. {{jane.doe@lx.test}}
# Using *ADSIEdit*, change *userPrincipalName* to {{jane.admin@lx.local}}

!image-20251209-112037.png|width=400,alt="image-20251209-112037.png"!

# Using IGEL Setup, configure a session with the credentials:
## Enable Single-Sign On: *Off*
## Server: any RDP server, e.g. {{win2019-1.lx.test}}
## Username: {{jane.admin@lx.local}}
## Domain: {{lx.test}}
## Password: <the password>

!image-20251209-112751.png|width=686,alt="image-20251209-112751.png"!

# Save
# Start the session:
## expected result: the session successfully connects to the server
## observed result: the session fails to connect to the server and shows an incorrect logon name

!image-20251209-113113.png|width=686,alt="image-20251209-113113.png"!

The scenario can be made more subtle/realistic:

# Set up IGEL client to login to Active Directory domain lx.test
# Set up an RDP session with Enable Single Sign-On: On
# log in to IGEL session with the username jane.admin@lx.local
## Expected result: login is successful
## Observed result: login is successful
# Start the SSO RDP session
## Expected result: login is successful
## Observed result: login is not successful

The RDP client apparently replaces the suffix part of the provided logon name with the domain, which is not warranted. In extreme cases this can even result in logging in the wrong user (if the users have the same password, which is of course unlikely, but not impossible).

Windows native RDP client, as well as other VDI clients for IGEL OS all support username having a different suffix than the domain and don’t try to ‘fix’ the username.

h3. Impact:

There is at least one customer who uses Evidian as authentication infrastructure, and for whom the combination of Evidian client configured to use UPN as username, and RDP session doesn’t work.

But the behavior itself is very strange. The RDP client is changing the given user logon name for no good reason. The modified name is not guaranteed to work at all. The only reason that we don’t hear many complaints is that using a UPN suffix that is different from the DNS domain name is uncommon.

The much more sensible way to handle a mismatch between the UPN suffix and the DNS domain would be to just keep the UPN entirely as is.

column1: Evidian: UPN mode not respected by the RDP session
column58:
When ‘use UPN’ is enabled in the Evidian app parameters, the app requests the user’s UPN from the EAM server. The intention is to use user’s UPN as their username in the RDP/CTX/etc. session.

Expected result:

username in the RDP session is the user’s UPN as can be verified by the RDP session logs

Observed result:

username is not the user’s UPN and instead is <short username>@<full domain name>

Analysis:

When ‘use UPN’ is enabled, rsUserAuth passes the user’s UPN as username, but also passes the fqdn domain name as domain to the hua binary an ultimately to the session startup script.

And the RDP app, when presented with a username in the user@suffix format and a separate domain value will replace suffix with the separately provided domain name. As a result, the RDP app will not respect the passed in username as UPN and replace it with <short username>@<domainname> which may not necessarily match the UPN.

-Proposed solution:-

-In the session starter script (evidian_trg_start.py) check for the value of ‘use UPN’ param (app.evidian.options.upn_format) and nullify the domain name if it is true.-

Upon further research, this looks like an incorrect behavior on the part of the RDP client. [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3608|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3608|smart-link] 

h3. Proposed workaround:

implement a parameter-controlled flow that check:

* if UPN mode is enabled for Evidian
* if the session type is RDP
* if the username has a domain suffix already

then don’t put anything into the domain parameter of the session. This should fix the RDP behavior UPN usernames at least in some use cases.

h3. Further research:

UPNs must be unique within an AD forest. And in multi-forest environments with trust relationships, UPN suffices are still expected to be unique. As a reliable rule, when a user logs in with their UPN, they don’t need to specify their domain separately, since the UPN is enough to identify the user. The domain does not add anything to the UPN to help identify the user and might even create more confusion, if the UPN suffix is different from the dns domain.

*That means that it should be safe to drop the domain parameter value for all sessions, if the UPN mode is enabled.*

*P.S.* It looks like there are only two unambiguously supported logon formats for AD users:

* <NetBIOS domain>\<sAMAccountName>
* <userPrincipalName>

Other combinations are supported in practice, but essentially Windows tries it’s best to interpret the input if the canonical interpretation fails to identify the user. Thus, when given <NetBIOS domain>\<userPrincipalName>, Windows will first try to look for sAMAccountName that matches the part to the right of \. And only if that fails and the right part ‘looks like’ a UPN, might Windows try to look for UPN matches. 

Same for <dns.domain>\<sAMAccountName>. Windows will try to resolve dns.domain into NetBIOS domain, but this is not guaranteed to succeed.

Why is this relevant? Because evidian client retrieves exactly 4 user attributes from the EAM server:

* _UserDomain_, which is the DNS domain name, *_not_* _the NetBIOS domain name_
* _UserLogin_, which is the sAMAccountName
* _UserPassword_, which is, well, the password
* UserPrincipalName, which, again, is the userPrincipalName

So, when the UPN mode is not used, there is no way to construct a canonical <NetBIOS domain>\<sAMAccountName> logon format, which can lead to problems in some rare cases. And constructing something like <sAMAccountName>@<dns.domain.name> is not guaranteed to match any UPN, or to be correctly interpreted otherwise. Although in practice Windows does seem to correctly guess that the part before @ should be treated as sAMAccountName.

All in all, although most of the non-canonical combinations of NetBIOS and DNS domain names with sAMAccountName and userPrincipalName are resolved correctly, there is a potential for failed logins when these non-canonical combinations are used. So, whenever we have enough information, we should pass the user logon identifier in one of the two canonical forms. 

And evidian doesn’t provide enough information for the non-UPN format.

column1: Evidian: fails to connect to RDP/Citrix session when more than one session is configured
column58:
Current implementation looks for a fixed session name and only checks the session with the largest index. If the name doesn’t match, no session is started.

This is unexpected for the administrator who may reasonably expect that if a session with the expected fixed name exists, it should be started by the evidian app, even if other sessions with other names exist too.

column1: IMH | make libvirt close the decrypted device when libvirt.virStorageVol.delete() is called
column58: The libvirt function delete() for the virStorageVol class currently does not close the decrypted device if it is still open when trying to remove a LV from the igel type pool. This prevents virt_manager from also deleting the LVs of the domain if the “Delete associated storage files“ check mark is set. It should also allow us to use the libvirt delete() function instead of crypt_close().

column1: Evidian: Citrix: remote desktop connection to pre-defined resource interrupted
column58:
h3. Scenario:

As a customer, I want my users to tap their badges to the reader and automatically log in to a remote desktop. The VDI infrastructure is Citrix, the authentication infrastructure is Evidian.

h3. Implementation: 

* Evidian app is configured to start a pre-defined Citrix session. 
* The Citrix session is configured to automatically start a named resource (application, in this case a published desktop).

h3. Expected result: 

the users taps their badge, Evidian app starts the Citrix session, once the session is started the remote desktop is started and the user can start working in the remote dekstop.

h3. Observed result: 

… once the Citrix session is started, the remote desktop connection is visibly being started and then abruptly interrupted w/o showing the user their remote desktop. Meanwhile the user session on the remote server is successfully started, but the user doesn’t see it on their thin client device.

The autostart option for the Citrix Secure Access Client is not functioning. This affects users who rely on this feature for automatic startup.

The Citrix Secure Access Client should start automatically when the system boots up if the autostart option is enabled.

The autostart option does not initiate the Citrix Secure Access Client as expected.

The bug is present in the Citrix Secure Access Client.

Set {{app.citrix_nsgclient.sessions.citrix_nsgclient0.autostart}} to true.

02/Dec/25 11:17 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;I would also vote for the approach to run the greeter-window (or plural, windows, one for each monitor) maximized.

In general, windows are controlled by the windowmanager.
The windowmanager knows the reserved size and position for a panel (= taskbar, window of type DOCK).
Therefore, the windowmanager will automatically shrink a window, to not collide with a taskbar.
See [https://specifications.freedesktop.org/wm/latest/ar01s05.html#id-1.6.11|https://specifications.freedesktop.org/wm/latest/ar01s05.html#id-1.6.11]

{quote}The purpose of struts is to reserve space at the borders of the desktop. This is very useful for a docking area, a taskbar or a panel, for instance. The Window Manager should take this reserved area into account when constraining window positions - maximized windows, for example, should not cover that area.{quote}

Currently, the greeter-code tries to detect a window of type DOCK
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-greeter/browse/window.c#5067-5109|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-greeter/browse/window.c#5067-5109]

column1: Quest KACE agent (ampagent) crashes with segfault during inventory
column58:
For ROCHE, together with Sven Hain ([sven.hain@quest.com|mailto:sven.hain@quest.com]) from Quest I created the Quest KACE Agent (ampagent) as App for IGEL OS. 
After a successful implementation at ROCHE this should get an official, public app via IGEL Ready / Alliances team. 
The app is a little tricky, because it is designed to run on almost any Linux Distribution and version. 
In the original source there are several daemons and even old-style init.d daemons. 

I think I figured out which files & folders need to be persistent and what is necessary for the agent to run. 

*Current status of the app:*

* The app can be configured via profile, gets installed and starts communication with the Quest KACE Server
* During registration it gets the servers certificate and configuration parameters and stores them persistent. 
* One initial step, obviously before the client gets fully registered at the KACE Server is a full inventory 
In its logs you can see that it tries to call ipkg-query and apt list 
Right after that the agent crashes and the journal reports a segfault 
I assume that is caused by not getting any inventory information from IGEL OS.
* I tried to “fake” dpkg-query by adding a faked “script” to /usr/bin calling igelpkgctl -list | grep installed, but that did not help

Guess we need support on DEV-Level to work with Quest to find a solution for this behavior. On their side or on our.

*Remark:* the customer first wanted to have a complete list of all installed “packages”like they get this from their Ubuntu Servers, but I told them  that won’t happen. 

They now prefer, like I would, some kind of ipkg -list | grep installed. Maybe with some additional information like App Name, Version, Installed on, Size

column1: Login: 5 seconds unneeded delay
column58:

In {{/usr/sbin/igel-session-wait}} there is a wait for file {{/run/user/$ID/igel/igelsession_ready }}, but this file isn't created any more (in OS 11 through {{killwait_postsetupd igelsession}} in pam_igelsession). So it waits until the timeout of 5 seconds.

Also IGEL Smartcard isn’t supported any more ({{auth.login.igelsmartcard}}), so the complete wait mechanism can be removed.

02/Dec/25 5:51 PM;712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8;Status update:

GTKmm Approach: 
Researched how to keep the input handling in GTKmm by monitoring not only our main window but also the child windows and dialogs that get created. This approach is very complicated and error prone because some of the dialogs that are created are instantiated from the libigelwebkit library. Monitoring and connect / disconnecting to the corresponding signals for each window is cumbersome and would rely on polling the application for its child windows as there is no signal when the number of  child windows changes.

X11 Approach:
To listen for global x11 events we have to use XSelectInput on the X Root window and then monitor the XDisplays Connection filedescriptor for changes. After connecting to this and keeping it from blocking our GTK mainloop I seem to get events very sporadically (And not even the ones I filter for). It seems an XGrab is recommended to catch more events but that breaks the input handling of our window.
=> After spending some time on this and not getting a satisfying solution i’d go with the approach described below.

There is a XScreensaver extension in X11 we can poll to get the time in milliseconds that the user has been idle. This looks like a straight forward solution that covers our needs without the extra effort needed implementing this functionality ourselves.

02/Dec/25 5:07 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;What does not work:
not using fullscreen, but simply set the main-window maximized without window-decoration (mocked fullscreen).
Does not work.

This is window-manager specific (!)
The window-manager can always decide to make a window fullscreen, if you try to mock fullscreen.
Also, the window-manager can maximize a window, if you give the window the size of the monitor.

Quote from gtk-docu:

{quote}the [window’s] state is at the window managers discretion. For example, it might decide to maximize a window that almost fills the screen.{quote}

From [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11865150/let-a-window-display-above-a-fullscreen-window-in-gtk|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11865150/let-a-window-display-above-a-fullscreen-window-in-gtk]:

{quote}The main way to tell the window manager to keep winB above winA is through the "transient for" hint, set in GTK+ with [gtk_window_set_transient_for()|https://developer.gnome.org/gtk3/3.16/GtkWindow.html#gtk-window-set-transient-for].

But the behavior is basically going to vary with window manager (which is intended). So you kind of need to just live with that and assume people will use a WindowManager that works how they want it to.{quote}

This explains why we have the problem in 12.7 with xf-windowmanager and firefox in fullscreen.
We do +not+ have the problem on our dev-VMs (certainly with another window-manager, not xfwm).
We do +not+ have the problem on 12.8 with mutter window-manager (tested on 12.8 with firefox in fullscreen, print, use gtk-print-dialog, print-to-file, open filechooser).

So, {{xfwindowmanager}} causes the problem.

* Should we patch xf-windowmanager?
* Should we patch gtk-3, the gtk-filechooser/print-dialog?
** create the filechooser out of the print-dialog:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkprinteroptionwidget.c#541-547|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkprinteroptionwidget.c#541-547]
** set filechooser transient for parent:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkfilechooserdialog.c#669-675|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkfilechooserdialog.c#669-675]
Quote from docu:
”Dialog windows should be set transient for the main application window they were spawned from. This allows window managers to e.g. keep the dialog on top of the main window, or center the dialog over the main window.”
** set the filechooser modal:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkprinteroptionwidget.c#575|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/gtk-3-bookworm/browse/gtk/gtkprinteroptionwidget.c#575]
Quote from docu:
”Modal windows prevent interaction with other windows in the same application. To keep modal dialogs on top of main application windows, use {{gtk_window_set_transient_for()}} to make the dialog transient for the parent; most window managers will then disallow lowering the dialog below the parent.”

I’d like to make you aware of one security issue we found *but which is in our opinion not worth to fix it*. We need your decision whether we can move on without doing anything.

* in one situation, this can be circumvented:

** AND with base_system < 12.8.0 (i.e. 12.7.4)
** AND when user wants to change the stored file path
** then the user can see the desktop
* [we know the reason for it|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13121?focusedCommentId=261511] - at the end it is because of the behavior of the old XFCE window manager (which is used in 12.7.x)

* we think that we can live with this issue, because
** in most use cases, “print to file” will not be allowed by the admin
** the issue will only be in 12.7.x which will soon be replaced by 12.8.0 with our new mutter which does not show the above issue!
** admins should never configure the system so that desktop icons are given → desktop can be seen, but nothing can be done by the user

column1: Lenovo T14 Gen 6 AMD | GPU hangs
column58:
I’m seeing very frequent GPU hangs with this machine.

It is typically very easy to reproduce and seems to be happening often whenever there is an overlay window active, but also generally whenever the mouse cursor is being hidden.

My current workaround is a script to wiggle the mouse, e.g.,

{noformat}while :; do xdotool mousemove_relative 1 0 sleep 0.001 mousemove_relative -- -1 0; sleep 0.1s; done{noformat}

and keeping the mouse out of the currently active/focused window.

That works, but is unnerving.

The GPU hangs seem to show up in dmesg as well:

{noformat}[Wed Nov 26 11:05:14 2025] amdgpu 0000:c4:00.0: [drm] REG_WAIT timeout 1us * 10 tries - optc3_lock line:128
[Wed Nov 26 11:25:15 2025] amdgpu 0000:c4:00.0: [drm] REG_WAIT timeout 1us * 10 tries - optc3_lock line:128
[Wed Nov 26 11:28:29 2025] amdgpu 0000:c4:00.0: [drm] REG_WAIT timeout 1us * 10 tries - optc3_lock line:128{noformat}

Doing some research, it looks like it might be fixed by upgrading MESA to 25.0.4 or newer: [https://community.frame.work/t/solved-amdgpu-crashes-and-artifacts-with-mesa-25-kernel-6-13/65312/51?page=2|https://community.frame.work/t/solved-amdgpu-crashes-and-artifacts-with-mesa-25-kernel-6-13/65312/51?page=2|smart-link] 

{{stable/os12}} currently includes MESA 25.0.7, which should be new enough, while {{stable/old/12.7}} is on MESA 25.0.2.

I’m contemplating backporting MESA 25.0.7 to 12.7 to see if that fixes the issue.

The {{REG_WAIT timeout}} messages are gone, though, but the whole UI still freezes, which can be temporarily fixed by restarting the window manager (xfwm4 or mutter). Some apps like Zoom also have to be restarted, since they fully stop painting.

Disabling PSR as mentioned by [~accountid:712020:0a53f544-6c21-42a8-a85f-f6e0aad28b0a] via {{amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x12}} seems to help - since I have enabled this kernel option, I haven’t seen any freezes. I’m 90 % sure that disabling Panel Self Refresh via the dcdebugmask value {{0x10}} should be enough, but adding {{DC_DISABLE_STUTTER}} ({{0x02}}) probably also doesn’t hurt, whatever that does.

I’ll retest with only {{amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x10}}set (dropping the 2 and {{amdgpu.gpu_recovery=1}}) to make sure that this is really the only thing fixing the issue.

That said, even if the issue is gone with this flag being set, it’s not a real “fix”, since disabling Panel Self Refresh has a huge impact on battery life, as far as I know. The modern idle functionality and power saving features highly depend on the panel refreshing by itself, so that the GPU can actually go to sleep and not draw power.

column1: Fix permissions for UMS CA certs
column58:
The rmagent installs UMS CA certificates in the system-wide OpenSSL trust store (/etc/ssl/certs) since the IGEL OS 12.7.3. This is done by creating a symlink in /etc/ssl/certs/ for each certificate in the /wfs/igel-rmagent/trust-store/. But the /wfs/igel-rmagent directory is accessible only by root, so user applications fail to load OpenSSL trust store.
As a solution the CA certs must be copied into the /etc/ssl/certs directory, the files must have 0644 permission.
column244: * Fixed access OpenSSL trust store for user applications.

column1: igelpkgd: Rework app installation process in  UpdateDaemonClient
column58:
h2. Actual behaviour

When the installation fails or is canceled, the UpdateProgressWrapper pointer in UpdateDaemonClient is reset to nullptr. This design leads to unwanted error handling and potential segmentation faults.

h2. Expected behaviour

The app installation process should handle errors gracefully without causing segmentation faults. The UpdateProgressWrapper should maintain its state even if the installation fails or is canceled. Restart the igelpkgd process if it fails, which requires restarting the igel-packagemanager.service.

h2. Other information

The UpdateDaemonClient holds a [std::unique_ptr<UpdateProgressWrapper>|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igelpkgd/browse/igelpkgd/src/UpdateDaemonClient.h#78] pointer where all the information of a current installation is stored.

column1: Fix configuration of the storage of the rmagent's key in the ARM product
column58:
The file /etc/igel-rmagent/rmagent.conf contains static configuration of base option. As the ‘identity' storage the [file:///etc/igel-rmagent|file:///etc/igel-rmagent] is configured at the moment in the ARM project. But in IGEL OS the /etc isn’t a permanent file system, so that after a reboot the previous key is away and the new one (created during boot on demand) doesn’t suit anymore and so the TLS handshake fails, as the rmagent can’t prove that it has the private part of the key signed in the /wfs/igel-rmagent/cert.pem.

Solution: Set the storage location to a permanent filesystem - WFS. Eg:
”identity”: “file:///wfs/igel-rmagent”

column1: local app portal: Slow start-up time and unresponsive UI
column58:
h2. Impact

The App-Portal triggers the {{igelpkgd.update}} function on startup. This causes a slow startup time and makes the UI unresponsive for users.

h2. Expected behaviour

The update should only be triggered when an actual installation of an app begins.

h2. Actual behaviour

Currently, the {{igelpkgd.update}} function is triggered at startup, resulting in a non-reactive UI and delayed startup.

h2. Steps to reproduce

* Launch the App-Portal.
* Observe the startup process.
* Notice the slow startup time and unresponsive UI.

h2. Environment

* Latest 12.7.4
* Nightly 12.8

h2. Workarounds

N/A

h2. Other information

For more details, refer to the code snippet: [MainWindow.cpp#56|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/app-portal/browse/appportal/src/viewmodel/MainWindow.cpp#56]

column363:
21/Nov/25 4:48 PM;712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8;Summary

# pmclient.update was triggerd in pageLoadFinished event (leading to multiple calls, slowing everything) 
=> Remove pmclient.update as it is not needed, we listen to pmclient availableApplicationsChanged which is sufficient to inform us about changes to the repositories
# Gtk::Grid container was added to Applicationwindow multiple times in pageLoadFinished leading to Warnings in log
=> Only add once during init and update on changes
# Multiple unneeded webview.load calls when the dropdown was updated with new entries
=> Disconnect the changed_signal of the dropdown prior to repopulating it with new data and then connecting to it again.

Also modernized logging and made it easier to follow to easier find issues like the ones above. And tested installation, uninstallation of apps to ensure proper functionality

column1: DefaultBrowser: Links open in Chromium even though xdg-settings reports Firefox as default and inconsistent xdg-open behavior!
column58:
*Title:* Links open in Chromium even though xdg-settings reports Firefox as default. xdg-settings get default-web-browser sometimes hangs.

*Preconditions:*
Install latest versions of Edge, Chromium and Firefox via UMS profile.
Do NOT configure any browser explicitly as the default via UI (no preferred browser set).
Confirm standard xdg utilities are present (xdg-open, xdg-settings).

*Step to Reproduce:*
1. Install Edge, Chromium, Firefox using UMS profile and apply profile to IGEL device.
2. Open a terminal session on the IGEL device.
3. Verify current default web browser by entering the following cmd: xdg-settings get default-web-browser
   3.1. Observed that it prints: firefox.desktop
4. Try to open a URL via xdg-open: xdg-open "http://www.google.com"
   4.1. Observed: window opens in Firefox browser.
5. Perform a manual click test: in a terminal or text environment, type www.google.com and Ctrl + mouse-click (Ctrl+Click a link).



*Actual Result:*
1. xdg-settings get default-web-browser often reports firefox, but clicking a link opens Chromium instead of Firefox.
2. Sometimes xdg-settings get default-web-browser hangs/does not return output, inconsistent behavior. Behavior is intermittent, not consistent across repeated runs.


*Expected Result:*
xdg-settings get default-web-browser should return the system default browser reliably (e.g., firefox.desktop).
xdg-open <URL> and clicking links via GUI should open the reported default browser (Firefox) consistently. No hanging of xdg-settings command.

column1: Horizon: "save last user name" adds the domain more than once
column58:
When “save last user name” is enabled and the domain is typed separately from the username, the username is saved as “domain\username”, which is still valid. And after another connection, the username is saved as “domain\domain\username” which is not valid anymore and forces the user to edit it manually.

h3. Steps to reproduce

Important connection server details:

* The server should be configured to hide the domain name in the client login Window:

!image-20251125-091535.png|width=548,alt="image-20251125-091535.png"!

I haven’t tested if the same effect can be achieved with a direct connection plugin.



# Create a Horizon session with minimal configuration:
## session > valid connection server address
## global > allow unverifiable certificates (if necessary)
## session > save last user name
## session > domain
# Save and close
# Start the session
# Connect to the server; login window appears as expected.
## Expected result: the Username field is empty, because there hasn’t been a last user yet
## Observed result: the Username field includes domain and backslash: <domain>\
# Add username and password and click login; login is successful.
# Close the Horizon client.
# Start the session again.
# Connect to the server; login window appears.
## Expected result: not sure, open to discussion
## Observed result: the Username field contains <domain>\<last user name> and the Login button is available
# Add the password and click login; login is successful.
# Close the Horizon client
# Start the session again.
# Connect to the server; login window appears
## Expected result: the Username field contains a valid username
## Observed result: the Username field contains <domain>\<domain>\<last user name> and the Login button is unavailable

column1: Auto Re-Enrollment for Expired Certificates - Beyond Renewal Window
column58:
Implement automatic certificate renewal: if a device certificate is already expired _and_ the 30-day pre-expiration window has passed, the system should automatically trigger a re-enrollment to deploy a new certificate.

Add logic on IGEL OS devices to:

# Detect certificates that are expired and outside the standard 30-day renewal window.
# Automatically trigger the device re-enrollment process in this scenario.
# Retrieve and install a new valid certificate upon completion.
column223:
* Expired certificates past the 30-day threshold are automatically detected.
* Re-enrollment is triggered without user intervention.
* A new certificate is successfully issued and deployed.
* Device logs reflect the detection and re-enrollment steps.
* Normal certificate renewal behavior remains unaffected.

column1: Two power button ACPI events result in 90sec timeout during shutdown
column58:
If the system is configured to shut down after x seconds when pressing the power button, then we run into this error:

* Pressing the power button twice in a row
* IGEL OS runs into a 90sec timeout before the system shut downs.



This is a general issue which can be reproduced on any hardware.

It first occured in LG factory, because their power button sends 2 ACPI events at once.


See [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12942|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12942|smart-link]

column1: rmagent must use only hardware NICs for determining MAC address of device
column58:
The MAC address of the NIC involved into the connection to UMS is used as the primary key to store hardware information of a device in the UMS DB. Some customers connect to their UMS over a VPN (eg NCP VPN), in that case the MAC address of the VPN interface is determined as the ‘activehwaddr' which is used then by UMS for storing/accessing hardware info, but the MAC address isn’t always unique (at least in case of NCP), so that several devices are linked to the same instance of the hardware info in the UMS DB.

The solution:
the rmagent must check whether the active NIC is a real hardware device. If the NIC is not a hardware device then the rmagent must choose another interface having a valid IP config in this order:
1. ethernet
2. wifi

column1: igel-desktop: internal tray-app covered by a notification
column58:
h3. Problem / Bug

A notification can overlap an internal igel-desktop tray-app. Both open at the same time, the notification covers the tray-app. 


h3. Solution

Idea: two events for both directions to inform backend/frontend about opened notifications / tray apps 

* igel-desktop backend already has the information about open UIs in general, with the ‘ui-areas’ signal
** but we especially want the information about open internal trays.
** ui-areas also include the start-menu, which is not interesting here in this ticket.

column1: LG CQ6xx series - Shutdown via power button takes >90 seconds
column58:
LG showed me the issue live at their Now&Next booth.



Issue is a blocker for their factory, because they shut down the devices via power button after factory preload test.



How to reproduce:

# Change default power down action in setup to shutdown instead of suspend 
# Press power button



Seems like a systemd service might run into a timeout, probably igel-network-online.target
column80:
Initial debugging, figured out that the root cause is a deadlock when processing multiple shutdown events, and that the issue is triggered for LG because the power off button has both fixed function (FF) and control method (CM) definitions in ACPI, so a single button press triggers two distinct events.

Start of a workaround implementation.;07/Nov/25 12:08 PM;b1d0318d-2627-4315-b998-6b172fa4c420;28800

In all cases, systemd-logind logs the short hardware key press twice, which is odd. This is not happening on a Lenovo laptop, so the action seems to be triggered twice and that might be some part of what is causing this.
column367:
04/Nov/25 2:22 PM;712020:9faabc93-72fc-451e-b514-dd2fd1240c23;Also reproducible with 12.6.0, even with a full factory reset.

The device features two ACPI power buttons (exposed as {{/dev/input/event1}} and {{/dev/input/event2}}) - one CM (Control Method) and one FF (Fixed Function). The ACPI spec says that whenever a FF button is available, it should be preferred over the CM button. Obviously we’re not doing this.

{noformat}[    0.315418] ACPI: button: Sleep Button [SLPB]
[    0.318836] ACPI: button: Power Button [PBTN]
[    0.319119] ACPI: button: Power Button [PWRF]{noformat}

The kernel originally ignored additional buttons once it found one of a type, but that was removed 21 years ago and it since always exposes all buttons it finds.

So then… maybe {{systemd-logind}} should ignore a CM button if a FF button has been found? Requires a deeper dive into this whole matter…
column368:
04/Nov/25 7:10 PM;712020:9faabc93-72fc-451e-b514-dd2fd1240c23;This issue is reproducible with any kind of hardware if the HW button is pressed twice in rapid succession.

I’ve tested it on a Lenovo L14 Gen 6 and it happens there as well, if the HW button is pressed twice relatively rapidly (Lenovo laptops require a press of about a second to register, though).

Thus, in general this issue seems to be caused by two shutdown events being executed in close time proximity.

Not sure if the shutdown operation is supposed to be idempotent or not. We’ll also need more debugging to figure out what exactly is happening at shutdown time and what seems to be deadlocking (until it is killed 90 seconds later).
column370:
05/Nov/25 9:44 AM;712020:9faabc93-72fc-451e-b514-dd2fd1240c23;[~accountid:712020:0a53f544-6c21-42a8-a85f-f6e0aad28b0a] Yep, great idea, will do that.

Meanwhile, I found out that the issue can be triggered on any device if you just press the HW power off button twice in rapid succession. Some HW power buttons require a press of at least a second or so (like Lenovo laptops), but pressing it twice will reliably reproduce the issue on all machines.

Looks like running shutdown twice leads to a deadlock in some service. Eugen suggested that it’s probably just a service behaving incorrectly and not systemd(-logind) acting up.

column1: igelpkg: documentation mentions igel/input.json supporting regexps for source field, but it doesn't
column58:
Page 10 (or really 14) of the igelpkg documentation “From Zero to Hero” mentions that the {{source}} field of entries in {{igel/input.json}} supports regular expressions, but looking at the code (and trying a regexp in there), it’s obvious that nothing actually matches the {{source}} field against {{re.fullmatch ()}}(or any regex engine).

This is probably a feature that was supposed to implemented at some point in time, but was forgotten, and the documentation still spells out the originally planned feature.

Both should be synced up.

In general, it probably makes a lot of sense to support regular expressions for {{igel/input.json}}, although strictly speaking permissions directly in git (but that won’t work for unpacked files).

column58:

column81: Investigating the grab and ungrab focus in the INputManager and it is effect on the gtk context menu;04/Nov/25 8:21 AM;57472b02-4edf-47c2-88ed-36591f890ddb;25200
column362:
04/Nov/25 2:09 PM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;We were able to find a solution to make the gtk grab the focus when it creates the context menu implementing the following :

1 - Implement a separate {{on_button_release_event}} event handler in the IconSocket: This is needed because if we send a a button release instantly on right click while having the focus the context menu will be closed immediately after appearing. 
2- Change the behavior of the {{InputManager::on_button_event_external}} To grab_focus if focus is not grabbed than ungrab the focus: This have been proven to be necessary so that the gtk can grab the focus. The ungrab focus by it self should be enough but in the case of the gtk menu it was proven that the menu will not show if the {{on_button_event_external}} is called while the focus is ungrabbed. So as a work around we grab the focus in this function than make sure that it is ungrabbed before the event is sent to the gtk.

column1: enable_*_service not working for template services

29/Oct/25 9:41 AM;712020:f51b0662-9da8-4f9c-9795-40af8572495a;[~accountid:557058:cc5c73b0-c7fe-4b8e-a783-43b2040be3d3] in /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, initially, libopenh264.so.8 and libopenh264.so.2.6.0 are provided as dummies (by libnoopenh264). That is required so chromium starts, even if no shared object was downloaded, yet.
The script runns as soon as igel-network target is available via systemd service.
It checks the provided libopenh264.so.8, finds the major version: 8 and looks on libopenh264 github for the latest version of said major version, downloads it and replaces the provided libopenh264.so.8.

In my tests, that works but I could imagine that the service did not start for some reason.
column365:
29/Oct/25 12:04 PM;712020:f51b0662-9da8-4f9c-9795-40af8572495a;The main issue seems to be that the igel-openh264-installer@chromium.service is not started in some cases…might very well be connected to the igel-network-online.target
I will remove said target and check internally if the system has access to the internet:

* if no shared object in /services_rw/chromium/openh264 → wait for internet → download latest matching shared object
* if a shared object is available that matches the current major version (how to find out without internet?) → don’t wait for internet but immediately copy the file

OR

* no not copy at all but create symlink from /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu to /services_rw/chromium/openh264/
* be aware that this would require a bind-mount like so:
{{mkdir /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openh264}}
{{mount --bind /services_rw/chromium/openh264 /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openh264}}
{{ln -s /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openh264/libopenh264.so.2.6.0 /services/chromium/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libopenh264.so.8}}

Also, when downgrading, the script does not detect that the latest version does not match the current major version:

* libopenh264.so.8 has libopenh264.so.2.6.0
* downgrade → requires libopenh264.so.7 with latest version libopenh264.so.2.5.1
* finds libopenh264.so.2.6.0 and installs that because it is the “latest“ version but does not match the major version required

column1: After base system update to version 12.7.2+2 Chromium bookmarks disappear
column58:

The original base system version is 12.7.2+1

column1: M70q Gen6 - After resume from suspend, audio tray icon missing and no audio playback possible
column58:
I have only tested this on M70q Gen6 with OS 12.7.2 PR1 so far.



How to reproduce:

# Igel Setup → Security → Logon → *Login with local user password* → set a password
# Suspend for 1 minute or more
# Wake device from suspend, enter local user password



In approx 50% of cases, igel-system-tray does not show audio symbol anymore.
I think there might be a timing issue with pulseaudio here.

{noformat}pactl list short sinks

pactl list short sources
0	auto_null.monitor	module-null-sink.c	s16le 2ch 44100Hz	SUSPENDED{noformat}


Edit: Pulseaudio should not be running in the first place, since we have pipewire as default.



Workaround:

Log out and login again -or- retart pulseaudio service

column1: App dependency issues cause remote management to fail after some time
column58:
Certain app dependency errors cause RMagent to eventually fail, preventing further remote management. After rebooting, or manually disconnecting/connecting RMagent, remote management starts working again for a while, then the pattern repeats.

While RMagent is still active, it produces log messages about once per second, including JSON dictionaries with the apps to be installed. Once the log messages stop, remote management is unavailable. When restarted manually, the entire process repeats.

h2. Steps To Reproduce

h3. Install on the client:

Chromium Browser 139.0.7258.127 BUILD 1.0
Chromium Multimedia Codec 138.0.7204.49 BUILD 1.0

h3. Assign a new Chromium Multimedia Codec Version via UMS:

Chromium Multimedia Codec 137.0.7151.55 BUILD 1.0

This causes an Error message on the device which appears every second. The Attached log shows every second a error and after some time the rmagent stopps with a segfault.

column1: FollowUp - CWA 2503 Build 2: smart card AD authentication fails
column58:
FollowUp from [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3105|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3105|smart-link] to test Citrix login + Igel UIDialogLib + Smart card, there might be open some work.

Details see comments below, here the summary:

* Generally login works fine with smartcard - I found an issue with smartcard login to IgelOS: [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13709|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13709|smart-link] 
* Switching between IGEL and Citrix UIDialogLib is solved now - [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3772|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3772|smart-link] can removed now.
* Switching IGEL and Citrix UIDialogLib works now with activated usecitrixconfig.
column226:

*  revert to CWAL 2503 buld1 or older

With CWA 2505 B 1.0, manual login or authentication (after failed autologin) is possible via the Citrix login window.

With version CWA 25.03 B 2.0, however, manual login is not possible. The same error message appears repeatedly, as with autostart: “Login failed due to wrong credentials...”

Additional information how customer is using it:

{quote}EQUNUMLIBRSER=P;NUMORG=281;NUMEQNUMLIBRSER=§{HOSTNAME};TYPEOFFRNUM=S;SITEACCUEILEQULIBR=CHARTRES

NUMEQNUMLIBRSER=§{HOSTNAME} define the device name
TYPEOFFRNUM=S define the offering type (S/R/C/T)
SITEACCUEILEQULIBR=CHARTRES define the physique site name{quote}

column1: enable_system_service not working for services in /lib/systemd/system
column58:
h2. Impact

The {{enable_system_service}} command does not link services located in {{/lib/systemd/system}}. Users cannot enable these services automatically, but they can still start them manually. This issue may affect multiple applications.

h2. Expected behaviour

The {{enable_system_service}} command should link all services located in {{/lib/systemd/system}} automatically.

h2. Actual behaviour

The {{enable_system_service}} command does not link services in {{/lib/systemd/system}}. Users must start these services manually.

h2. Steps to reproduce

* Run the {{enable_system_service}} command in the [install.sh|http://install.sh] script.
* Check the services located in {{/lib/systemd/system}}.
* Observe that the services are not linked.

h2. Environment

The bug is present in the environment where the {{enable_system_service}} command is executed, specifically when dealing with services in {{/lib/systemd/system}}.

h2. Workarounds

Users can manually start the services as a temporary workaround.

h2. Other information

This issue was detected while working on the {{cloudflare_warp}} app. It may also affect other applications, indicating a need for a fix in the base system.

column1: igel-desktop: windows not visible on lockscreen
column58:
*bug description*

When in lock-screen / login mode, some windows like the system-tray are not visible anymore.



*remark*

Probably related to the latest changes to the screenlock extension where a new layer was introduced in order to not shortly see the desktop content.

entry-point would be the WindowRaiser.cpp in the igel-desktop code-base, igel-desktop/backend/plugins/authentication-layer/window-raiser/WindowRaiser.cpp

This is about creating a cloned ClutterActor of the original window (like tray-window or on-screen-keyboard or the greeter itself), 
and raising this cloned actor higher in our z-ordering, to be above the cloned-greeter-actor, but under our desktop-UI (taskbar).
Such windows must be detected (greeter by window-title, others by the X-Property which is defined in the libXigelscreenlock extension.
See the git/bitbucket history of this WindowRaiser.cpp



*tasks*

* all windows should be visible and usable as it was before

column1: getsetup3: resetuservalue and resetvalue raise an error that can not be excepted
column58:
resetuservalue and resetvalue raise a weird getsetup.socket error, if the value has not been overridden. That error can not be caught with even the broadest of exceptions.

There is a workaround for that that is used in:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/pwa/browse/input/all/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pwa_config/config_item.py|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/pwa/browse/input/all/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pwa_config/config_item.py] - Line 388

This bug has been here for quite a while and can be easily reproduced by having trying to reset a value that was never set.
column362:
14/Oct/25 9:50 AM;712020:590271f0-d8b1-4789-b812-dca0b6ac1880;[~accountid:712020:f51b0662-9da8-4f9c-9795-40af8572495a] Can you please give a minimal example? I tried resetting a value that has never been set before and it doesn’t raise an exception:



{code:python}#!/usr/bin/python3
# <app>
# 	<foo>
# 		<bar>
# 			value=<>
# 			type=<string>
# 			runtime=<true>
# 		</bar>
# 	</foo>
# </app>
import getsetup3
if __name__ == "__main__":
    with getsetup3.Getsetup("rw") as gs:
        gs.resetvalue("app.foo.bar")
{code}
column363:
14/Oct/25 9:58 AM;712020:590271f0-d8b1-4789-b812-dca0b6ac1880;[~accountid:712020:f51b0662-9da8-4f9c-9795-40af8572495a] I think I know what's going on. Please remember that write operations in setupd are transaction based (transaction start, setvalue, transaction commit).
If you open an rw connection to setupd using the python with-Context-Manager, the transaction is only commited on the {{__exit__}} so when you leave the with-context.
So any set operation within this with-Context is only commited to setupd, once leaving the with-context.

As a general rule: Close rw connections to setupd (leave the rw with-context) as soon as all write operations are done so they are all properly commited to setupd.

column1: “Save/Detach and Apply on Reboot” not working , actions not applied after reboot
column58:
When assigning or detaching an App/Profile to a device in UMS, the “Save and Apply on Reboot” and “Detach and Apply changes on Reboot” options do not always work correctly.
If the device is rebooting at the same time the action is sent, the App/Profile is not applied or removed after reboot, and any later “Apply on Reboot” actions stop working.

However, when using “Save and Apply Now” or “Detach and Apply Now”, all pending App/Profile changes are immediately executed and reflected on the device.

h3. *Steps to Reproduce:*

# Assign a  Profile/APP to a device.
# While the device is rebooting, detach the Profile/APP using “Detach and Apply changes on Reboot.”

During additional testing, I was able to identify the trigger for this issue.

If a device is rebooted at the same time an object is assigned with “Save and Apply on Reboot”, the device does not pick up that action once it starts. After this happens, any subsequent “Apply on Reboot” actions become blocked, meaning no new queued actions are processed.

Essentially, the first missed action prevents the queue from executing any further “Apply on Reboot” tasks.

In my specific case, a Browser Profile (Firefox, Edge, and  Chromium) was assigned to the device. While the machine was rebooting, I detached the profile using “Detach and Apply on Reboot.” Once the device finished rebooting, the browser apps were not uninstalled, and from that point onward, any object assigned or detached using “Apply on Reboot” no longer worked.

With this new input, I will update the bug.
