socks proxy localhost:3128 does not work
column58:
cntlm is not prepared to handle the socks protocol via its port 3128. With tsocks and strace on cntlm one can see that cntlm does not undertand the protocol. It gets stuck after reading the client’s initial message waiting for more input and does not respond. Therefore at the moment it is at best useless to configure socks proxy localhost:3128 in the case of proxy autoconfiguration.

Potential solutions:

* cntlm might be able to handle socks on the same port as http and ssl depending on its confiration file
* cntlm might open another port for socks. Then that might be configured for applications to use. In this and the former case SOCKS5Proxy must apparently be specified in the configuration file. 
* Not configuring a socks proxy for applications to use in the case of automatic proxy configuration could also be an option. Can cntlm do anything useful at all for the client via socks, i.e. FindProxyForURL evaluation or NTLM authentication?

column58:

column1: Fix modules (kernelstore) relying on CWD during install/imagepath staging
column58:
IGELmaker’s {{helper::rcopy}} sub has had a bug for probably 10 years, in the sense that switching the cwd didn’t work like designed. It’s heavily used for installing modules/staging them into the imagepath.

The original switch to the module’s data directory worked correctly, but at the end of the function, it was supposed to switch back to the original cwd as set when the sub was called. The original cwd was called by a shellout to the {{pwd}} tool and used the data verbatim. Unfortunately, the returned value included a newline at the end, and using that in the {{chdir}} sub lead to a failure every time.

Fixing this is easy, but unfortunately, some modules’s (private) install scripts currently rely on the buggy behavior of the cwd being set to the module’s data dir. Fortunately, though, this is only the case for the {{kernelstore}} modules, and that can also be fixed quite easily.

Will supply a PR for this.

column364:
12/Mar/26 3:50 PM;712020:650c2ae4-5451-4371-aaca-21f4e1331e77;There are some points that must be addressed (speaking from a real hardware perspective):

* If by ‘Multitouch Gestures’ you mean this new Touchscreen subpage introduced since 12.7.5 [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13272|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13272|smart-link] (mid-December or so), they (the gestures) definitely didn’t work in the version mentioned in the ticket (12.7.2) as they were not yet released.
* If your setup uses only one touchscreen display, it doesn’t really make sense to use the Elo Multitouch driver (that brings unneeded complexity for a rather simple setup).
* Additionally, if your setup makes use of more than one touchscreen device, it doesn’t make sense to use EvTouch as it doesn’t support multimonitor configuration ([https://kb.igel.com/en/igel-os/current/evtouch-usb|https://kb.igel.com/en/igel-os/current/evtouch-usb|smart-link] )
* Calibration is not needed for Elo Multitouch as this is a more modern driver (the coordinates are already normalized for the display’s resolution, the controller does all that math inside it). This doesn’t mean that calibration is prohibited → you can do it, but there may be some side effects.

*I’d say that the problem seems to be inside Citrix* as it may not correctly forward touch events to the VM. *On a real hardware, everything works fine* (there are still some bugs open, but this is entirely something else).

Please add more details regarding the setup and what doesn’t function properly.

6.2 + 6.3 → were just introduced in [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13272|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13272|smart-link]  since 12.7.5

column1: Can't delete igf partition after uninstall of an app
column58:
Lets assume firefox is installed in /dev/igf2

Then following steps are enough to delete the partition:


{noformat}umount /services/firefox
/etc/igel/crypto/force_umount /dev/igf2
igeldelete 2{noformat}


But this will not work if the app was uninstalled previously, like:


{noformat}igelpkgctl uninstall firefox

umount /services/firefox
/etc/igel/crypto/force_umount /dev/igf2
igeldelete 2

# Resulting error
Device or resource busy{noformat}


On deleting following mounts will be added and _not_ removed.

** overlay on /tmp/check_rw_firefox*
** /dev/dm-4 on /services_rw/firefox*

I think theses mount should no longer exist after app was uninstalled.

column1: Check free space on EFI partition during DualBoot installation
column58:
During DualBoot installation of IGEL OS, the IGEL bootloader is extracted onto the EFI partition. Currently, there is no validation to ensure sufficient free space is available beforehand.

If the EFI partition does not have enough free space, the extraction may fail silently or lead to an incomplete installation.
column223:
* Before extracting the IGEL bootloader to the EFI partition, the installer checks the available free space.
* If there is insufficient free space:
** Log a clear message indicating the issue (e.g., “Not enough free space on EFI partition to install IGEL bootloader”).
** Abort or handle the installation gracefully.
* If there is sufficient space, continue installation as usual.
column244: Added validation of free space on the EFI partition during DualBoot installation. If insufficient space is detected, the process now logs a clear error message in C:\ProgramData\IGEL\logs\efi.log

column1: Existing IGEL_EFI_* bootloader variables block DualBoot entry creation
column58:
From Mattias Jacobsson:

_Hi all dual booters!_

_I have tested the rc7 (with rc6 image) and rc8 (with rc9 image) on my Lenovo P14s (AMD). Initially with a older (I believe) Win 11 installation and now recently with fresh installed Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 24H2, same behavior both times: Installation works fine (here I only add the base and leave cert, license and settings field empty), machine do a reboot, initialize IGEL partition etc. and finishes of with a second reboot. After that I see no trace of the dual boot on any restart of machine._ 

_Going to the boot menu on start I see two IGEL options (see below) but neither work for boot._

_Log files attached. Where can I start troubleshooting?_

*Problem:*

When using the DualBoot bootloader recovery (this is also done in installation phase), the process fails if there are already existing bootloader variables with the names {{IGEL_EFI_1}} or {{IGEL_EFI_2}}.

These variables seem to originate from a previous IGEL OS installation and remain in the system. Their presence prevents the creation of a new {{IGEL_EFI}} entry required for DualBoot.

*Proposed Solution:*
Update the recovery logic to check only for the exact variable name {{IGEL_EFI}}. Ignore variables with suffixes such as {{_1}}, {{_2}}, etc.
column244: Resolved an issue where existing bootloader variables (IGEL_EFI_1, IGEL_EFI_2) blocked DualBoot bootloader installation and recovery.

column1: Lenovo T14 Gen 6 internal microphone not working
column58: Our IT distributed Lenovo Thinkpad T14 Gen 6 (AMD based) but it turned out the internal microphone is not working. It turns out we are missing the kernel modules *snd-acp70* and *snd-sof-amd-acp70* which make the microphone working after they were added to the firmware. But up to now we did not even build the kernel module therefore we also need to change the kernel config.
column362:
18/Sep/25 9:04 AM;712020:2cd15539-aafc-4feb-b251-ca7080d9f64f;As we already have the devices out in the wild I created a solution which work with UMS file transfer and custom commands.

For this:

# Take the attached *fix-mic-acp70.zip* file and copy it to the UMS server and extract it there
# Copy the extracted *fix-mic-acp70.sh* file via UMS filetransfer to the the ThinClients (permissions as executable) */wfs* directory
# Add the command */wfs/fix-mic-acp70.sh* to *System → Firmware Customization → Custom Commands → Base*

After a reboot of the ThinClient the internal microphone should then start working. The script checks the hardware and the kernel so it can be rolled out on all hardware devices without harm. So simple speaking you can generate a UMS profile and assign it to every machine.

column1: igelpkg - check status of upload process before checking the result
column58:
Our TeamCity pipeline recently encountered issues successfully publishing apps.
From my quick analysis, I might have identified the issue:

Once the publisher finishes uploading the ipkg data, it performs an HTTP GET on {{/process/<id>/result}}, which blocks server-side until the temporary ipkg is moved to its final destination.  
The HTTP connection remains open until the server provides a response. This process might take a while, and I suspect that either Nginx or the Node.js runtime is hitting a connection timeout here.

We should poll the current status of {{/process/<id>}}, and once this is finished, perform a GET request on {{/process/<id>/result}}.

column1: Windows creates new Recovery Partition after major update, blocking merge of freed space
column58:
After a major Windows update, Windows  11 automatically creates a *new Recovery Partition*.

This causes an issue when the IGEL OS dual boot feature is later uninstalled:

* Windows reduces the size of its system partition to make space for the new Recovery Partition.
* The new Recovery Partition is then placed between the Windows partition and the IGEL OS partition.
* When uninstalling the IGEL OS dual boot feature, the freed disk space can no longer be merged back into the Windows partition because the Recovery Partition lies in between.

*Proposed Solution / Consideration:*

* Prevent Windows from creating a new Recovery Partition during major updates by disabling the Recovery Environment beforehand with: reagentc.exe /disable
* In testing, disabling the Recovery Environment prevented Windows from creating the new partition after the update.
column362: 05/Sep/25 9:11 AM;712020:669c6177-2627-4770-97b6-0c52d822f253;[~accountid:712020:1782088a-93ea-48e8-815b-0eb853137df8] Could we not move the recovery partition to the end of the hard disk after uninstalling IGEL OS and before increasing the size of the Windows main partition?
column363: 05/Sep/25 9:40 AM;712020:1782088a-93ea-48e8-815b-0eb853137df8;[~accountid:712020:669c6177-2627-4770-97b6-0c52d822f253] Unfortunately not. There’s no way to move partitions while Windows is running. You can only shrink or resize partitions, or create new ones in free space. So I think we should first handle this as a known issue with a workaround to disable the Windows recovery partition: reagentc.exe /disable

column1: kiosk-app: Printing pdf only prints toolbar
column58:
Currently printing in the igel-secure-kiosk app with a PDF loaded leads to an almost empty page with only the PDF.js toolbar showing at the top.

!pdf_print.png|width=16.666666666666664%,alt="pdf_print.png"!

*Steps to reproduce:*

* Configure a toolbar item with Print Action
* Open igel-secure-kiosk app
* Navigate to a PDF file in the browser window
* Click on the Print toolbar item and confirm the print dialog



*Current Workaround:*

Clicking the Print button in the PDF.js toolbar leads to a correctly printed PDF (PDF.js does some preprocessing when its own print button is clicked).

!pdf-print-buttons-20250903-095601.png|width=25%,alt="pdf-print-buttons-20250903-095601.png"!

!image-20250903-105009.png|width=1919,height=844,alt="image-20250903-105009.png"!



*Challenges:*

* The PDF.js viewer that automatically gets used when a PDF is opened in the webview is rendered in an {{<iframe>}}
* The origin of the {{<iframe>}} is {{'webkit-pdfs-viewer'}} while we operate in the {{'html'}} origin meaning we cannot inject JS to access contents of PDF.js (CORS prevents it)


*Possible Solutions:*

# Create a webkit extension and run it in the browser webview to be able to access the DOM and click the print button when the internal toolbar print action item is clicked
## Create webkit extension to manipulate DOM and allow access to it from the webview (So consumers like igel-secure-kiosk can interact with the extension)
## Override the default handler of the webkit {{print}} signal to be able to suppress the print dialog when the PDF.js javascript calls {{print()}}
## Load the extension in the external webview of igel-secure-kiosk
# Download the PDF/Blob to a file in the background (/tmp) and then print from that file without any user interaction
## Figure out how to download the PDF in all cases (File, Blob, Blob in Popup)
[https://webkitgtk.org/reference/webkit2gtk/2.39.6/method.WebView.save_to_file.html|https://webkitgtk.org/reference/webkit2gtk/2.39.6/method.WebView.save_to_file.html] useful ?
## Find a way to print that file in the background with the right print settings (best case use the GTK Print Settings)

This command is useful to find out which interface packets will go through: ip route get <destination ip>

The easiest way to determine the network interface type is to look at the output of “nmcli device”, because then Network Manager does it for you. The interesting physical types are ethernet, wifi, and gsm (=WWAN). You can probably ignore entries whose state is not “connected”. 

Other connected interfaces may be apart from lo (type loopback) various virtual devices on top of the physical ones, tun for VPN tunnels or macsec  or bridge or bond or team etc. Then in the case of multiple connected physical interfaces those virtual ones would have to be inspected in detail to find out which is used for AVD packets. A good guesss would be ethernet first, then wifi second, then gsm.

column1: IMH | unnecessary error message when creating new VM
column58:
When creating a new VM using virt-manager, an error message about permissions is displayed when no LVs are present in the imh VG.

This only happens for the “Create a new virtual machine” dialog in virt-manager, not when creating a new volume via the volume-manager dialog.

Workaround: Selecting “No” actually causes the VM to be created sucessfully.

column1: setup-assistant: wrong finish-page when skipping/canceling onboarding-attempt
column58:
When attempting to onboard with email-address, and reaching the external website, then abort the onboarding and proceed to the end of the setup-assistant-flow, you are stuck.

Reprod:

* in setup-assistant reach the OBS-page where you can enter an email-address
* enter mail and click ‘Continue' → external website opens up
* do +not+ proceed with onboarding, instead click ‘back’ or ‘skip’

* {color:#ff5630}*wrong*{color} information displayed:

“This device will now be prepared, which will take a short moment. It will reboot automatically once it is ready.”



I assume, the datacontext-values are not correct in this scenario.
Something about
igel::serialize::property(&Finish::connectingStage, "connectingStage"),

* backend starts loading the external webpage and switches view to external and when page-load-finished, backend replies with NoErrors
* frontend gets the NoErrors reply and starts {{ObsActionTypes.OpenOnboardingServiceClosed}}
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/state/obs/obs.effect.ts#29-31|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/state/obs/obs.effect.ts#29-31]

[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/state/finish/finish.reducer.ts#59|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/state/finish/finish.reducer.ts#59]

** the reply only indicates the opening of the external obs-website

[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/views/finish/finish.component.html#1|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/setup-assistant/browse/frontend/src/setup-assistant/views/finish/finish.component.html#1]

In the second workflow the vlist is forwarded from the device to UMS.

The empty vlist in the second case makes it impossible to define settings for the parameters in the WebApp because it does not know these. Also the UI description is empty in this case.



One thing which might explain this is that in the second case the device tells me after the installation of the app that I need a special license for using the app. But as the vlist is not updates one the app is loaded in UMS, configurations will never be possible, even after a licensing change.

01/Dec/25 8:35 AM;712020:53d5dd05-f070-44c9-a4d7-f230dae2a6ad;h3. Findings so far (from Ala and Andreas): 

* The issue does NOT occur on 12.7.x, only on 12.8.x 
* The issue happens on applying the display layout and you see the display gets refreshed (the display turns black then get back) if the layout is applied without that refresh the issue does not happen.
* On the front end side the html elements of the rectangles representing the displays (blue with id on them) are still having the draggable set as true and the rectangle is moved we receive the start drag and end drag events.
* On the other hand the parent rectangle (the one in gray) where the displays gets dragged on is no longer receiving dragged on or the droppedOn events when the displays are dragged around => might indicate that the html tree is broken.
* Issue also occurs when changing temporary mirror mode in normal display tray app
* problem also occurs when a very basic drag and drop demo is used inside the window (instead of our display layout surface)
* drag and drop demo does also not work in other tray apps like bluetooth after display layout was applied
* drag and drop demo does not work at all in new modern desktop UIs like start menu (appropriate handlers for drag and drop events seem to be amiss)
* also other demos like the ones from MDN are not working after display was applied
* igel-desktop.log has the same content before and after applying a layout
* setting other datacontexts like mouse input does not break anything

h3. 
Hypothesis and what has been tried so far:

* I have considered the fact that we might be breaking the front-end react state but it does not seem to be the case because even if we only send the state in the beginning and then stop sending the state from the backend the issue still happens. 
* Tried to reload the webview on display change still nothing, I have even tried to reset the AdvancedWindow every time I open it from the display window but still did not solve the issue => which means that the issue is not only in the AdvancedWindow state but maybe the whole system_tray
* The issue gets solved if we restart the igel_system_tray service which might be an indication that applying a new layout might require to restart the process (not sure about this).

h3. More ideas

* debug webkit2gtk , especially [DropTargetGtk3.cpp |https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/webkit2gtk/browse/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/API/gtk/DropTargetGtk3.cpp#70,77,87,94,99,254,261]and [DropTargetGtk4.cpp|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/webkit2gtk/browse/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/API/gtk/DropTargetGtk4.cpp#72,81,89,100,105,248,262,275] to check where the code is jumping out

09/Dec/25 8:47 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;more thoughts on this:

* when dragging a monitor inside the display-config-dialog, a new window is created (the little monitor-rectangle, which is dragged)
* this new window has other window-title “igel-system-tray”, simply because it is created out of the igel-system-tray process
* the new window is not the display-config-dialog itself, which has window-title “Display Configuration”
* the new window is detected by several classes within our mutter-plugin (“window-created” signal)
** WindowRaiser detects it, and decides that it does not want to get raised higher
** OpenWindowManager detects it, and decides to not add it to the list of open windows for the taskbar
** TrayContainer detects it: [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/tray-panel-port/TrayContainer.cpp#59,70-72|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/plugins/desktop-layer/tray-panel-port/TrayContainer.cpp#59,70-72]
*** {{detected a new window from a known external-tray-icon process}}
the known external-tray-icon process is the igel-sytem-tray process, detection works by matching same PID
*** TrayContainer clones the window-actor of this dragged little monitor-rectangle, moves it higher in the z-ordering and registers it in the InputManager
*** {{register events and insert cloned actor above inputGrabActor}}
*** the cloned actor gets input-events, which are handled in our InputManager
*** but no drag- or drop-events are registered in our InputManager, because there are no drag-events for a ClutterActor
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/mutter-plugin/InputManager.cpp#194-197|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-desktop/browse/backend/mutter-plugin/InputManager.cpp#194-197]
*** therefore, no drag-event is propagated further to the original window
**** this explains Ala’s previous comment: “the parent rectangle (the one in gray) where the displays gets dragged on is no longer receiving dragged on or the droppedOn events when the displays are dragged around”
**** this also explains Andrea’s test:
”drag and drop demo does not work at all in new modern desktop UIs like start menu (appropriate handlers for drag and drop events seem to be amiss)”
because for all the igel-desktop WPEwebkit UIs (like start-menu) we also have input-actors registered in the InputManager

column1: Unable to Parameterize UMS Server During IGEL OS VM Provisioning in Proxmox
column58:
When provisioning a new IGEL OS virtual machine in Proxmox and attempting to install the OS, the image initiates an automatic onboarding process to a preconfigured UMS server.

This automatic behavior acts as a blocker because it does not allow us to define or override the UMS server used for onboarding. As a result, we are unable to test onboarding to different environments or dynamically provisioned UMS instances.

Furthermore, if we try to *disable the automatic onboarding step* during testing (e.g. through automation using Robot Framework), the IGEL OS installation flow falls back to a *manual GUI installer*, requiring human interaction to proceed with setup steps (e.g. clicking through “Next” buttons and confirming actions).
This *breaks automation* completely and makes headless provisioning or continuous testing pipelines unfeasible.

*Expected behavior:*
IGEL OS image should allow the UMS server to be passed as a configurable parameter during provisioning (e.g. via kernel arg, config file, or Proxmox argument), and should allow fully headless installation without mandatory GUI interaction.

*Actual behavior:*

* UMS onboarding is hardcoded during initial boot/install.
* If disabled, installation falls back to GUI flow that requires manual input.

column1: Audio Tray App | UI "Input"/"Output" section disappear when using multiple headsets
column58:
When using multiple headsets with the new HP ProDesk 5 G1i, under specific circumstances the UI section “Input”/”Output” in the Audio tray app just disappears. 

h3. Environment

* Device Model: HP ProDesk 5 G1i, Intel N50 (CPU)
* USB headset: Poly Voyager Focus 2
* Headphone jack headset: any
* OSVersion: 12.7.2 and 12.8 (no issues in 12.7.1)

h3. Steps to reproduce

The issue can be seen by triggering a number of different combinations. One of such is:

* Plug in 2 headsets: one in the headphone jack (built-in) and one as USB
* Select input and output devices to be from the same headset. E.g. USB output and input
* Switch the input OR output to be from the other headset. E.g. built-in output and USB input
* Switch the input OR output to be from the same headset again. E.g. USB output and USB input
* The “Input” or “Output” section will disappear (depending on which was switched for.. if switching output then “Input” will disappear, and vice versa)

h3. Remarks

I also cross-checked this with the debug app “igel-audio-control” and there all devices are shown at all times. However - when the “Input”/”Output” section disappears in the tray UI, then the chosen input/output device is also *deselected* in the “igel-audio-control”. This indicates that there is something in the backend which has changed. I can then reselect an input/output device, and it shows up again in the Audio Tray UI again. Also, configuring the different combinations of input and outputs via “igel-audio-control” works fine.

*The issue occurs both with pipewire and pulseaudio.*

column1: Horizon sessionhandler logoff script fails to log off the user
column58:
h3. Steps to reproduce:

# configure a Horizon session with saved user credentials
# start the Horizon session and connect to the remote desktop
# start an application, e.g. calc
# run the logoff script in the user context: 
{noformat}/services/horizon/sessionhandler/logoff --igelsession <session name>{noformat}
# Expected behavior: the user is logged off from the remote session (usually this is a long enough process to be visible in the horizon window); when they connect again the application (e.g. calc) is no longer running
Observed behavior: the logging off is not visible; the horizon window just disappears; when the user connects to the session again, the application (calc) is still running

Reproduced in:

* base_system 12.7.1
* horizon 25.03

Most likely the versions don’t matter much

h3. Analysis:

the logoff script reads the user credentials from setupd and then sends an XML API POST request to the horizon broker in order to authenticate the user; if authentication is successful, the script proceeds to get the user-ID from the broker response and then uses more XML API POST requests to obtain the session-ID and send the logoff signal to the broker

in fact, the initial authentication request from the logoff script always fails, because the HTTP POST request doesn’t have the required JSESSIONID cookie

normally, when the Horizon client interacts with the Horizon broker, the first request is not an authentication request and instead a get-capabilities request. the broker responds with its supported capabilities and sets the JSESSIONID cookie. then a later authentication request has the correct cookie and succeeds

h3. Proposed solution:

add a non-authentication request to the logoff script, before the authentication request, to get the correct cookie

h3. Further improvement:

use the session object from the python requests library to automatically handle cookie updates, instead of doing it explicitly after every request

column362:
18/Jul/25 4:55 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;It’s no monitor-handling display-configuration problem.

The problem is: the igel-greeter brings up one big window for each monitor.

* on primary monitor the important window with the password-input-field
* on every other monitor a “empty” window, just with the background-image, it seems.

When multiple monitors are mirrored in a mirror-group, the greeter still brings up one window for each monitor.
Actually, I saw the same issue once on 12.7.1 with a mirror-group of 3 monitors.

Right now in our igel-desktop-code:

* greeter brings multiple windows, only one is the important one.
* the time-order, when these windows are coming in, seems to differ (-> sometimes it’s fine and we get the expected result)
* the igel-desktop window-detection sees one greeter-window, maybe first the important one with the password-input-field.
* the window-detection sees another greeter-window
** lifts the second incoming window higher, OVER the previously greeter-window with the password-field.
** the second greeter-window now covers the first one (FAIL)
** the second greeter-window just shows the background-image, nothing more.
* only, when monitors are mirrored, this is a problem, because the greeter-windows cover each other
* without mirror-group, no problem, because one greeter-window per monitor

I tried to detect, if one of many greeter-windows is on primary monitor, but while mirroring, every monitor is primary monitor. Does not help.

That’s it so far.

What I could think of:

* the one important greeter-window with the password-field needs another marking, to be able to distinguish it from other “blank” greeter windows
* ask Martin

but this does not help.

column367:
24/Jul/25 10:44 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;some more explanation:

mirroring the primary monitor results in multiple primary monitors.
The greeter tests each monitor if it is primary.
If yes, the greeter re-parents the one single login-mask-widget to the new window for the primary monitor.
With multiple primary monitors, the greeter detects the next primary, and re-parents the login-mask again to the new window.
The result:
The greeter creates a window for each primary monitor, but only one of them has the login-mask.
Then it CAN happen, the a window without login-mask covers the one window with the login-mask.

The solution:
Save the first found primary-monitor-rectangle
and for each other monitor, test if the next rectangle is equal to the primary-rectangle.
If yes, no need to create another new window, because the primary monitor already got a greeter-window.
This should result in only one greeter-window for the primary monitor.

This solution also works, when the primary monitor is in a mirror-group, and there is/are other monitor/s in the display-layout outside of the mirror-group.
The non-mirrored monitors still get the empty/blank window.

column1: scan_repos.py | Script gets stuck in endless While-loop due to expired CA certificate
column58:
h3. Summary

The script gets stuck in an endless While-loop due to a “continue” when it encounters an error. In this case, the issue was an unhandled SSLError due to the CA certificate being expired. The path to the CA certificate was hardcoded, and thus the newer certificate was never considered. 

h3. Task

Handle any potential errors and exit the program instead of continuing in an endless While-loop. Make it more robust by giving the path to the {{/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt}} which is a concatenation of all available CA certificates, so that we don’t run into any problems with a specific certificate being expired.

base system 12.7.1+1 or 12.6.1+1

# select Firefox as the default web browser
# open terminal as user
# check default application for {{x-scheme-handler/https}}
{{xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/https}}
Expected output: {{firefox.desktop}}
Observed output: {{chromium-browser.desktop}}

h4. (a more relevant way to reproduce in addition to the above)

# install horizon (latest version)
# create a horizon session with ServerURL {{view.tulsatech.edu}} (_real customer, don’t ddos unnecessarily, I would use a test server if I had access to one with SSO authentication configure_)
# run the horizon session and double-click the server icon
Expected behavior: the SSO login page opens in Firefox
Observed behavior: the SSO login page opens in Chromium

h3. Analysis

Changing the default web browser in the config updates{{ /userhome/.config/mimeapps.list}}. In particular, three mime types are updated:

{noformat}application/x-extension/html=firefox.desktop
application/xhtml+xml=firefox.desktop
text/html=firefox.desktop{noformat}

It looks like under certain circumstances (e.g. with Horizon Client redirecting to an SSO login page), the relevant mimetype (or rather scheme) is x-scheme-handler=

The default app for this scheme is not defined in {{.config/mimetapps.list}}, but it is defined in {{/userhome/.local/share/applications/mimeapps.list}} in the following way:

{noformat}x-scheme-handler/http=chromium-browser.desktop;firefox.desktop;igel-minibrowser.desktop
x-scheme-handler/https=chromium-browser.desktop;firefox.desktop;igel-minibrowser.desktop{noformat}

The solution could be to run 

{noformat}xdg-mime default <selected default browser> x-scheme-handler/http
xdg-mime default <selected default browser> x-scheme-handler/https{noformat}

That would update {{.config/mimeapps.list}}, which takes priority over {{.local/share/applications/mimeapps.list}}

P.S. And why does{{ .local/share/applications/mimeapps.list }}have the {{[Added Associations]}} section that duplicates the {{[Default Applications]}} section? There are warnings in the {{journalctl}} about this and {{[Default Applications]}} takes precedence anyway, so the duplicate entries in {{[Added Associations]}} seem irrelevant.

h3. Summary

*igel-minibrowser* fails to start when *LD_LIBRARY_PATH* is defined in the environment

h3. Significance

When a third-party script or binary opens a URL, the default browser is invoked, based on the _https_ schema configuration in *mimeapps.list*

If no other (firefox, chromium, etc.) browsers are installed, *igel-minibrowser* is the default browser.

If the third-party script/binary accessing the URL happens to define *LD_LIBRARY_PATH*, *igel-minibrowser* fails immediately with the error:

{{/usr/bin/igel-minibrowser: symbol lookup error: /usr/bin/igel-minibrowser: undefined symbol: _ZN4Glib7ustringaSEOS0_}}

*Example*: Omnissa Horizon Client 24.06, 25.03 redirects to a URL for SSO authentication. When *igel-minibrowser* is the default web browser, login window fails to open and makes authentication impossible.

h3. Steps to reproduce

base-system 12.7.1, 12.6.1+1

# create a bash script, e.g. *run-minibrowser.sh*:
{noformat}LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/omnissa:
/usr/bin/igel-minibrowser $@{noformat}
# run the script

{{run-minibrowser.sh --url https://google.com}}

*Expected result*: igel-minibrowser window opens and displays Google's web page

*Observed result*: igel-minibrowser window doesn't open

column1: ZoomVDI Smart Virtual Backgrounds parameter differs from the underlying ZoomVDI behavior
column58:
h3. Summary

# The Support Smart Virtual Background parameter in IGEL config for ZoomVDI has 3 values: off | auto | always

ZoomVDI itself only has two modes: auto and always.

# The implementation of the “auto” option in IGEL app is different then the auto mode in ZoomVDI and also redundant.

h3. Steps to reproduce

Hardware: Standard IGEL UD7 device.

IgelOS: 12.7.1 (or any other)

ZoomVDI: 12.4.10 (or any other)

CWA | RDP | AVD | Horizon - latest versoin

# Set Support Smart Virtual Backgrounds to Off in the IGEL config for ZoomVDI.
# Connect to a VDI session (cwa, rdp, avd, horizon)
# Start Zoom VDI Workspace and sing in.
# Open Setting > Virtual Backgrounds (not the exact path)
# Set the “Green Screen” option to Off.

*Expected result:* virtual backgrounds and/or blur cannot be selected.

*Observed result:* virtual backgrounds and blur can be selected.

h3. Why this is important

Easily misleads the user regarding the actual behavior of the presented options.

*Off* - user could think that this turns off support for smart virtual backgrounds. In fact ZoomVDI would still support smart virtual backgrounds if it determines the hardware/software to be supported

*Auto* - user could think that this simply lets ZoomVDI decide whether smart virtual backgrounds should be supported. In fact, Igel uses its own logic (which is probably different from Zoom's logic) and _may_ force support for a device that ZoomVDI itself would consider unsupported.

h3. Details

h4. Behavior of “Off”

The default behavior of ZoomVDI is to detect support for smart virtual backgrounds automatically (link).

Setting SMARTVB=1 in ZoomMedia.ini forces support for smart virtual backgrounds on all devices. (link)

From tests, by default the parameter is not set at all. A ZoomVDI support article claims that the default behavior matches smartvb=0. ([https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065298|https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065298|smart-link] )

There is no statement in any of the ZoomVDI support articles, that setting smartvb=0 turns off the support for smart virtual backgrounds on supported devices. There is only a claim that setting smartvb=1 forces support for smart virtual backgrounds on unsupported devices. (see bottom section here [https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065893|https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065893|smart-link] )

In tests, when SMARTVB=0 (directly in ZoomMedia.ini, or through settings Support Smart Virtual Backgrounds to Off in the config) smart virtual backgrounds are still available in ZoomVDI.

h4. Behavior of “Auto”

ZoomVDI support articles don't provide details on how exactly ZoomVDI detects supported configuration. There is a list of CPU requirements in terms of generations, models, frequencies, and CPU cores ([https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065893|https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0065893|smart-link] ). 

In our code, “auto” checks for the avx2 flag in the cpu features and sets SMARTVB=0 if the flag is absent, and SMARTVB=1 if the flag is present.

In tests, I can suppress the avx2 flag in grub boot options. This makes the “auto” option to set SMARTVB=0. Smart virtual backgrounds are still available in ZoomVDI on my test device.

Since ZoomVDI autodetection cannot be turned off, there is no need for our code to try to replicate it. The check for avx2 feature is unnecessary.

h3. Suggested modifications

Present only two options in the config: *auto* | *always*

*Auto* should set *SMARTVB=0*

*Always* should set *SMARTVB=1*

No additional logic to “detect” supported devices from our side is required.

After=igel-desktop-final.target
After=igel-notify-ui.service

column1: igel-greeter | “Too many failed unlock attempts." when hotplugging docking station
column58:
When hotplugging the docking station during the Login screen, when it is displayed on an external monitor, causes the error “Too many failed unlock attempts. Wait to try unlock again…” when the Login screen shifts to the internal display. This happens even though no unlock attempts were made. 

I have given the exact laptop I used, but I’m not sure if this is hardware related.

h3. Environment

* Device Model: Lenovo ThinkPad L14 Gen4 (AMD) + Lenovo ThinkPad Universal USB-C Dock
* OSVersion: 12.7.1 (not happening on 12.6 nor 12.8)
* State: Managed

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Setup login for local user (Security → Login → Local User)
* Plug in docking station with 2 external displays
* Enable all displays in Display Tray app and make an external display the primary screen
* Verify that locking the desktop results in the login screen being on the external screen
* Hotplug the docking station while lockedc

h3. Current Behaviour

* When hotplugging the docking screen, the Login screen shifts from the external display to the internal (expected), but after a brief moment is reloaded and then shows the message “Too many failed unlock attempts. Wait to try unlock again…“, even though no unlock attempts have been made. 

h3. Expected Behaviour

* The Login screen should be functional immediately and not display any error messages.
column362: 10/Jul/25 2:05 PM;712020:ab44469e-3f45-431f-ae7c-a2e231d764c6;While investigating the problem, I also found another bug. The number of times an invalid authentication is set by the registry {{auth.login.lockout_threshold}}, but due to the way this mechanism was coded the real number of wrong authentication that the user is allowed to do before locking the system will always be lockout_threshold - 1.

column364: 28/Jul/25 10:50 AM;712020:ab44469e-3f45-431f-ae7c-a2e231d764c6;[~accountid:712020:669c6177-2627-4770-97b6-0c52d822f253] The previous comment was made while I was investigating the problem. column1: CWA: faulty StoreCache configuration process
column58:
When cwaconfig wants to configure StoreCache.ctx too ealy (after reboot) the config service runs into a timeout. This is because it trys to use storebrowse command, which itself wants to have AutManD and ServiceRecordD, which are not present at that time. They will be started but not with our conditions → this breaks the CWA workflow 

Fix: 
enabling the storecache config only when selfservice session is triggered (because storefront doesnt need it) and not automatically when the config service is started at boot.

column1: LAN tray app does not handle restrictions on Ethernet device activation correctly
column58:
Ethernet interfaces for which there is no instance of network.interfaces.ethernet.device% may only be activated if their index (= line numer in /config/net/en-interfaces starting from 1) is less than or equal to $(numinstances network.interfaces.ethernet.device%)+$(get network.global.eth_enable_supernumerary). I.e. if eth_enable_supernumerary is 0 then only interfaces for which there is an instance of network.interfaces.ethernet.device% shall be configurable. The tray app so far does not respect eth_enable_supernumerary.

Ethernet interfaces for which there is an instance of network.interfaces.ethernet.device% may only be configured if the corresponding network.interfaces.ethernet.deviceX.active is true. If this is false the LAN tray app shows a DISCONNECT button for an unconfigured interface and then shows an error “The ethernet device is not connected. Cannot disconnect“ and still shows a disconnect button. So the user gets the impression that under certain circumstances the interface could be connected.

Context: The customer for whom we did [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11115|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11115|smart-link] wants to make sure that only one Network interface is active at a time.

column1: Laptop Touchpad - Right click not working
column58:
Since 12.8 the right click on touchpad doesn’t work.

h3. Investigation

* Right-click method has been changed from buttonarea to clickfinger
* Tapping is disabled at boot and after udevadm trigger, despite being enabled in the TC setup
* Scroll method is two-finger at boot and after udevadm trigger, despite being set to right edge in TC setup
* Using “xinput watch-props <dev>” I can see that 

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Use 12.8 on any laptop with touchpad
* At boot, tapping is disabled, scroll methos is two-finger despite having different settings in TC setup
* Using “xinput watch-props <dev>” we can see that these properties are being set correctly, but then overwritten again
* Restarting the service which initially configures the settings makes it work as expected: “su user; systemctl --user restart igel-synclient-config”
* Calling “udevadm trigger” shows the faulty behavior again, and we can see using xinput that the properties are being reset again

17/Nov/25 11:22 AM;712020:1d4a3d11-82d3-4645-99a7-6929168e11cc;Initial investigation:

* For 12.8, the xinput behavior Click Method Enabled has switched from buttonarea to clickfinger. 
* For 12.8, the service which initially sets the xinput values to match the tc setup (especially two finger scroll, and tapping enabled) does not seem to work properly. The service “igel-synclient-config” runs successfully, but somehow these values get reset later.
* The above point means that tapping is disabled at boot (even though setup says enabled) and that scrolling is two finger (even though setup says disabled). Changing any of the other touchpad settings runs the script again (via node_action). Calling the script manually or restarting the service also has the same effect.
* A lot of settings in the setup don’t do anything when using the libinput driver. E.g. the Actions for buttonareas.
* evdev driver does not work at all.
* Right click is a bit inconsistent, even when using the buttonarea, this only applies to actual clicks. When tapping, only a two-finger tap produces a right click (maybe this is as designed though?).

* “xinput watch-props 9” shows that the tapping and scroll behavior is being correctly set, however it’s being overwritten towards the end again.
* I haven’t found anything yet which indicates who is doing this resetting.
* If the service is restarted and everything works as expected, a “udevadm trigger” call forces it to not work again.
* 12.7 works fine, and it’s not clear why a udevadm trigger call here is not breaking things.
* Adding a service restart/calling the script inside of a udevadm rule (for example similar to the one disabling the touchpad), is unfortunately not working… Otherwise this could have been a temporary fix until the root cause is found.

* I can see with dconf-editor that some of the settings for touchpad are incorrect (e.g. Tapping is disabled, even though the TC setup says it should be enabled). However, I see this also in 12.7 where everything works fine.
column376:

* mutter uses settings from dconf/gsettings which overwrite the settings we set directly using xinput
* In the long run, we want to rethink touchpad handling in general, but for now, we need to make sure behavior is as before. 
* TODO: test if it’s possible to replace the xinput calls in igel-synclient-config with gsettings calls for the specific touchpad settings which would otherwise be overwritten.

column1: AVD | MS-Teams screen share video is showing wrong/displaced colors
column58:
When receiving a screen share video, our client sometimes shows wrong and displaced colors!

Seems to be a Intel device typ issue, prospect Continental has FUTRO S740 and Optiplex 3000, both with Intel CPUS, i saw the issue on S740 and HP T550, both also with Intel CPU.
On the UD3 i cannot see the issue which uses a AMD CPU.
It is also aspect ratio related, sharing from a Ultra Wide Screen with e.g. 3860x1600 does not show the issue, sharing from 1920x1080 or 2560x1440 shows the issue.

How to reproduce:

# Grab a Intel Based device like the mentioned above
# Install Igel OS 12.7.0 and AVD 1.3.2 to it
# Login to a AVD Session, i used AVD from Igel@Igel
# Get a call from a device with Full HD aspect ratio (e.g. i used my Windows Laptop with Full HD with another teams account)

column1: WiFi SIID with "space" as first character - No connection established

IGEL OS failed to establish connection, no sign of root cause could be found in journal.

# Create WiFI hotspot on Android phone
# Choose SIID name with space as first character, e.g. “ MyHotspot”

Mitigations attempts:

* Change to WPA2 → Failed
* Remove password check completly → Failed
* Rename from “ MyHotspot” to “MyHotspot” → Success



Additional info: Non-IGEL devices can connect to the hotspot even with space as first character of the SIID.

column1: Setupd: node_action in session instance template executed during boot

{noformat}<sessions>

       </name_localized>
       <icon>

* check the service with journalctl

column1: Citrix - Ignore X Errors
column58:
While starting resources in Citrix Workspace App (CWA), X Window errors occasionally appear, especially when related to graphical windows. Based on research and testing, the following common causes and findings have been identified.

# *Compatibility Issues:*
#* Errors have been frequently observed when applications run on Wayland but may function correctly when running under X11 (also known as Xorg).
# *Memory Limitations:*
#* Running out of available memory on the server, particularly when reconnecting to a session with higher color depth, can lead to connection failures. Though seemingly straightforward, multiple factors contribute to this issue.

h4. Recommended Workaround:

Adjusting the following parameter in {{~/.ICAClient/wfclient.ini}} can significantly reduce these errors:

{{IgnoreXErrors=20.0/3, 2.0/6, 2.0/3}}

h3. Observations from Testing:

* *Without Setting* {{IgnoreXErrors}}*:*
** Error message "Bad X Request 2.0 caused error" appears both in the ICAClient.log and as a visible error window on the desktop.
** {{citrix-wfica: error on dialog title:(null) body:The X Request 20.0 caused error: "3: BadWindow (invalid Window parameter)".}}
* *With* {{IgnoreXErrors=20.0/3, 2.0/6}} *Set:*
** The mentioned error no longer appears in ICAClient.log or as a pop-up.
** Applications that previously exhibited uncertainty due to this error now launch properly.

h3. Should we set this value default? 

* This parameter primarily acts as a suppression mechanism rather than a fix for the underlying issue. It only ignores specific X Window System errors, preventing their corresponding error message boxes from appearing.
* While this reduces visible disruptions and significantly enhances performance by enabling successful reconnection to multiple applications without errors, it may also conceal potential underlying issues since it doesn’t show the errors in ICAClient.log and as a pop-up.

h3. Should we Recommend this setting for Reconnect feature users?:

Yes, this parameter should definitely be a recommendation, even if the problem does not originate from this function and has no direct influence, but this setting significantly improves performance by restoring the connection to maximum applications without an error occurring.
column244:
When a user attempts to launch a resource, launch may fail, resulting in specific X errors, and these errors can be ignored by entering them in the following registry key. Following values are set to default. 

| Registry |`app.cwa.wfclient.thinwire30.ignorexerrors`|
| Value | *2.0/6, 2.0/3* (default) |

Note: This parameter is primarily used as a suppression mechanism and not to resolve the underlying problem. It only ignores certain X Window system errors and prevents the corresponding error messages from being displayed.

04/Jun/25 10:56 AM;712020:c2f113c7-926b-43c8-9951-8fd54c1ca916;The *IgnoreXErrors* parameter serves as a valuable workaround for certain X Window System errors, most notably BadWindow (2.0/3, or 20/3), BadDrawable (55.0/9) and BadGC (60.0/13). Its main benefit is to suppress annoying error messages and allow sessions to continue, improving the immediate user experience in environments where direct resolution of underlying graphical issues is not immediately possible. However, ignoring these errors does not resolve the root cause of the problem, as the error is not logged when ignored. 

X Window System errors are typically reported with a structured format that pinpoint the exact failure: 

*X Request Major.Minor caused error: "Error_Code: Error_Name (Error_Description)"*

Here are some of the examples of these errors 

||IgnoreXErrors Parameter||X Error Name||Description||Context in Citrix||
|55.0/9|BadDrawable|Invalid Pixmap or Window parameter in a drawing operation.|Common in seamless application mode on Linux thin clients, often due to timing or window management issues.|
|60.0/13|BadGC|Invalid Graphics Context (GC) parameter used for drawing operations.|Common in seamless application mode on Linux thin clients, related to graphical state management.|
|2.0/3
or
20.0/3|BadWindow|Operation attempted on a non-existent, invalid, or destroyed window.|Can occur with window creation/destruction timing, or Wayland compatibility issues.|
|2.0/6|BadAlloc|Insufficient resources (e.g., memory, graphics buffers) for the requested operation.|Indicates client-side resource exhaustion; often due to inadequate hardware or X server limits.|

column1: KML: running handle_crypt via pkexec only works via SSH
column58:
Opening an encrypted LV using handle_crypt and pkexec only works when using SSH.

KML keys are stored in kernel keyrings which have traditionally been associated to the session. There have been problems with this in the past, this particular issue popped up after we switched to using pkexec in IMH to start the image upload UI and virt-manager.

It has been fixed via [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-955|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-955]
column244:
Changes to the KML affect anything related to encryption and key storage. Things to be tested explicitly:
* New device setup via OSC (without migrating settings)
* Device encryption via PIN, TPM PCR, TPM PIN, TPM PCR+PIN
* Generic key storage (e.g. store a website password in Chromium, log off the protected web site, close Chromium, start it again and verify it is able to fill in the user name/password)

09/May/25 5:38 PM;712020:489d1d34-dd68-46fd-9375-d253d120b022;[~accountid:712020:391f9e97-2260-49b8-8337-8824d0196357] This is normal behavior - logging out of one application does not terminate the session in another. This has been the standard behavior always.

AppPortal seems to work around this by not keeping users logged in when they refresh the page - if you log in to AppPortal and refresh the page, the Login button is there instead of your name. If you click it you’re instantly logged in, because you didn’t click Logout manually.

ServiceNow does not do this, and never did - unless you logout manually, or your tokens expire, you remain logged in.

The profile app operates on a similar basis as ServiceNow in that particular aspect. 



Note - there is a way to instantly terminate all user sessions, and this is respected by the profile application - this action however is an administrative action, and is not a part of a regular logout flow.

To summarize - this is expected behavior, and cannot be changed at this time.

column1: Lenovo P3 Tiny | Display Tray app fails with "Failed to apply display settings"
column58:
h3. Summary

While working on two other tickets [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11540|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11540|smart-link] and [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11541|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11541|smart-link] I discovered another issue. 

When using the Display Tray app to configure the displays, there is sometimes the error “Failed to apply display settings” and after that only one screen works. This always happens when attempting a configuration where the displays are vertical in some way (even if just one display is on top of the other, i.e. otherwise completely horizontal), but it sometimes also happens when trying to activate screens which have been inactivated from a previous failure. 

The drm seems to work fine, as {{get_drm connectors}} shows all available displays, even if the Display Tray configuration fails to configure them.

In the logs I can find this.

h3. Environment

* Device Model: Lenovo ThinkStation P3 Tiny

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Start the device with 2+ Mini-DP and 1 HDMI displays

column1: IGEL Smartcard cannot be written in 11.10.150 or newer
column58:
With OS 11.10.150 it is no longer possible to write new IGEL Smartcards. It is still possible to read Smartcards that are written with older versions.

Technically, the Gtk GUI application /usr/bin/scardgui, running as user user, is used to select sessions defined in setup. To write the settings to the smartcard, the application uses the valuelist command of setupd, which now is restricted to root.

Idea for re-implementation:

Write a socket activated system service which receives name, password and session list from {{scardgui}}. The service must retrieve the session settings from setupd (via valuelist), build the setup.ini to write to the card and call the tool {{personalize}} to write the card.

The tool personalize should be able to read the setup.ini from stdin, to avoid writing it to the file system.

column1: igel-desktop: allow disabling hotkeys: prevent "open start menu" when taskbar deactivated
column58:
When a hotkey for “open startmenu” is configured, but “use taskbar” in UI > Desktop > Taskbar is disabled, then the hotkey should not open the start menu.

Remark: OS 12.7 brings just an error message.


Another non-disabled hotkey issue:

* have terminal window open
* lock the screen, greeter come up, covers everything, other windows gets minimized (desktop-peek is triggered when greeter appears)
* press ALT+Tab
* the previously opened terminal window gets focus ({color:#ff5630}*FAIL*{color}).
It stays hidden, but you can see a changing mouse cursor when moving over the position where the terminal window should be, and keyboard events passed to the terminal, not to the greeter.

Such hotkeys should be disabled, when lockscreen is active. {{WindowRaiser.cpp}} calls {{factory.get<IKeyHandler>()->disableHotkeys();}},
which is not respected everywhere in {{KeyHandler.cpp}}



*task*

* do not trigger this special hotkey (like “open-start-menu”) when taskbar is disabled
** we know this certain hotkey-entry in KeyHandler (hopefully)
** in the callback behind this hotkey, check on the setup-param, if the taskbar is disabled, and if yes, do nothing.
*** there are multiple setup-param to disabled the taskbar, when in desktop, in lockscreen, or in login-screen,
but when greeter is active, hotkeys should be disabled anyway
* do not trigger all hotkeys when in login / screenlock 
** check if hotkeys are disabled when greeter active
** IKeyHandler->disableHotkeys() is called when greeter gets active.
should work, re-test
*** KeyHandler changed a lot since {{disableHotkeys}} got introduced. The new parts do not respect, if hotkeys should be disabled or not. Needs fixing.

16/Feb/26 10:58 AM;712020:71f2a6a6-cb1e-452c-8cb8-739c420ef441;Update: After taking a deeper look into this issue and it mostly turns out to be about current architecture design and it could be happening in all of our current environments:

problem statement: concurrent fails moving files from temp to final location while uploading. Size of the file is irrelevant. Its observed while uploading  huge files like base OS and few apps with Size in KB’s.

Recommended Solution: its observed that we are using two Azure file shares one for files_temp and one for final location post upload which causing this issue. we can use one Azure file share with two different paths within same PVC which avoids these errors. but this will be tested first in lower environments and then be implemented.

Other Workaround with current solution: it could be the Storage class is injected by Azure CSI drivers with default mount options “Soft” and “ retrans=1” which could be causing these errors which can be overridden explicitly by editing storage class by setting them to “hard“ and “retrans=5”. 

we would be trying these in couple of days and update ticket accordingly.

column1: rmagent has to return exit code of aborted commands
column58:
The rmagent aborts all running commands (with pthread_cancel) on a disconnect but no exit status is returned to the caller. In case of a local command this causes the caller waiting forever for an exit status.

To remedy this issue the rmagent must return the exit (error) status to the caller in case of a local command.

column1: Cyclic dependencie between igelmaker and igel-pxe-initrd
column58:
In case of an update of the kernel an update of igel-pxe-initrd is also required, as it includes a copy of the kernel.
But igel-pxe-initrd will use stable/os12 of igelmaker to update to the latest kernel version. And in the current setup igelmaker will fail when building osc as it detects the different kernel versions. This means a new kernel will not end up in stable/os12 and with that an update of igel-pxe-initrd is also not possible.

09/May/25 9:21 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;After I looked into the logs, I see some possibilities..

Our {{open-window-manager}} knows about the {{lightdm-igel-greeter}} window, by receiving {{MetaWorkspace::window-added}} signal.

But our {{WindowRaiser}} does not handle the {{lightdm-igel-greeter}} window.
Two possible options:

* {{WindowRaiser}} does not get notified about this greeter-window by {{MetaDisplay::window-created}} signal and does not know this window at all
* {{WindowRaiser}} gets notified, but {{WindowRaiser::windowHasLockRaiseProperty}} returns {{false}} without logging (unfortunately) and this window gets not handled further

I will add more logging at least.

12/May/25 12:07 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;from the new logs:

{quote}[2025-05-09 10:30:00.468 UTC] [139739953593088] [Debug] [Igel-Desktop][WindowRaiser] [onWindowCreated]: window does not want to be raised higher. lightdm-igel-greeter{quote}

FAIL. Seems like the greeter-window does not (yet?) have the necessary property set.
Our code tests on
{{#define IGELScreenlockAtomName "igel-screenlock-layer-atom"}}
defined in libXigelscreenlock

Probably, our mutter-plugin code tests the new window too early, when it is not yet fully through the libXigelscreenlock-extension.
something like this. timing problem.
I behaves different on Proxmox VM or vSphere VM.
I thought about connecting to some signal or xEvent, to get notified, when the properties of a xWindow changes, but this seems to be quite hard.

At least to have the panel in correct state, a bullet-proof solution could be, to just test for the window-title “lightdm-igel-greeter”.
Then, we certainly recognize the greeter-window and can act accordingly.
This would be a very easy fix for this problem.
Same approach already done with “setup-assistant”.

But for any other window (like our notifications, or igel-system-tray-windows), it could happen, that this window does not yet have the property set, and then is not detected to be raised higher in the z-ordering.

I also add more debug logging regarding this igel-internal xWindow property, if a window has it or not.

column1: igel-desktop: multiple tray apps open at the same time
column58:
*reproduction*

* open time-date tray
* click on system-tray icon like wifi
* => both are displayed (FAIL)



The same is true for igel-system-tray with notification-center, or start-menu and system-tray / notification-center.

Desired behavior: Only one of start-menu, notification-center, system-tray, igel-desktop-tray can be opened at the same time.



*tasks*

* find out, why igel-system-tray and igel-notify-ui do no longer respect each other
** they do in 12.7 → notify-ui-panel and any system-tray-window cannot be open at same time
** this is solved by improved focus-handling (/)
* igel-desktop must be informed when notification-center or igel-system-tray is clicked
No, This is solved by improved focus-handling (/)
* a notification overlaps an internal igel-desktop tray-app (!)
Both open at the same time, the notification covers the tray-app. 
Not handled in this ticket, new ticket [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12959|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12959|smart-link] 
Idea: two events for both directions to inform backend/fronend about opened apps / notifications / tray apps (x)
** inform igel-desktop frontend when a notification pops up, not handled in this ticket (x)
New ticket, because the workload on this ticket already was massive.
** closing the language-keyboard-layout-tray-app on click on button “Change Language” is no longer necessary,
because the triggered node_action notification about terminating user-session will inform igel-desktop frontend (the language tray-app) with the new event.
Tray-app will be informed by the new event and should close.
** solution between igel-system-tray and igel-notify-ui:
*** igel-system-tray provides dbus information if a tray-window is open
*** igel-notify-ui checks these dbus information and moves a notification away, repositioning next to the open tray-window
** analyze this in new ticket [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12959|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-12959|smart-link]

04/Nov/25 11:06 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;regarding simultaneous open external tray and internal tray:

Direction:

* internal tray open -> click on external tray icon (/)
** working fine after adding {{if (auto_ungrab) ungrab_focus()}} in the input-event-handler for {{InputManager::on_button_event_external}}
see commit on this ticket.
** when internal tray is open, out big {{input_grab_actor}} is reactive and the desktop-layer-webview has the focus
** with {{ungrab_focus}} , we remove focus from the layer-webview and the internal tray closes automatically
** then the mouse-click-event gets propagated to the external-tray-widget and the external tray window opens
* external tray window open → click on internal tray icon
** notify-ui-panel-window open → click on internal tray icon (/)
working fine, the desktop-layer-webview gets focus on mouse-click and the notify-ui-panel-window gets focus-out event and hides automatically.
** igel-system-tray window open → click on internal tray icon (a11y for example) (!)
Not working because igel-system-tray WindowManager ignores focus-events, if they are keyboard-grab/ungrab events, see
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/browse/backend/src/WindowManager.cpp#73-93|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/browse/backend/src/WindowManager.cpp#73-93]

Maybe we have to go with the idea in the ticket-description: inter-process-communication

We do not want to close igel-system-tray window when we click on empty taskbar-area (between open-window-list and tray-area).

Yes, they do.
The event-filtering in the igel-system-tray ignores the focus-out by keyboard-grab

* audio-tray-window stays open if FN-keys volume-up/down pressed (/)
* any igel-system-tray window stays open when click on our new webview-UI (internal-trays, start-menu-button) (x)

column374:
06/Nov/25 5:23 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;Found a solution in igel-system-tray event-filter:

* {{XIEnterEvent}} has also field ‘detail’, which can be tested
* the audio FN keys produce events with detail = {{XINotifyAncestor}} or {{XINotifyVirtual}}
* an input grab in out InputManager produces event with detail = {{XINotifyNonlinear}} or {{XINotifyNonlinearVirtual}}
* so more if-cases in the event-filter of igel-system-tray base-window should solve this issue
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/browse/backend/src/WindowManager.cpp#73-93|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/browse/backend/src/WindowManager.cpp#73-93]

found this by using {{xev}}, which is available in the base_system [https://linux.die.net/man/1/xev|https://linux.die.net/man/1/xev]

column1: A shared object can't be loaded from a data partition of an app
column58:
As the data partition is mounted by default with the noexec flag, no shared objects saved on a such partition can’t be loaded by Linux dynamic linker, which requires the exec flag on the filesystem holding the shared object. This is the primary cause why the Widevine DRM plugin doesn’t work in any web browser app.

*Workaround*: Remount the corresponding data partition with exec flag during boot at a possible early stage.

(Eg mount -o remount,rw,nosuid,nodev,noatime,compress=zstd:6,space_cache=v2,subvolid=5,subvol=/,exec /services_rw/edge)

*Possible Solution:* Make this flag configurable at the runtime, so the potential customer doesn’t need a such custom command.

column1: FN+F11 does not generate an acpi event anymore (Lenovo ThinkPads)
column58:
Function key for maximizing a window (CTRL+FN+F11) on Lenovo ThinkPad L14 Gen 5 (AMD) no longer works in 12.7 since the key press for FN+F11 no longer produces an ACPI event. There is also an error message in the journal:

{{kernel: thinkpad_acpi: unhandled HKEY 0x1320}}

However, this error message also occurs with 12.6.1, where the function key works as expected since it is still producing an ACPI event.

*Update*: I see the same issue with Ubuntu 24.10 which uses kernel version 6.11.

h3. Environment

* Device Model: Lenovo ThinkPad L14 Gen 5 (AMD) (IGEL-0934)
* OSVersion: base_system-12.7.0+nightly.20250327.DEV
* State: Unmanaged

h3. Steps to Reproduce

Press CTRL+FN+F11 and nothing happens. Check with acpi_listen and see no event for {{ibm/hotkey LEN0268:00 00000080 00001320}}. Check journalctl -f for error. 

h3. Expected Behavior

Generated ACPI event: {{ibm/hotkey LEN0268:00 00000080 00001320}} as well as CTRL+FN+F11 should maximize the current window.

column1: Failed invoking of the upgrade to OS12 executed by local command on device
column58:
As it was never intended to be executed in that way, the execution of the upgrade process initiated by a command on device was never tested. So it is impossible to trigger upgrade to OS12 just by execution of  {{/usr/share/pyshared/igel/upgrade.py}} on device side since 11.10.210, as the direct execution of the command leads to a wrong usage of the  {{/usr/share/pyshared/igel/upgrade.py}}. Because since 11.10.210 the generic command from the UMS involves more than one step, so the rmagent automatically gets the authorization token from the UMS, needed by the script for registering in OS12 remote management.

This can be easily fixed but it will require a new firmware.

column1: GenericForms: python-igelnotify - two dialogs in parallel (finalized now)
column58:
At my login dialog I want to give a user a hint, that he has to supply a password. I’d prefer to do this as an overlay to the current dialog to show there is no ongoing with the main login dialog.

I’d provided another GenericForm “Please supply a password” with a button only and I plan to display that for 5 sec but the time should shortened if user clicks to “Ok” Button. Timeout implementation is to be done…

Currently, before I added a lock mechanism with hint_submitted, the script run endless: The ok to the hint GenericForm is transferred to the main login dialog too: That login_on_submit() states no password set and calls the hint again.

There are two cases visible with the attached source, I made it visible by adding a lock mechanism. Start LoginWindow.py as documented below and press ENTER to close the input without adding any data. Due to missing password a hint-dialog is presented:

# Press TAB (for focus to “Ok”) and ENTER (for “Ok”) hint_on_submit() and login_on_submit() are called directly afterwards.
# Click on “Ok” releases hint_on_submit() only, but TAB (for focus change from “Cancel” to “Ok”) and ENTER (for “Ok”) releases login_on_submit() twice.

It looks that mouse click on “Ok” is handled differently than ENTER.

There are some more issues:

a) As documented above, strangely “Cancel” has the focus when switching back from hint-dialog to login-dialog.

b) The hint-dialog, a simple one with one primary button only, lacks the focus for the button on show(). Sometimes I can’t give the button a focus by pressing TAB don’t matter if I click into the dialog.

c) For proper dialog handling it’s required to set the focus to a specific field. I didn’t found that in the docu. Please add this feature as soon as possible.

d) On login-dialog there is a hidden tab position: Type TAB to switch thru the fields then you’ll get a tab-hole between “Login”-button (primary) and first input field (user_field). Please remove that hidden field focus.

Thank you!

----

Use … to play and keep password field empty:

{noformat}$ python3 LoginWindow.py{noformat}
column362:
31/Mar/25 8:30 AM;712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a;[~accountid:712020:289f037f-8785-42c6-b39d-21c4f6346eef] Thanks for the feedback on our current generic form - we always strive to make it better and it helps to get real developer feedback.

As far as I’ve understood, there are five issues / improvements you encountered:

* (main issue in ticket) Submit handling with two dialogs:
** I ran your script on an IGEL OS, and for me it behaves differently as you described. 
** But before digging into that, I strongly encourage to NOT open a separate dialog just for displaying a hint. That approach has many downsides, technical and UX related:
*** flickering / different size for main and hint dialog
*** you need to take care of escape handling
*** not common to open a new dialog just for displaying some message
*** Accessibility: using an auto-close is really bad; user must be able to stop it → please don’t do such things; also lost of context;
*** missing consistency to other generic-forms from IGEL (e.g. see VPN)
** How others are doing it: 
*** short description text that user must provide username and password (IMO also optional, for your small dialog that should be really clear)
*** disable login button until both provided
*** use messages when errors occur like “wrong password or username”
** => If I got it right, then your main issue should not be there anymore
* (a) Focus handling when switching back to other dialog 
** also here, I have other behavior and with my suggestion also not relevant anymore
* (b) Auto-focus handling for forms without input elements
** currently, the internal form-dialog-component auto-focuses to the first not-empty input field; from UX perspective, always the first input field which is not empty should be focused; 
** we could extend it so that the application can provide an id for the element which should be focused on start => will create a separate ticket
** but: with my suggestion above, using only one dialog, you will not have this problem in your case and thus not a blocker for you
* (c) Focus API to set focus on specific element
** see comment above - => [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11305|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11305|smart-link] 
** “as soon as possible” - we’d like to do that for all of our software, but we have priorities and to be honest, I don’t think that this is a real blocker for anyone; especially in your case, when following the suggestion I’ve made and how all others are using the generic-form => backlog
* (d) hidden tab position
** the hole you’ve mentioned is the focus on the window itself; I think you are right and we should skip focusing the window itself and instead go directly to the next element within the window
** => [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11306|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11306|smart-link] 



In summary: please try the common approach - if you want, we can also discuss it together. IMO this ticket can then be closed, I already created the new tickets.

column58: The Lockdown activation prevents access to PCI and MSR registers but we need this for energystar compliance in some cases. So we need to change the Lockdown to allow ryzenadj and x86_energy_perf_policy .

column1: Applying settings dialog despite 'Save' action clicked in the Config Dialog
column58:
If I check Security / “Active Directory/Kerberos” / “Login to Active Directory domain”, save the config and click on “No” in the “Apply Settings” dialog, then the config is applied without the node_action. The check mark remains set, but the node_action is left out.

I’d expect one of these behaviors:

# The check-mark is removed again and the node_action should restart when it is set again. The “Save” button (save configuration) should be grayed out again, as the config is original until it is set again.
# The check-mark remains, the “Save” button (save configuration) also remains and the node_action should be reactivated when it is triggered again.

It looks to me as a general issue hitting similar situations for other parameters.

----

With other words:

If node action is skipped once for a setting/change, it can’t executed anymore with the old behavior. Both proposals above improve the situation, the node action may executed later.

There might be an optimal solution: If “Apply Settings” dialog provides “Cancel setting” (revert setting to former state - proposal 1), “Delay node action” (proposal 2), “Skip node action” (current cancel/no) and “Apply/Yes”, then the user would have all possibilities available.

column1: Remove "save"-button from UI in virt-manager
column58:
The “save”-button for a domain causes issues due to how the mapper volumes are handled in the XML-configurations.

Decision: Remove the “save”-button from the UI in virt-manager - it would save the domain state to a RAM disk anyway and be removed on reboot.

column1: igel-desktop: start-menu "do not close when using on-screen keyboard"
column58:
difference between start-menu closing but igel-system-tray-windows stay open when clicking on the on-screen-keyboard:

* when start-menu gets opened, we grab input in out mutter-plugin, mostly to know, when a mouse-click hits outside of our mutter-plugin-UI (outside of the start-menu)
** In this case, a click on the on-screen-keyboard tells the mutter-plugin-backend to unfocus the WPEwebview
** the html in the webview probably gets notified about focus-out and our frontend-code closes the start-menu (I assume)
* when igel-system-tray-window is open, our mutter-plugin does not interfere with the input/focus-handling
** In this case, a click on the on-screen-keyboard is not detected by our mutter-plugin and not piped through our InputManager
** the open igel-system-tray-window does not get a focus-out event.
I assume the on-screen-keyboard software does not grab focus on its window.
So, there’s no focus-change, and the igel-system-tray-window does not auto-hide on focus-out and stays open.

Possible solution:

* In our mutter-plugin, we detect the on-screen-keyboard-window and create a input-region out of it, which is registered in our InputHandler
* Then, the button-press hit-detection takes this new on-screen-keyboard-input-region into account
* If the button-press-event hit the on-screen-keyboard-region, we do not unfocus the WPEwebview, but only send the event further down to the original on-screen-keyboard-window



----

Old ticket description, moved to [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13237|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-13237|smart-link] 

*analysis results*

* Felix and I tested current behavior and compared also to OS 12.7
* our igel-desktop UIs (e.g. start-menu) are not rendered inside of a real window (in contrast to e.g. igel-system-tray windows)
* in IGEL OS 12.7, opening a tray app and then click on another window title bar (e.g. terminal) does two things:
** closing the igel-system-tray-window (because of focus-out on outside click)
** focus and trigger the appropriate action (e.g. close, maximize) directly, no other click needed
* in IGEL OS 12.8, with new mutter-plugin tray-apps, we need two clicks:

10/Nov/25 12:24 PM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;difference between start-menu closing but igel-system-tray-windows stay open when clicking on the on-screen-keyboard:

* when start-menu gets opened, we grab input in out mutter-plugin, mostly to know, when a mouse-click hits outside of our mutter-plugin-UI (outside of the start-menu)
** In this case, a click on the on-screen-keyboard tells the mutter-plugin-backend to unfocus the WPEwebview
** the html in the webview probably gets notified about focus-out and our frontend-code closes the start-menu (I assume)
* when igel-system-tray-window is open, our mutter-plugin does not interfere with the input/focus-handling
** In this case, a click on the on-screen-keyboard is not detected by our mutter-plugin and not piped through our InputManager
** the open igel-system-tray-window does not get a focus-out event.
I assume the on-screen-keyboard software does not grab focus on its window.
So, there’s no focus-change, and the igel-system-tray-window does not auto-hide on focus-out and stays open.

Possible solution:

* In our mutter-plugin, we detect the on-screen-keyboard-window and create a input-region out of it, which is registered in our InputHandler
* Then, the button-press hit-detection takes this new on-screen-keyboard-input-region into account
* If the button-press-event hit the on-screen-keyboard-region, we do not unfocus the WPEwebview, but only send the event further down to the original on-screen-keyboard-window
