column1: migration_prepare damage sys partition
column58:
If one uses migration_prepare on a system which was newly installed via OSC then it can be that the sys partition get’s damaged. So if the reboot with repartitioning is not happening this can lead to a non working system which is quite bad.

After some searching the error was found as we use a free section to replace a section of the sys partition but for the moved partition this section is not marked ad used and gets overwritten which is the cause for the issue.

# IGEL run generic Open H264 update script

[Unit]
Description=Run generic Open H264 downloader.

ConditionFileIsExecutable=/services/%i/bin/igel-openh264-installer.py

Note the igel-network-online target is a Foo target that if there is not network there will not start, and creating that the igel-app-ready.target is not fully fullfill.

*Fact:*

* At the moment a system with chromium installed and no network, no wifi and not ethernet, will have igel-apps-ready.target not starting due to chromium hangs in this h264 service



*Task:*

* See if this dependency is really needed, if not removed
* See if there is a more friendly approach. 

Here is an idea: Keep the h264 installer service associated with igel-network-online.target (maybe BindsTo, WantedBy), but make it independent from chromium etc. In the rare cases where it downloads something restart those services that so far have the After relationship with the installer

So the bug happens because of a *segmentation fault when closing the window.*  
The segmentation fault occurs on data_clear for object with the same pointer as the terminal variable from terminal-window.c: terminal_window_action_new_window 

This function we have patched in debian/patches/IGLE_custom_command.patch. 

There we have created this variable. I believe the error occurred because the original author saw in other part of the code [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/xfce-terminal/browse/terminal/terminal-window.c#1633|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXTHP/repos/xfce-terminal/browse/terminal/terminal-window.c#1633] that when we emit_signal we do  g_object_unref but he did not see that there is a g_object_ref  just before calling emit_signal.
*The solution to this bug is to add g_object_ref before calling the emit-signal* so later on the terminal is not cleared before it is supposed to be cleared and we end up with a segmentation fault.

column1: Apps built for 12.5 re not installed on 12.6.0 (because Coredump wfs)
column58:
Under certain circumstances, apps, built for 12.5 are not installed on 12.6.0.

This behavior was reported by [~accountid:712020:46c05308-49c0-4448-a918-50103bee0e0b].

*Expected result:*

* App is installed during next boot after assigning it via UMS profile.

*Actual result:*

* App is not installed after reboot but notification to reboot again is presented (endless loop).

*Steps to reproduce:*

* Base System: 12.6.0
* Apps: Conky, ACME (built for 12.5)
* update.auto_update_on_boot = true
* Assign app via UMS profile with app version defined
* Chose the option to install the app after the next reboot
* Device if powered down when assigning the profile but the issue also happens when the device is powered on at the moment of the assignment

*Findings:*

* Works on 12.5.2
* Works with apps that re built for 12.4
* Works if update.auto_update_on_boot = false
* Works if choosing to install the app “now” when assigning it via UMS profile

[~accountid:712020:46c05308-49c0-4448-a918-50103bee0e0b] provided logs and has a snapshot of a proxmox VM that he could provide if required for analysis.



*Findings at Breixo’s side:*

* Coredump of wfs at the middle of the process, letting the updated without a  “reliable“ resource needed to read the journal.json and write it.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
So far there is not wfs reliable and present for read/write during all the update process, what is happening is undefined behavior. 
{panel}

* All the tickets found linked against this issue to the ticket.

This might point to incompatibilities of Zoom with the Debian Bookworm base. The issues are occasional crashes (some of which apparently related to the services_rw partition running full), short freezes during video calls and UI issues.

To get started, here’s a UI issue on 12.6.0:

* Launch Zoom and wait until the main window is displayed. Everything looks OK, the list of upcoming meetings (a web content control).
* Close the main window.
* A new window appears but only the frame is visible, the window contents are transparent.
* Close the new window.
* Click on the Zoom icon in the taskbar.
* The main window opens again but the section usually displaying the upcoming meetings won’t work anymore. Sometimes it’s just black, sometimes it shows garbled content, e.g. partial chat messages when switching from the “Team Chat” tab to the “Home” tab.

column1: setupd - finer node_actions in templates are not taken into account
column58:
Considering this setup.def:

{noformat}<app>
	<foo>
		<bar%>
			<baz>
				value=<>
				type=<string>
				runtime=<true>
			</baz>
			<test>
				value=<>
				type=<string>
				runtime=<true>
				node_action=<touch /tmp/test>
			</test>
			node_action=<touch /tmp/bar>
		</bar%>
	</foo>
</app>{noformat}

After creating an instance for bar%, the bar node action is triggered (/)
Changing foo.bar0.baz triggers the {{touch /tmp/bar}} node_action (/)
Changing foo.bar0.test triggers only the {{touch /tmp/bar}} and not the {{touch /tmp/test}} node_action (x)

This only happens with multiple node_actions inside the template bar% definition.
With fixed (non-template) parameters, the "finer" node_actions takes precedence.

13/Feb/25 2:54 PM;712020:d4e7358d-f576-40df-93f5-aac61445d5dc;The IdP functionality for the login itself is working properly, for OS11 and OS12.
The problem appears with the "active" password change (triggered by the user, using the "Change password" feature on OS site).
The behaviour also differs between OS11 and OS12.

Solution for OS12 (12.6.1.tp2, UMS 12.07.100.rc4):

Adding the AD config on OS site (Security > AD/Kerberos) additionally to the enabled "UMS as Identity Broker" feature (Security > Logon > UMS as Identity Broker).

>> then password change works.

Solution for OS11 (11.10.150, UMS 12.07.100.rc4):

Adding the AD config on OS site (Security > AD/Kerberos) additionally to the enabled "Shared Workplace" feature (Security > Logon > Shared Workplace).
Plus enabling the feature "Login to AD domain" (Security > Logon > AD/Kerberos) additionally to the SWP feature (otherwise a krb file is missing at /tmp/).

>> then password change works.

Issue is occuring on two different ADs.
The AD users have the permission to change their passwords.

As discussed with Peter and Martin.

column1: IMH Installer Problems in RC1
column58:
The IMH installer currently causes a couple of issues, especially when installing on a system which has seen previous versions of IHV/libvirt. In particular:

* The default storage pool should be the IGEL Logical Volume pool
* The network is not set up properly
* If there are existing GPT partitions or volume groups labeled ibvirtd/ihv, they should be renamed to imh by the installer instead of trying to create new volume groups
* The “convert” partition/volume group should not be created and OVA import disabled until we found a way to do this on the fly

Note: please check with Anton on what needs to be done to activate networking properly. There’s a system parameter if I remember correctly. The installer should not try to enable network features which require this system parameter but enable all other networks features. I believe this only affects the software bridge feature.
column223: IMH should work normally even when switching from libvirtd/ihv. There should also be a working network configuration.
column332: Install ihv, configure everything and check it works, then remove ihv and install imh.

column1: NumLock tampered
column58:
On newer base systems (12.5), it has been reported that NumLock is in an wrong state after bootup.

* Karte auf den Reader legen (Beep)
* Pin auf Numpad (geht nicht)
* Fenster mit cancel abbrechen
* Karte auf den Reader legen (Beep)
* Pin auf Numpad (geht)

I assume that the new base system uses x11-wayland, which has issues with QT5.

ℹ️ 

I can reproduce the issue with *12.5.0*. After starting, the Numpad does not work in IAFI (even though Numlock is enabled). After clicking in the IAFI input field it works. I get the same behavior when a USB keyboard is unplugged and plugged in. +With+ +*12.4.2*+ +everything works without problems+. It seems to be related to a change in the base system >= 12.5.0. I wrote a simple PyQt test application (main.py, main.qml) with which the behavior can be recreated.

[^main.py] [^main.qml] 

Steps to reproduce:

# Copy main.py, main.qml to e.g. /userhome/
# In userhome run: python3 main.py
# Make sure Numlock is enabled
# Application with input field shows up. Continuously press keys on the Numpad.
# Meanwhile, unplug the USB keyboard and plug it back in again.
# After plugging in the USB keyboard, the keys on the Numpad no longer works

column1: Suspend/Resume not working with 6.12.x kernel on HP mt645 G8
column58:
With the 6.12.x kernel the internal Panel of the HP mt645 G8 stays black after Suspend/Resume. After some test the issue was introduced with Kernel 6.10.x. After a longer bisecting session it turns out the commit: [https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?h=v6.12.13&id=0d38f6009e4e4e511fb5c3c673d54bf0c242c4b7|https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/commit/?h=v6.12.13&id=0d38f6009e4e4e511fb5c3c673d54bf0c242c4b7]

Is the cause for this issue reverting it solve it. As it is not sure if this is the correct way we add a amdgpu module parameter which can be set to change the behaviour back and solve the issue. A test if this parameter can be set after module load time shows this must be already set when the amdgpu module is loaded otherwise it prevents the suspend from working.

I have the same issue with the webkit2gtk apps.

On my hardware, the following environment variable is set:

{quote}user@ITCE446B01FE16D:~$ env | grep DRI
LIBVA_DRI3_DISABLE=1{quote}

But this env-variable is not causing the issue.
Note the difference: in ticket description LIB{color:#ff5630}*GL*{color}_DRI3_DISABLE, on my hardware LIB{color:#ff5630}*VA*{color}_DRI3_DISABLE

It’s really the LIB{color:#ff5630}*GL*{color}_DRI3_DISABLE variable, which is loaded into the systemd-environment for certain systemd-services.
The notify-ui or system-tray systemd-services load their environment like this:

{quote}[Service]
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/igel-desktop{quote}

with

{quote}user@ITC7085C2949521:~$ cat /etc/default/igel-desktop
LIBGL_DRI3_DISABLE=true{quote}

since 12.4, it got introduced in [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8663|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8663|smart-link] 


If I edit this {{/etc/default/igel-desktop}} to
LIBGL_DRI3_DISABLE=0
or simply remove it or rename it to igel-desktop.orig,
and restart the systemd-service, it works fine, correctly rendered windows.


*This needs to be fixed for 12.8* 
It’s not related to a specific mutter-version.

Workaround: configure a dummy StoreFront server.

So, you need to give it some time to settle. On my setup, about 2 seconds.

column1: Chromium + Proxy | Cannot set chromium to use systemwide proxy settings
column58:
*Summary*

Although Proxy does generally work, it is not possible to configure Chromium to use systemwide proxy. If configured to do so, it will always run into an “No internet” error.

*Reproduction*

# Install OS 12.6.0.rc6 and Chromium 132.0.6834.110 Build 1 RC1
# Configure TC Setup
_TC Setup > Network > Proxy System-wide proxy configuration = Manual proxy configuration_
_TC Setup > Network > Proxy > HTTP Proxy = 192.168.34.37_
_TC Setup > Network > Proxy > Port =_ -_3129_-  _3128_
_TC Setup > Network > Proxy > Username_ 
_TC Setup > Network > Proxy > Password_
_TC Setup > Apps > Chromium Browser > Global Settings > Proxy > Proxy Settings = Use system proxy settings_
# Apply changes and reboot device
# Open chromium
+>> Result:+ No connection to the internet via chromium possible

*Additional Infromation*

* If Chromium is configured to “_Auto detect proxy settings_” it will detect the systemwide proxy settings and can establish a connection to the internet
* Although Chromium cannot successfully establish connection to the internet, the device itself does. Connection to the UMS exists.

*Environment*

HP t655 | IGEL-0653 | BIOS M45 v1.08
OS 12.6.0.rc6
Chromium 132.0.6834.110 Build 1 RC1
Beside Chromium and its dependencies, only PWA 1.0.0 Build 2 was installed



Edit: Wrong Port mentioned in the Ticket description. I corrected it accordingly

Edit:

After further tests were conducted we discovered the following issue.
If the _SSL Proxy_  in _System > Network > Proxy_ is configured additionally to the _HTTP Proxy_, then it will work.
Strangely however, _SSL Proxy_ does not need to be configured, if _Chromium > Global > Proxy_ is set to “_Use fixed proxy servers_”

column1: Switch to ICG takes too long
column58:
If the UMS is preferred over the ICG but in a particular environment (public WLAN) only the ICG is reachable, then the attempt to connect UMS takes too long, especially in case of HA with more than one UMS. For each UMS the rmagent always does these steps:

* if there are locally made changes then write them to UMS
* if there are some modified custom device attributes then write them to UMS
* get remote settings from UMS

Each step is executed independently from the result of the previous step, so if the UMS isn’t reachable at all then a such attempt can take 3*45sec = 135sec per UMS (45sec is the connect timeout by default). 

This behavior can be improved if a single attempt to connect a one single UMS is terminated after the first failed step. Then a max delay per UMS would be the configured connect timeout, by default 45sec.

06/Jun/25 10:12 AM;712020:c2f113c7-926b-43c8-9951-8fd54c1ca916;I have tested this function with Notepad, Calculator and Paint together, and in 7 tests all three were always started. Maybe it has been improved recently. However, I have seen the following failure points that can be improved. 

* Pattern matching with fnmatch.fnmatch(x.get('label'), autostart_resource)
** x.get('label') must be a string. If it is None or not a string, fnmatch.fnmatch() triggers a TypeError.
* run_storebrowse hangs. The code uses timeout=180, so if the underlying run_storebrowse call never returns (or returns something unexpected), we could be stuck for three minutes (180 seconds) before time runs out.
* If run_storebrowse itself throws an exception instead of returning a process handle, we’ll be thrown out of the loop unless wrap it in a try/except.
* eval_storebrowse_result should return exactly three values (exit_code, error_code, error_message). If it returns fewer or more values, an error will probably occur.

column366:
02/Oct/25 7:29 PM;712020:c2f113c7-926b-43c8-9951-8fd54c1ca916;After many tests and different attempts, i have decided not to progress in this topic because of the following reasons, besides newly implemented Apprestart feature indirectly fixes this problem as it has watch and launch technique. Adding a new fix could negatively result in false duplicates of the same app. Here are some of the reasons:

# Two mechanisms racing: *ensureStarted()* (one-shot) and *apprestart* (continuous) both try to launch. If X11 hasn’t extracted the window yet, both assume it’s missing and trigger a launch, resulting in duplicates.
# X11 visibility lag: After launching, there’s a variable delay before CTXCTL sees the app in {{_CTX_PUBAPP_LIST}}. Your checks occur during this blind spot, leading to false “missing” reports and unwanted relaunches.
# Name mismatch: The app launches with the *store name* ({{resource['name']}}) but is detected by the *X11 title*, which can be truncated, localized, prefixed with “#”, or different altogether. Fuzzy matching helps, but it can still misfire.
# Overlapping timers: Multiple GLib timers can be scheduled for the same {{launch_id}} (ensure + restart + retries). If we don’t cancel pending timers when the app appears, those timers will still fire and launch again. Repeated checks during startup can stack retries. Even longer initial grace period (e.g., 20–30s) is not enough.
# Patterns: Generic patterns can inadvertently match multiple resources, causing “missing” reports and launches, even though the actual app is running with a slightly different title.

column363:
07/Jan/25 2:47 PM;61669e8b071a720071bdee03;The signatures themselves of old apps are still valid, and since the SDK key is not present in productive systems, it has no implications on which apps can be installed on productive systems.

In terms of testing: we need to compare apps against old versions, and for resigning, I like to check the app’s signature beforehand. The other way I see is to check an app only at submission, which might overlook (unintentional) modifications to ipkgs before resigning. The signature check is basically our re-signing insurance.

Implication is also, that companies cannot hand in apps build with old SDK anymore, as they will not be accepted anymore. All currently pending requests would therefore need to be rebuilt with new SDK environments.

column1: Systemd timer persistency not working
column58:
We linked the /var/lib/systemd/timers to /wfs/systemd/timers but the persistentcy is still not working I assume this is because of the wfsd which manipulates the last modified time when syncing content during boot.

If this partition runs full Zoom will behave erratically, may even crash. One low hanging fruit is the log directory:

* rm -Rf ~user/.zoom/logs/*

The directory ~user/.zoom/data/cefcache is usually cleared out when stopping Zoom but if this doesn’t work for some reason, consider clearing it out, too, while Zoom is not running.

Last. but no least, if you remove all entries in ~user/.zoom, you’ll have reset Zoom to factory defaults and will have to log in again.

column1: Wrong Citrix Logoff workflow
column58:
When you click on a IGEL storefront session, the icon turn into a “Logoff Icon“.

Unfortunately, when you click the logoff icon, it seems like it does not logoff, but do a disconnect instead.

In contrast, using the Citrix sessionhandler (/services/cwa/sessionhandler/logoff …..) does a correct logoff.

So, I think we should introduce a reg key within the Citrix subsystem to control that behavior (choose between disconnect or logoff)
column244: * With a Citrix logoff, all applications are now terminated correctly and not just a disconnect is executed.

column1: Webkit not corrcectly imported in last security update for stable/old/12.5
column58:
Only one webkit2gtk version API 4-0 (compiled against libsoup2) was updated,
the webkit2gtk API-4.1 (compiled against libsoup3), which is used by all modern desktop components, was not updated.
Both API versions are compiled from the same source and should always be updated together.
When using {{./bin/addpkg}} the correct versions are imported.
This mismatch lead to crashes in setup-assistant and local app portal.


In the future please be more careful and have a closer look at the PR, you can clearly see that the description does not match with the content and the description is even mentioning a 2.47.2 version which is a development version not meant for production use. Not sure where this version came from.
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/pull-requests/11753/overview|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/pull-requests/11753/overview] 

*Task*
Please have a look in the automation scripts why this happened.

h2. Analysis

* OS 12 before 12.5 used the SID version of Webkit2GTK compiled on top of Ubuntu Focal.
* OS 12.5 never received an update to Webkit2GTK, thus kept using the SID version compiled on top of Ubuntu. Part of the reason for this was that one of the ABIs we need was dropped in the latest SID version
* In preparation of security updates in 12.6, we switched to the Bookworm version of Webkit2GTK
* I’ve updated and compiled this Bookworm version of Webkit2GTK for 12.5.3
* The security update script then got confused by the SID entries in src/debian for parts of Webkit2GTK in stable/old/12.5 and ended up with a mix of Bookworm and SID versions in the commit message but for some reason the only changes in the diff in the PR were for the Bookworm components.

h2. Next Steps

* We need to find out why the script didn’t update the SID-based packages as it announced in the commit message
* We should add a check that prints an error (or at least a warning) when a security update results in a mix of different distributions for a single source package.

Bzgl thirdparty und igel ( das Ergebnis von checkout-additional-repos.sh ): 

Ich war für alle repos in igel und thirdparty auf dem master branch.

Ich musste in IGEL/externaldriver.sh den wacom pad driver auskommentieren, sonst hat der kernel nicht gebaut.

Dann jeweils:

sudo ./igelbuild.sh menuconfig  (keine Änderungen vorgenommen, exit und übernehmen) 

sudo ./igelbuild.sh

Den Kernel habe ich dann jeweils in diesen Branch integriert:

[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/commits?until=refs%2Fheads%2FQCL-4621-hp-t660-sqashfs-error-testing|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/commits?until=refs%2Fheads%2FQCL-4621-hp-t660-sqashfs-error-testing]

Damit macht IGEL OS alle ~30 Sekunden einen factory reset, man schafft damit in 2 1/2 Minuten je einen Zyklus.

Logfiles und Anzahl der Factory resets werden unter /license/frl/ gespeichert.

Wenn man den Test anhalten will, dann dann man das über touch /license/frl/stop oder touch /wfs/stop machen.

Leider fängt mein Skript nicht alle SQUASHFS Fehler auf, da manchmal die Services beendet wurden durch den squashfs Fehler.

Falls im Logfile unter /license/frl/squashfs.log keine Fehler angezeigt werden, aber das Gerät trotzdem hängen bleibt, dann ist es sehr wahrscheinlich SQUASHFS.

Diese Fehlerbilder gibt es:

# Gerät bleibt im IGEL logo hängen (muss man mit power button override ausschalten)
# Gerät überspringt den Onboarding Dialog und bootet auf Desktop durch.
Meistens kann man hier ein Terminal mit CTRL+ALT+F11 öffnen und sieht im journalctl die SQUASHFS Fehler.
journalctl | grep SQUASHFS
# Dann kann man auch ein systemctl start igel-check-squashfs-error durchführen, dann wird der fehler in die Logdatei geschrieben.

Einen Fehler im log oder die beiden oben beschriebenen Probleme innerhalb der ersten 10 Factory resets.

column1: RDP Web Access: allow login without password and no credentials dialog
column58:
A RDP file may include "prompt for credentials on client:i:0". This is supported by current implementation, but username and password (e.g. "clear password:s:secret") must be included. 

The intention is to hide the credentials dialog if "prompt for credentials on client:i:0" is available - even if no password is provided.

The second approach is to configure a filter string, that must be included in RDP file. Netscaler adds a line that starts with “pol_name=”. If that string is configured as filter, no dialog is shown.

My understanding is this:

In OS11, the igel_display_daemon listened to DRM events and therefore resizing was detected and triggered a xrandr call by the user_display_xrandr script.

In OS12.5, the igel-system-tray detected the changes but most of the time it “snapped back” because the saved user config was used.

When Chromium browser is started, it also installs the PWA on its profile. That on itself is fine, also we are not able to prevent that from happening with shared policies.

The real issue is that my tooling treats it as a new PWA installation and fires its logic and notifications as if the PWA was a fresh install. This will confuse the user and will also reload the icon and so on.

We have to find a way to prevent that from happening.

Tasks:

* (/) remove /userhome/.gnome/apps as persistent for PWA
* (/) check in /services_rw/pwa/userhome/.config/pwa/Default/Web Applications/Manifest Resources/ instead of /userhome/.gnome/apps for new directories
** (/) compare id with files in /userhome/.gnome/apps
** (/) if found check name and create file with url and id on PWA rw part
* (/) only set custom name if if not installed yet (if no file for url on rw part)
* (/) do not ask to open pwa after creating session if a pwa browser is aleady open
* (/) test

column1: Chromium OS12: handle custom policy ExtensionInstallForcelist
column58:
[~accountid:712020:f51b0662-9da8-4f9c-9795-40af8572495a] knows the details

ExtensionInstallForcelist seems to be used quite frequently to roll out extension installation via setup or UMS profile. We are using said policy to install our own extension (Igel Utility) which handles download blocking and the download confirmation dialog. The custom policy overrides the policy and thus removes our extension, meaning that our download blocker and the download confirmation dialog are not active.

We need to merge ExtensionInstallForcelist and not override it with the custom policy.

Alternatively, we could add a new parameter to force install extensions but customers, already using the custom policy will still have the issue.

column1: Citrix plugin function compose_with_fb() called with uninitialized data
column58: At Uniklink Magdeburg (Andreas Huth) they run a configuration that leads to a call of v3_compose_with_fb(). This is already problematic as this function is not efficiently implemented, i.e. it would show bas performance. What makes things worse is, that it was called with a partly unititialized argument struct image_buf *fb. Here we saw fb->lossless_op = 4. The header file  H264_decode.h (from Citrix) only specifies values from 0 to 3. Since the rest of struc image_buf contains nonsense data (obviously uninitialize) this leads to a crash. We nee to make the IGEL Citrix plugin more robust against such situations.

column58:
Since our 12.4.0 release the mobile broadband connection configuration is not anymore possible with UMS/WUMS profiles. The parameters are still available in a local TC Setup, but not anymore in the WUMS profile configuration dialog. See attached screenshots.

The problem is that with [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-7445|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-7445|smart-link] the “network.interfaces.mobile_broadband.connection%“ instance template was removed.

Attached find a IGELmaker patch/fix that already was successfully tested - at least from configuration perspective (not functional).

27/Nov/25 4:09 PM;712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8;h2. Summary

h3. Researched webkit-wpe codebase for cursor setting / updating.

The libwebkit-wpe-fdo backend we use in libigelwebkit assumes it is running under a Wayland session and signals cursor changes via the wayland protocol. The platform can then react to these signaled changes. Since we are not running in a wayland session, we cannot react to these.
=> Once we switch over to Wayland we should get the signaled cursor changes and react accordingly

h3. Looked into webkit-wpe api 2.0 Webview::mouse-target-changed signal

This signal is emitted when the mouse cursor moves over an element such as a link, image or a media element, and then provides a context object which contains some info.

=> This approach was discarded as it doesn’t seem to fire for every DOM element and the context object only has info like {{is_link}}, {{is_media}}, {{is_text}}, etc and only provides link uri or media titles or labels.

h3. Went with sendPointerEvent()

This function is dispatching the platforms pointer event with the x and y position to the wpe view backend and is called from igel-desktop InputManager.
In libigelwebkit-wpe prior to passing this event on, we query the current DOM Element at that position via Javascript and then get its computedStyle.cursor property to aquire the cursor set via CSS.

We monitor the currentCursor and emit a cursorChangedSignal to the libigelwebkit-wpe consumers with the css cursor style so they can react and map the cursor style to the available platform cursors.

In the igel-desktop we react to the cursorChangedSignal and map the cursorStyle to the available MetaCursors to set the cursor.

column1: Network system tray confused by changing MAC address
column58:
The issue occurs with MAC address passthrough. Please see the screenshot. The setup shows that the second Ethernet interface (usually a docking station, in my case an Ethernet USB dongle) shall get the MAC address from the first interface (usually built-in). The first ifconfig output shows the first Ethernet interface while the second is not plugged in. The second ifconfig output does not show the first interface (removed by unbinding the driver) anymore but instead the second that received its MAC address from the first. The address 00:E0:4C:68:01:D7 that appears in the system tray dialog is the native one of the USB dongle. That is overridden immediately after plugging in in the udev context. Obviously Network Manager still sees it and reports it to the system tray, which gets confused. Apparently the number of undesired entries increases by one with each plugging-in.

In OS12 MAPT is currently only on this branch: feature/LX8-10131-fujitsu-thunderbold-docking-mac-address-passtrough

column1: igel-nmc.service logs python error in journal
column58:
igel-nmc.service (nmc.py) produces:

{quote}Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]: [nmi:26] ERROR: dnget failed
Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]: Traceback (most recent call last):
Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]:   File "/usr/share/pyshared/igel/nmi.py", line 24, in dnget
Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]:     return I18N.inst.idnget(k, False)
Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]:            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Okt 28 08:15:29 ITC7085C2949521 nmgtk.py[7519]: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'idnget'{quote}

Probably because of the split of nmc.py and nmgtk.py.
nmc.py runs before nmgtk.py (system-systemd before user-systemd)
and wants to use nmi.py, but nmi is not yet initialized.
It gets initialized in nmgtk.py.

column1: CTX daemon method call not blocking
column58:
Example:

{{/services/cwa/sessionhandler/logoff --resource someAppOrDesktop }}returns immediately, because the call to the dbus method ( {{response = signout_method(urls)}} )

just returns a dummy response ({{Signout request completed}}), which is wrong at this time.

column369:
28/Oct/24 9:22 AM;712020:c2f113c7-926b-43c8-9951-8fd54c1ca916;I have fixed 30 seconds timeout issue when specified sessions are closed by ensuring all the apps under the specified sessions are closed. And one time I have seen timeout of dbus, it fails to respond to signout method call, it happens because of switching to synchronus apporach by removing the queue. The reason for this switch from asnchronus to synchronous was asked due to the problem mentioned in the ticket, it turned out that the solution is a different one which is already implemented. While the daemon works in both synchronous and asynchronous approaches, synchronous communication can simplify the interactions between classes, making the code easier to understand and maintain. However, when multiple threads are involved, blocking operations (dbus monitoring and method calls at the same time), synchronous behaviour leads to concurrency problems, makes the application unresponsive or leads to unexpected behaviour. This is the reason why the daemon may not respond at times, restarting the service will bring it back. Switching to an asynchronous approach (action handlers perform non-blocking operations) solves all these problems. After switching it, i have tested several times, results were quite promising, so far i haven't seen any dbus method call failures, and unexpected behaviors. 

And for the session handlers (disconnect and signout), when called with --resource, please use single quotes (' ') instead of double quotes (" ") because shell will escape some special characters, that's why we have observed incorrect behavior when passed exact same string.

"disconnect --resource "#DEV 2019 $50 -4v"   treated as  "#DEV 2019 -4v". But single quotes treats as a literal string.

18/Oct/24 4:20 PM;712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae;I don’t understand the problem in full maybe we should talk next week but the app is creating the conf snipper in the install.sh which is very bad. it writes stuff to a readonly location during the execution of the install.sh which will be gone after the first reboot.

The ld.so conf snippet with the app name is automatically created during building from the SDK igelpkg.

install.sh script is only executed once on install or after an up/downgrade not on every boot.

Adding subfolders of /usr/lib/<arch> to ld.so.conf seems to be bad practice. I had a look how debian is handling it and the reason why they put it into subfolders is that they support different implementation of libblas so there installation mechanism links the lib directly to the /usr/lib/<arch> folder.

{noformat}ls -lah /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libblas.so.3
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 47 Nov 27  2022 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libblas.so.3 -> /etc/alternatives/libblas.so.3-x86_64-linux-gnu{noformat}


So IMHO this is clearly a bug in the app.
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/virtual_background/browse/igel/install.sh|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/virtual_background/browse/igel/install.sh]

And the app should either move the libs directly in the libs folder or also create a symlink. This install.sh hack always ever worked on the first boot after app installation.

column1: Lid close during shutdown operation suspends the device
column58:
h3. Description

When closing the lid on a laptop device, after starting a shutdown operation, the device is not powered off. Instead the device is unintentionally suspended or just monitors are switched off, depending on the configured lid close action (see parameters system.actions.lid.*). This can lead to a higher power consumption.

h3. Hardwre

HP mt645 G7

h3. Steps To Reproduce

* Open an AVD session and keep it running in the foreground
* Press the power button of the laptop
* Confirm you want to shut down the device
* Close the lid right away (as in a second or so)

HP laptops don’t have any pulsing/blinking power LEDs during suspend. In order to verify whether the device has entered suspend state instead of shutting down, open the lid after 30 seconds and check whether you see the login screen right away (suspend) or IGEL OS boot logos.

*Task*

* when the shutdown gets trigger we have to mask  to sleep.target and suspend.target should be masked.

{noformat}  systemctl mask suspend.target sleep.target{noformat}

*From where it comes the +dev:*

column363:
15/Oct/24 9:03 AM;712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae;This is a case problem, the base_system you assigned is 12.5.0+dev but the image in the portal is 12.5.0+DEV, your image got auto uploaded from a device where you installed a custom image from the igelmaker. The UMS/WUMS  does not care about the case but the App Portal does.
This can only happen with the DEV portal and custom build igelmaker images because both add +dev to the version igelmaker in lowercase and the build automation in upper case.

Please remove the 12.5.0+dev lowercase from your UMS and import the correct version from the Portal with upper case.

column1: Thinlinc setup configures wrong selected monitor
column58:
If the IGEL OS12 configures monitors ordering from right to left ([2][1]), then the Thinlinc setup configures wrong monitor. In that case the session configured for the monitor #2 will be displayed on the #1 monitor. This happen because the Thinlinc always counts from left to right and from top to bottom, so the actual monitor’s number must be calculated according to the configured monitor order.

See the documentation of the Thinlinc client by Cendio:

[https://www.cendio.com/resources/docs/tag/client_config_params.html|https://www.cendio.com/resources/docs/tag/client_config_params.html|smart-link]
column362: 15/Oct/24 1:44 PM;712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae;We can not change counting of monitors because of one app. In IGEL OS the primary monitor must always be the first because of how we patched our XOrg.
column363: 15/Oct/24 2:05 PM;712020:2d964323-be83-492f-8b8e-ca3eddc43546;[~accountid:712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae] This recalculating must be done only in the thinlinc config not in the xorg or screens/monitors config. Each monitor has a number from 1 to N, assume that we configured a [3][2][1]  monitor setup, now we configure our the thinlinc session to be displayed on the monitor #1. Currently the session will be displayed on the monitor #3!  For the thinlinc session config we have to use the index+1 of the monitor setup instead of the monitor number.

column1: Unable to create a custom CI partition after several updates of base_system
column58:
As old partitions are never removed by the updated, so after several updates (~12) of the base_system there is no space to create a custom CI partition.

At the moment the IGEL OS12 doesn’t provide any framework for purging old (not being in use) app’s partitions. The updated/igelpkgctl must provide an API for creating of a RW partition with a given number and size, so that it can be used for creating of a custom CI partition, custom partition or other configurable RW partitions with a certain defined partition number.

column1: [igelpkg] parent directories in dirs.json are always root owned
column58:
In an app that has this part in dirs.json:

{noformat}{
    "path": "/userhome/.local/state/foo/bar",
    "owner": "777:100",
    "permissions": "755",
    "persistent": true
}{noformat}

The final bar directory is user owned and accessible - so far, so good.
But all parent directories in the path will be root owned, especially /userhome/.local/state, so mkdir /userhome/.local/state/new as user will fail.

I'm not sure if the whole directory path chain should have the same owner as the final bar path, maybe there are cases where the parent directories should be kept root owned.
-If this is the case, this can be workarounded with a chown in install.sh-
column362:
09/Oct/24 5:24 PM;712020:590271f0-d8b1-4789-b812-dca0b6ac1880;I think the issue is in the generated post_mount.sh script. It has this part:

{noformat}mkdir -p /services_rw/app/userhome/.local/state/foo
chmod 755 /services_rw/app/userhome/.local/state/foo
chown 777:100 /services_rw/app/userhome/.local/state/foo{noformat}

which keeps the parent directories root owned, especially /userhome/.local/state

column1: Race condition when installing both apps and certificates at the same time
column58:
There’s a race condition when installing both a community app developer certificate and a community app at the same time. Ideally, RMagent would install the certificates first, then install the app but this id difficult because the UMS sends the requests independently and RMagent works on them without any specific order.

On top of that, other types of certificates, e.g. browser certificates, may have the exact opposite requirement: first install the browser app, then the certificates which are then processed by a script which adds them to a browser-specific [binary]  database.

This will require help from the UMS.

column1: igel-tcsetup: Passwords cannot be cleared
column58:
h3. Original Ticket Description:

If a password was set in TC-Setup, it can only be changed but not cleared.



h3. Updated Ticket Description:

Example pages:

* Page1: Security > Password
* Page2: Security > Logon > Local User
* Page3: Network > Network Drives > Windows Drive



*Analysis results:*

* in OS12:
** Page1 + Page2:
*** when a password was set, it is not possible to delete it in TC-Setup
*** the data is stored in */wfs/setup.ini*
** Page 3:
*** password can be deleted via reset button
** 
* in OS11:
** Page1 + Page2
*** when a password was set, it is not possible to delete it in Java TC-Setup
*** the data is stored in */wfs/setup.ini*
** Page3:
*** password can be deleted via reset button
* some remarks:
** Page1+Page2 in OS12 use “confirmPassword” which is not providing the reset button
*** reason for that: it should not be allowed to enable password (checkbox parameter which must be activated beforehand) without setting a password; so the combination of enabling (checkbox=true) and having an empty password is invalid
** Page3 is handled via “generic” + “password parameter” which displays the same UI control as for “confirmPassword” but with reset possibility
* conclusion:
** TC-Setup for OS12 behaves the same as for OS11
*** Page1 + Page2:
**** the only difference is that in OS12, it is always visible that a password is still given in the data (even though disabled because of the dependency)
**** in OS11, this is not so obvious, because the setting of a password is done in a modal dialog
** If there is the feature request that passwords are deleted in the setup files, then we have probably the following alternatives:
*** special handling in TC-Setup for Page1 + Page2: when checkbox parameter = false, then disable existing password values
**** => changes in TC-Setup backend
*** using “generic” + password parameter instead of “confirmPassword”; but then also the “disallowEmptyPassword” must be reimplemented; not sure, if this can be done without breaking concepts.
**** => changes in ConfigDialog
*** perhaps there are more alternatives

column58:

{noformat}user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ igelpkgctl uninstall conky

Packages to remove:
	conky-1.10.8+1

Do you want to continue? [Y/n]y
Processing 1 APP
[1/1] parse conky-1.10.8+1: [====================] 100% [OK]
[1/1] uninstall conky-1.10.8+1: [====================] 100% [OK]
user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ echo $?
0
user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ {noformat}

Installing an app is also possible, but the certificate needs to be in place first, avoiding this issue to be critical:

{noformat}user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ igelpkgctl install -rf conky-1.10.8+1.ipkg 
Processing 1 APP
[1/1] parse /userhome/conky-1.10.8+1.ipkg: [====================] 100% [OK]

user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ echo $?
0
user@ITCBC241155CFD7:~$ {noformat}

but that means, one can revert an app’s version to an older (vulnerable) version because the certificates/signatures match.

column1: Missing way of preferring WPA2 Personal to WPA3 Pesonal when network supports both
column58:
In OS11 the Wireless Manager respects network.applet.wireless.prefer_sae and by default configures WPA2 Personal when the network announces that it supports both WPA2 Personal and WPA3 Personal. In OS12 the igel-system-tray configures WPA3 Personal then.

See the linked support case for an example where WPA3 Personal fails due to driver or HW limitations.

With Network Manager 1.32.12 in our 12.4 configuring WPA2 Personal in the setup does still not work. NM additionally passes SAE to the WPA Supplicant without checking necessary requirements and so the connection still fails. NM 1.42.4 has improved checks, which at least in the mentioned SN case prevent that WPA3 Personal is allowed. See nm-supplicant-config.c

Regarding network.applet.wireless.prefer_sae: I have not seen an example where this has been changed  in customers' ini files. Just configuring WPA2 Personal is probably sufficient regarding maximum security, at least with NM 1.42.4. Maybe some day NM will make the right decision all by itself.

column1: cmty apps: Denylist is SHA256, but script checks SHA1 --> denylist is ineffective
column58:
I was able to load the dev-intermediate.crt on a productive system by force-copying it into /wfs/cmty/certs:

{noformat}root@ITCBC241155CFD7:~# keyctl show %:igel_cmty
Keyring
 547032616 ----s-rv      0     0  keyring: igel_cmty
 616058632 ----s-rv      0     0   \_ asymmetric: dev-intermediate.crt
{noformat}

The intermediate gets loaded into the “wrong” keyring but it shows that the denylist is ineffective, which would be needed for leaf certificates.

log says:

{noformat}cmty-apps-load-certs.sh Community certificate /wfs/cmty/certs/dev-intermediate.crt loaded successfully{noformat}

The Problem is that the fingerprint in the denylist is SHA256, and not SHA1, so the check/string compare in the script fails. Please use the SHA1 fingerprint in the denylist and ideally plan a denylist.sha256 which is checked against {{openssl -fingerprint -sha256}}.

Also, check if -fingerprint returns SHA1-Fingerprint and only then use the respective denylist.

*background info*

I had problems with my ISP (Telekom), so my LAN was connected, but of course no Internet accessible. So I opened a Wifi Hot Spot from my smartphone.

As can be seen in more details in the comments, the problem seems to be that setupd (or something else) cannot properly read certain parameters like {{network.interfaces.wirelesslan.device0.alt_ssid0.networkname}} . The parameters exist in the files (setup.ini/group.ini/setup.def).

column363:

column1: Citrix FIDO2 parameter issue
column58:
Wie heute besprochen, anbei der Workaround um die FIDO-Anmeldung in der CWA zu fixen.

 

In der AuthManConfig.xml steht beim aktivieren des Keys: app.cwa.authman.fido2enabled

<FIDO2Enabled>true</FIDO2Enabled>

drin.

 

In der authmanconfig_ctx.xml oder so ähnlich, steht als Beispiel aber:

<key>FIDO2Enabled</key>

<value>false</value>

 

Also habe ich per folgendem Kommando das ändern lassen:

 

grep "FIDO2Enabled>true</FIDO2Enabled" /services/cwa/opt/Citrix/ICAClient/config/AuthManConfig.xml &&
sed -i 's|<FIDO2Enabled>true</FIDO2Enabled>|<key>FIDO2Enabled</key><value>true</value>|g' /services/cwa/opt/Citrix/ICAClient/config/AuthManConfig.xml

column1: With proxy, the network connectivity always shows "limited"
column58:
If a proxy is configured, the NetworkManager connectivity state is “limited” at maximum, even if a connection via proxy to the connectivity URL is possible.

Thanks to [~accountid:712020:3c37eef8-8519-44b8-9b4b-f5057209ba9c] , the root cause is clear: NetworkManager wants to detect connectivity per interface, and therefore binds the socket to the respective interface. But then a connection to cntlm at 127.0.0.1:3128 via this interface fails.

column1: Update command does only reboot even if new apps got assigned in UMS
column58:
When I issue an update command in UMS, the IGEL OS currently just reboots even if no new app configuration has been assigned before. This should be avoided, because when nothing changed, why should the system reboot.
In case a new app has been assigned before, then the behavior is also not correct. It shows a message, that the apps have been downloaded, but that is not true. It simply reboots as in the case mentioned above. That is, because the information about the new app assignment has not been transferred to the IGEL OS. The OS will start fetching the new app after next boot, but when deferred app activation is active, then it needs another update command to be sent to the device to activate it.

In my opinion, the update command should trigger rmagent to fetch the current app assignments from UMS and then run the real update. When I assign a new app in UMS and send an update command I would expect it to install the assigned app and not to reboot, install the apps and eventually not even activate the newly installed app.

column1: "Reboot now or later" notification loop with installed community app and missing certificate
column58:
If a community app has been installed and the corresponding community developer certificate removed at a later time, the “reboot now or later” notification shows up after each system reboot.

Steps to reproduce:

* Install a community developer certificate and an app signed by that certificate
* Reboot and verify the app is working normally
* Remove community developer certificate from wfs/cmty/certs
* Reboot - the “reboot now or later” notification will be display after every boot.

I’ll attach a sample app and the corresponding developer certificate but you’ll need to build directly from stable/old/12.5 because the community app requirements will show up in 12.5.0.rc6.

*Repdouction steps*

Use version for igelfs_utils and igel_update present under:
feature/LX8-9651-community-apps-verify-signature-during-installation-backport-stable
feature/LX8-9651-community-apps-verify-signature-during-installation

* Install base_system from branch bugfix/LX8-9812-reboot-now-or-later-notification-loop-with-installed-community-app-and-missing
* Copy attached company.crt to /wfs/cmty/certs/ (folder must be created first)
* Install attached speedcrunch-0.12.0.ipkg from file via {{igelpkg install -f /tmp/speedcrunch-0.12.0.ipkg}}
* Reboot
* Check that app is mounted {{/services/speedcrunch}}
* Check that app is installed correctly {{igelpkgctl list installed}}
* Remove cert: {{rm /wfs/cmty/certs/company.crt}}
* Reboot
* Check that a notification pops up showing that app is not usable anymore
* Check that app is installed correctly {{igelpkgctl list installed}}
* Check that app is not mounted {{/services/speedcrunch}}
* Check /wfs/journal.json if app is marked to being downloaded

*Proposed solution:*

Only delete invalid partitions if they are not part of the active or future configuration. If they are part of the active or future partition config flag them with an error in the journal than the igelpkgd can show a error message

*Tasks:*

* Realize the changes in {{check_for_not_valid_partitions}} as expected to work with the journal
* The partitions that are not there because a not valid signature but they are in the future or actual configuration needs to provide a new error for it.

column1: Firefox: missing smartcard PKCS11 link
column58:
In order to use smart card certificates in Firefox, PKCS#11 library configuration has to be done. The corresponding configuration file is pkcs11.txt in the browser profile.

Add to function link_nssdb_certs() in file firefox_utils.py the creation of a symbolic link in default profile/pkcs11.txt pointing to /userhome/.pki/nssdb/pkcs11.txt .

column1: Citrix: Com port mapping configuration
column58:
When specifying a single Citrix Com port mapping the following way:

Local device: COM 1
Server Device: \\Client\COM{color:#ff5630}3{color}

Then in wfclient.ini will be written:

LastComPortNum = 1
ComPort3 = /dev/ttyS0

The port won’t be mapped.

Instead it should be:

LastComPortNum = {color:#ff5630}3{color}
ComPort3 = /dev/ttyS0

So the LastComPortNum has to be set to be the highest number of the Server Device instance values.

BTW, mapped com ports can be viewed inside the Citrix session in a cmd window with command “net use”.

Bug was found in a session with [~accountid:712020:8784a866-5fd8-4b6c-9afb-02ddeba155a8] in a session at a customer.

column1: NetworkManager delays suspend/shutdown
column58:
The NetworkManager-dispatcher.service sporadically starts during system suspend and delays the suspend process so, that the igel-sleep-final.target is sporadically skipped by the systemd. So some services can’t invoke actions pulled by the igel-sleep-final.target (unmount of wfs, resetting rmagent’s connection mode etc).

In the [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX7-10175|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX7-10175|smart-link] the issue seems to be fixed, so we need a port of that fix to the OS12.

column1: libvirt app installation fails if base system is installed on disk with msdos partition table
column58: app currently expects GPT part table to create LVM PVs for image storage. On systems with msdos part-tables base system already creates maximum number of 4 primary partitions.

column364: 23/Jul/24 4:15 PM;712020:669c6177-2627-4770-97b6-0c52d822f253;[~accountid:712020:66c61fac-739d-4add-aa6a-c5a5c1b514a6] How many primary partitions are on the MSDOS-partitioned disks? column367: 26/Aug/24 10:06 AM;712020:669c6177-2627-4770-97b6-0c52d822f253;MS-DOS partition formats don't support more than 4 primary partitions, all of which are already in use. There's no way we can support libvirt on MS-DOS-partitioned devices.

column377:
14/Aug/24 9:40 AM;712020:33877cc6-c74f-4389-884d-4526b850ad57;Found the reason for the user-session restart:


Since network is started without user-session, network is online earlier and igel-rmagent-apply-rmsettings-boot (igel-rmsettings-apply) comes earlier.
Sometimes earlier then the setup-assistant.
If so, the script's test on running setup-assistant does not hit, and the apply-notification is created, with do_default_action on notification timeout, which applies node_actions.
The setup-assistant may come up during this 20 seconds notification timeout.

The node_actions contain a x11-restart if the language got changed in the setup-assistant.

Solution:

* in the rmsettings-apply script, test on two filemarks
** one is created in root-context during lightdm_config if firstboot.target is default.target
** second is created in user-context during firstboot_wizard0 session start
* in the rmsettings-apply script, test again if setup-assistant is running, after the notification exited, and do nothing

column1: Chromium can not be started because of missing rw partition
column58:
After updating the base system to version 12.4.2.rc3,  removing several apps and reinstalling chromium, Chromium can not be started anymore. The chromium rw partition is not mounted under /services_rw/chromium. A look into the /wfs/crypt/partitions.json file shows that the zoom and chromium partitions use the same minor number 201. The zoom rw partition is mounted and accessable. Due to the same minor the chromium rw is not at all created/mounted/accessable.

After a deinstallation and reinstallation of the chromium app the rw partition *is not repaired.* The log files tclogs2.zip wfs_crypt2.zip were created directly after the reinstallation. You can see that igf201 (Used for zoom and chromium rw) was deleted and is not available at boot time.

12/Jul/24 4:12 PM;712020:7e66b073-1a07-4884-adf9-8aa0da966e50;[~accountid:61669e8b071a720071bdee03]

I checked a bit how that works. rwpart script checks /dev for the igf minors if creating a new partition is requested and writes the determined minor number into /wfs/crypt/partitions.json config file. Afterwards it call handle-raw.sh which reads partition.json and mounts, creates partitions beaing in mentioned json file. Really creating the partition on disk and writing the partitions.json seems to be out of sync in a way. Determine a wrong minor could happen only if /dev  doesn’t contain the minor already if listdir is called. 

It could be the script, but it could be a problem with the managing queue in the updater or both. We should talk about it on Monday [~accountid:61669e8b071a720071bdee03]

column1: Device sends reconnectsync after wake up from suspend
column58:
We detected the following behaviour and we are not sure if this is a correct (or expected) behaviour:

If you suspend a device and it is started again (even after several days) the device does send reconnectsync and not updatedeviceinfo command. The result is, that device which are always suspended don’t get app updates or new settings, until settings are pushed or they do a real boot.

In my opinion, the device should do on wake up after suspend, the same as on boot.
column80: Analyzing of the problem - the main cause is figured out.;23/Jul/24 11:10 AM;hamburg;14400
column362: 22/Jul/24 4:54 PM;712020:2d964323-be83-492f-8b8e-ca3eddc43546;The issue can’t be reproduced. I tested it with the 12.5.0.rc3 in a Proxmox VM and on a real hardware, HP Elitebook, driven by a UD Pocket.
column363: 23/Jul/24 8:13 AM;5d2c7e5979d4ee0c8b1d0bfb;The issue does not occur on UDPockets, have you tried it with a UD3?
column364:
23/Jul/24 11:05 AM;712020:2d964323-be83-492f-8b8e-ca3eddc43546;I could reproduce the issue on a UD3 running OS12 installed on the internal flash storage. -The issue occurs if suspend is triggered over the shutdown dialog UI, whereas suspending due to inactivity or via UMS/rmagent works as expected.-

-If suspending is invoked from the shutdown dialog then the systemd igel-sleep-final.target will be not invoked at all, so the rmagent (and probably other services having handling on reaching of the igel-sleep-final.target) can’t properly handle suspend of the system.-

It seems that the igel-sleep-final.target sometime doesn’t start and system falls into sleep without reaching the igel-sleep-final.target. Probably there is no reliable dependency between the sleep.target and the igel-sleep-final.target. This would explain the sporadic nature of this issue - the igel-sleep-final.target is queued to be started but the system is going to real sleep earlier without waiting for igel-sleep-final.target.

So this problem is caused by the OS base system and not by the rmagent.

column1: rmagent cannot download files beginning with space
column58:
While parsing the incoming UMS message containing a file having spaces at the beginning, these spaces are trailing spaces after the file header in json format and they are ignored by the json-c parser but counted to the parsed content, so the expected size of the file is never read and the message is rejected as an incomplete message:

{"format":"urlfile","type":"file","length":"4"} abc

The example contains a file of size 4 (“ abc“), but the json parser stops at the first non-space char which is ‘a', so we’ll get only 3 bytes instead of expected 4.

column1: Issue with UMS "Corporate Identity Customization" of type "Screensaver Custom Partition"

(Working properly at IGEL OS11, e.g. 11.09.130.) –> see “Edit2“ below.
But not working at OS12, 12.4.1.
The settings are arriving on the device (see attached "os12setup-screensaver.jpg").
But the needed directory "/custom/" isn't created.
So the screensaver is starting, but not showing my picture, that should be within /custom/.
Looking at the CP setting at the TC-Setup, looks the same as on the OS11 device (see attached "os12setup-cp.jpg").

Edit:
my picture seems to be located not at /custom/screensaver/, but at /wfs/.customize/screensaver, see attachment “saver-file.jpg“.

Edit2:
It makes a difference wether you're using a newly created "CIC Screensaver CP" or and imported one (imported from an earlier UMS version than 12.05.).
With a newly created CIC > checking the TC-Setup on OS11, it shows that the path for the saver file is empty.
With a "old" imported CIC > checking the TC-Setup on OS11, it shows that there's content at the path for the saver file.
See attachment “pre-12.5-fwcsExport.zip“ for some old FWCs to test.

column1: TC Setup does not lock parameters with uservalues and usergroupvalues set
column58:
A parameter can have value, group value, user value and usergroup value assigned. If group value, user value or usergroup value are set, TC Setup should display the parameter locked, because these values have higher precedence over value. However this is only the case for group values.

How to reproduce:

* create local terminal instance
* issue: setuservalue sessions.xterm0.name user; killwait_postsetupd
* open TC Setup, it shows user as the name; parameter is not locked and can be modified
* modify name to base, Save and close setup
* displayed name remains user, also after reopening setup
* issue resetuservalue sessions.xterm0.name; killwait_postsetupd
* now displayed name is base on desktop and in setup

The same with setusergroupvalue and resetusergroupvalue.

column1: Internal display on P&F hardware is detected as being connected even though it is not physically connected
column58:
Xorg detects the internal display (touchscreen) on Pepperl & Fuchs proprietary hardware as being connected, even though it is not physically connected. This will affect the installation of OS12 because the OSC installation dialog and setup assistant will appear on the primary screen, which is not connected in this case, but will be detected as connected and therefore the customer will not be able to install OS12.

See logfiles: “RE_ FLX - BPC Standalone Display Mirror.zip” -> 2_tclogs.zip

h3. Hardware information

Device connected to eDP (built-in device/touchscreen) physically connects/disconnects to the device motherboard only via LVDS cable. The display controller board is mounted/soldered on the device motherboard. Therefore, Xorg detects the display as connected even though it is not. On the system side, we are not able to detect whether the display is connected or not, because it is always connected.

h3. Todo

* Detect P&F hardware with the given dmi information (See attached dmi_flx.txt)

* Disable internal eDP port when an external screen is connected to the device, e.g. dp1, dp2, …

column1: cups lpadmin no more allowed for root but only for user
column58:
Since 12.5
following happens:

{quote}root@LINUX-3:~# lpadmin -p test -v file:///dev/null
lpadmin: Forbidden

root@LINUX-3:~# lpstat -v
lpstat: No destinations added.{quote}

with /var/log/cups/error_log

{quote}E [13/Jun/2024:11:39:52 +0000] [Client 18] Returning HTTP Forbidden for CUPS-Add-Modify-Printer (ipp://localhost:631/printers/test) from localhost{quote}



Adding a printer with the {{lpadmin}}-command is working if called as user 'user'.
The user ‘user’ is in the ‘lpadmin’ group.

{quote}root@LINUX-3:~# getent group lpadmin
lpadmin:x:108:cupsys,user{quote}

In /etc/cups/cups-files.conf , we have:

{quote}# Administrator user group, used to match @SYSTEM in cupsd.conf policy rules...
# This cannot contain the Group value for security reasons...
SystemGroup lpadmin{quote}

and identical in /etc/cups/cupsd.conf .

I do not know why the behavior changed with 12.5 (some bookworm changes?).
But I would have solutions (either of them would work):

# add ‘root’ to the SystemGroup line in /etc/cups/cups-files.conf in the igelmaker module cups-daemon
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/browse/modules/bookworm/debian/igel/net/cups-daemon/added/root/etc/cups/cups-files.conf?at=refs%2Fheads%2Fstable%2Fos12#19|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/browse/modules/bookworm/debian/igel/net/cups-daemon/added/root/etc/cups/cups-files.conf?at=refs%2Fheads%2Fstable%2Fos12#19]
OR
# add
{{usermod -a -G lpadmin root > /dev/null 2>&1}}
to /services/cups_printing/bin/cups_server_config
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/cups-printing/browse/input/all/bin/cups_server_config#6|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIGAPP/repos/cups-printing/browse/input/all/bin/cups_server_config#6]



Some discussions on the internet:
[https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/235477/cups-add-printer-page-returns-forbidden-on-web-interface|https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/235477/cups-add-printer-page-returns-forbidden-on-web-interface]
[https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1405669|https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1405669]

column1: CLONE 11.10 RR - igel-proxy-config sets socks_port to socks host string
column58:

* A corrected spelling error “varuables” and
* the proxy password gets retrieved successfully only once.

{noformat}user$ get network.proxy.settings.sys_proxy_socks_port # > 3128
user$ /config/bin/igel-proxy-config
user$ get network.proxy.settings.sys_proxy_socks_port # > lx-squid.lx.test (source: sys_proxy_socks)
user$ resetuservalue network.proxy.settings.sys_proxy_socks_port
user$ get network.proxy.settings.sys_proxy_socks_port # > 3128{noformat}

column1: libwebsockets hides the origin TLS error while connecting
column58: Origin TLS errors occurred during connecting (SSL_connect() call) are logged by ‘info' log level which is off by default. So we see in the log only the follow up error - ‘read failed’. This makes investigation more difficult eg in a support case.

column363:
31/May/24 11:11 AM;712020:c7675f80-e40b-4883-9285-a0214f8dd8ed;Hi [~accountid:712020:3dc6e47a-0842-44dc-9482-98b7108798b5] ,

we have an answer from Atlassian on this topic.

Atlassian found a root cause of the issue: When a legacy page is created with external inline images, then converted to new editor, images get converted to inlineExtension. Upon checking this with devs on the behaviour we learned that, new editor does not support inline images with custom size.

There is already a bug ticket with Atlassian, that got reopened with our support ticket: [https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/CONFCLOUD-77304|https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/CONFCLOUD-77304]

In the meantime we have two options:

* Reupload the affected images to the pages on the Cloud site.
* Otherwise, change the way the attachment was added at the source site before the import happened, and perform the migration again. → I would not recommend rolling back a whole migration for this bug.

I am sorry, that there is no fix at the moment.

Do you have any other example pages for this issue to forward to Atlassian, so that the bug tickets gets the attention it deserves? 

Thanks and kind regards

Christina

column1: Clean up after failed automatic registering
column58:
If the automatic registering has been failed but the trust chain was obtained and installed, then the orphan trust isn’t removed properly, so it still remains in the /wfs/igel-rmagent/trust-store/cacerts.pem. The later successful registering process either via obs or scan-n-register leads then to an inconsistent state - cacerts.pem contains former certificates and this makes impossible to get connection to the UMS.

For details see the attached logs. 

Solution:

* Introduce a 'registering' state as the registering process consists of more than one step
* Each registering process has to wait for the previous one
* Failed automatic registering process must reset the trust store (call rmagent-trust-reset)
* Successful registering process must enforce the consequence of the trust store

The collision in this case was between rmagent-register and igel-rmagent-connector.service. But the connection is only made if the device is registered. It should therefore be sufficient to call rmagent-trust-reset if an error occurs during registration.

column1: printer: tray backend: improve driver detection
column58:
It can happen, that lpinfo -m offers multiple drivers for one printer model, and even a driverless option.
The print-tray-backend only uses one (the first?) found option for the model.
This may be a driverless option.
This does not work for usb-connected printer.

*Task:*

* rework the driver detection
** maybe use lpinfo --make-and-model “<model-name>“ -m
** or not only save one option per model, but all available options? and offer selection for user ?
** or prefer non-driverless option in usb case and if other option available
* prefer hpcups before hplip
* prevent driverless for non-network-printers
* use {{everywhere IPP Everywhere}} instead of {{drv:///cupsfilters.drv/pwgrast.ppd Generic IPP Everywhere Printer}} 
** {{dataContext.availableDrivers["Generic"]["IPP Everywhere"])}} to be used as fallback

More insight:
/usr/lib/cups/driver/postscript-hp list
for example delivers not only make and model, but also the MDL identification, which differs for same models.
This could be used to detect the correct driver. case insensitive string comparison.
The MDL ident is not included in {{lpinfo -m}} 

Jörgs example:

{quote}/wfs/user$ usbprinter -i
[ usblp0 ]
MFG: Hewlett-Packard
MDL: HP LaserJet P2055x
DES: HP LaserJet P2055x
URI: usb://HP/LaserJet%20P2055x?serial=S2A7RT3
Access: lp lp scanner 

--------------------------------
user@PILLE:/wfs/user$ lpinfo --make-and-model "HP LaserJet P2055x"  -m
drv:///hpijs.drv/hp-laserjet_p2055x-hpijs-pcl3.ppd HP LaserJet p2055x hpijs pcl3, 3.22.10
hplip:0/ppd/hplip/HP/hp-laserjet_p2055x-pcl3.ppd HP LaserJet p2055x pcl3, hpcups 3.22.10
drv:///hpcups.drv/hp-laserjet_p2055x-pcl3.ppd HP LaserJet p2055x pcl3, hpcups 3.22.10
everywhere IPP Everywhere{quote}

column1: Bluetooth pairing of keyboard needs key presses to reconnect after reboot
column58: Matthias Haas reported an issue with Bluetooth keyboard after a system reboot. The keyboard “consumes” some key presses before it works properly. Seems it does reconnect only when keys are pressed leading to some inputs getting lost.
column362:
15/May/24 3:57 PM;557058:cc5c73b0-c7fe-4b8e-a783-43b2040be3d3;Matthias did already some research and found this:
Linux can automatically reconnect Bluetooth keyboards after a reboot, but it requires some configuration. Here are the steps to set it up:

# Pair the Bluetooth keyboard with your Linux system. This is usually done through the Bluetooth settings or by running `bluetoothctl` in the terminal.

# Once paired, find the MAC address of your Bluetooth keyboard. You can get this from the Bluetooth settings or by running `bluetoothctl` and using the `devices` command.

# Edit the `/etc/bluetooth/main.conf` file and add the following lines, replacing `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX` with the MAC address of your keyboard:

```

[Policy]

AutoConnectDevices=XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX

```

This tells the Bluetooth daemon to automatically connect to the specified device on startup.

# Restart the Bluetooth service for the changes to take effect:

```

sudo systemctl restart bluetooth

```

After following these steps, your Linux system should automatically reconnect the Bluetooth keyboard when rebooting or powering on.[1]

If you have multiple Bluetooth keyboards, you can list their MAC addresses separated by semicolons:

```

AutoConnectDevices=XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX;YY:YY:YY:YY:YY:YY

```

Some desktop environments like GNOME and KDE also provide graphical tools to manage Bluetooth devices and enable auto-connect functionality for specific devices.[2]

column369:
17/May/24 12:17 PM;712020:6ec12684-75f8-475c-b5ef-b00de547e51a;I’ve analyzed these two performance issues:

# slow scrolling through apps on overview page
# slow hover effect on app card on overview page



*Checking different browsers*

* overview page (all apps):
** Chrome and Firefox: fast
** libigelwebkit in IGEL OS: slow
** epiphany (which is also based on Webkit): slow
** => performance is not good with any Webkit browser
** => not related directly to libigelwebkit
** => In general we can say that the rendering performance of Webkit is not as good as Firefox / Chrome. Developers must pay more attention to build up a good DOM and to have good styling via CSS
* overview page (apply filter like “supertux” or “Tunnel group” to only have a few app cards):
** all browsers: fast
* detail page:
** all browsers: fast
* => performance degrades with the number of app cards



*Slow Scrolling*

* main problem is the usage of the CSS styling “backdrop-filter” for every app card which is very resource intensive (it applies a blur filter on an HTML element)
** see [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/APP/repos/frontend-service/browse/src/components/ApplicationGroup/ApplicationGroup.style.jsx?at=release%2F12.4.0#24|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/APP/repos/frontend-service/browse/src/components/ApplicationGroup/ApplicationGroup.style.jsx?at=release%2F12.4.0#24]
* IMO, the styling is not needed at all and can be removed
* removing it increases scroll performance in Webkit (not as fast as in Firefox / Chrome, but fast enough)
* possible further optimization: use a lazy loading technique and dynamically show app while scrolling will further improve it



*Slow Hover Effect*

* main problem is the re-rendering of the DOM whenever a hover effect happens:
** this is because of the usage of “display: none ↔︎ block” for the description / action button
** see [https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/APP/repos/frontend-service/browse/src/components/ApplicationGroup/ApplicationGroup.style.jsx?at=release%2F12.4.0#150,193|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/APP/repos/frontend-service/browse/src/components/ApplicationGroup/ApplicationGroup.style.jsx?at=release%2F12.4.0#150,193]
** changing the display property leads to a complete DOM rerender because it affects the layout of the elements (and thus is very expensive)
* I could verify that hover effect is blazing fast when the two elements are not existing anymore
* I could NOT verify real alternatives because code must be adjusted for it
* possible alternatives:
** skip the CSS way of switching description with action button on hover (using “display” CSS property) and instead use a Javascript way (React state)
** there could be other pure CSS solutions, must be investigated
** UX solution: rethink the “hover effect” at all because of its downsides:
*** it does not work with mouse-less devices
*** it confuses the user (at least me) because I wanted to see the details (i.e. navigate to the details page), but instead clicked on the “install” button which suddenly appears



In summary: we are aware that Webkit engine is not the fastest one, but with some caution it is fast enough. See other applications like TC-Setup and Setup-Assistant or Tray Apps.

user$ resetuservalue network.proxy.settings.sys_proxy_socks_port

column363:
15/May/24 10:01 AM;61669e8b071a720071bdee03;CVSS3 would be 7.9 (High): [https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.0#CVSS:3.0/AV:A/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H|https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.0#CVSS:3.0/AV:A/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H|smart-link] 

The problem is that the leak affects components outside of the OS, which is why the scope of an attack is “changed”. Anyone seeing the password can have access to the full FTP server running in the client’s infrastructure…

column1: Serialization not working in igel-desktop
column58:
Serialization is not working in libigelmutter plugin. Reason for it is that mutter is compiled against json-glib which defines the same symbols als json-c used by libigelserialize. In order to fix that we need to build both libs symboled version information. json-c is already build with it and it is also enabled for newer json-glib. So update json-glib to latest version.
For more information see upstream bug:
[https://github.com/json-c/json-c/issues/621|https://github.com/json-c/json-c/issues/621|smart-link]

Setup-Assistant: rmagent state: not only listen to state-changes, but also check state inital
column58:
Setup-Assistant needs to check rmagent state inital on startup.

Currently we only listen to rmagent property-change signal and look for the ‘state’ property, to know about UMS-connection.
We use the early state ‘registered’ to know about auto-UMS-connection.
If the user triggered UMS-connection manually, the Setup-Assistant UI shows the finish-page already, before the rmagent-state changes happen.

But for auto-UMS-detection:
If the rmagent is not in its first state ‘unregistered’, but already further in its states, maybe already ‘registered’ or even ‘connecting’, the setup-assistant will never get a state-change to ‘registered’ and will never move into the auto-UMS-connection handling and never shows the corresponding finish-page in the UI.

In such a case it can happen, that the UI still shows the langage-page, then the last rmagent state ‘connected’ is signaled, and the setup-assistant starts a timeout to auto-reboot the system (60 seconds in the auto-UMS-detection case).

*Tasks:*

* check on rmagent state initially and start the auto-UMS-connection handling if necessary
** would mean immediately jump to the finish-page

The other ‘ICA’-processes are older and have a correct env var set. cwa0 is a child of systemctl --user - why do they have different env var sets? What makes cwa0 getting a wrong proxy setting?

column1: Handling WPA Enterprise in system tray
column58:
See [https://developer-old.gnome.org/libnm/stable/libnm-nm-dbus-interface.html#NM80211ApSecurityFlags|https://developer-old.gnome.org/libnm/stable/libnm-nm-dbus-interface.html#NM80211ApSecurityFlags|smart-link] 

If access point WPA flags and RSN flags do not contain NM_802_11_AP_SEC_KEY_MGMT_PSK or NM_802_11_AP_SEC_KEY_MGMT_SAE, it does not make sense to ask for a passphrase (WPA key).

If there is NM_802_11_AP_SEC_KEY_MGMT_802_1X or NM_802_11_AP_SEC_KEY_MGMT_EAP_SUITE_B_192 (not yet supported by us) it is a WPA(1|2|3) Enterprise network.

For activating a configured WLAN one can use the Roam(ssid) method of the com.igel.NetworkBackgroundHandling system D-Bus service (currently only on staging/os12) or of the com.igel.WlanConnectionEditor on the session D-Bus (old).

** backend already has this and sends it to the frontend
** {noformat}enum class WifiAuthType : unsigned int
{
  unsupported      = 0,
  open             = 1,
  key              = 2,
  usernamePassword = 3
};{noformat}

}{noformat}

column1: Failsafe Boot can lead to lost WFS partition
column58:
While testing with Grub failsafe boot I found that the WFS partition got deleted by the kernel driver.

After looking deeper into it the root case is that the partition magic is different from the sys partition due to migration from OS11 or if preserve settings was used in OSC.
column223:
* Do a OS11 to OS12 migration
* Boot normally into OS12 and check if WFS is valid (settings present)
* Boot with failsafe boot option
* Check if WFS is still present and valid (no lost settings)

column1: Cleanup of tmpfiles is disabled
column58:
Temporary files configured in /etc/tmpfiles.d can have an age.

On IGELOS some temporary files are configured to have an maxage of 10 days. These will never be cleaned because the timer systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer is disabled on our system.

[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/browse/modules/focal/ubuntu/igel/admin/systemd/functions/pkg_install?at=refs%2Fheads%2Fstable%2Fos12#25|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/BUILD/repos/igelmaker4/browse/modules/focal/ubuntu/igel/admin/systemd/functions/pkg_install?at=refs%2Fheads%2Fstable%2Fos12#25]

We should think about activating the cleanup timer, as there is a risk of running out of space.

column1: udev rules of apps do not get effective for cold plugged devices
column58:
If an app contains an udev rule, the rules do not get applied for cold plugged devices.

Example:
Grundig app with Grundig Digta Soundbox 830

/etc/udev/rules.d/95-grundig.rules:
KERNEL==”hidraw”, MODE=”0777”

If device is already plugged at boot, /dev/hidraw* don’t have correct access rights.

column368:
21/Mar/24 10:25 AM;712020:2d964323-be83-492f-8b8e-ca3eddc43546;There is bit of misunderstanding of the process of merging and applying of remote settings - the remote settings are always merged to the setupd at the end of the system slice _without_ asking the user. The user is only asked for applying of node actions. According to this - all the software started before the merging will use the previously configured language, whereas the software executed after merging of received settings will show display names in the currently configured language.

The remote settings must be merged without prompting the user because otherwise we lose the control over the remote management. This mechanism is implemented in that way since OS10. So I’d say it works as expected though it is a shortcoming. But this small shortcoming shouldn’t have a real matter in the real life, as the language is usually set once since onboarding and a lot customers disables the prompting anyway.

column58:
All-OR-NOTHING : I assume all three of them a re present and valid. If one is not present, none is present.

{{2024-03-12 15:37:42.672 [auth_only] sessions.wvd2.options.default-user }}
