All clients such as AVD, Citrix .... which are administered by an identity provider such as Evidian or Imprivata must have the following session parameters.
This is to avoid that the providers having to know where to find the parameters for user, PW and domain. 

OS11: 

* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.username   (NAME is the instance of the session, like: avd0) *(value must start with a “.” )*
* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.pw 
* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.domain

Example:

* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.username* = .settings.username 
* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.pw* = .settings.password
* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.domain* = .settings.domain	

original pathes: 

* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.username	
* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.password	
* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.domain	

ToDo for OS11:

* (/) Horizon
* (/) Citrix
* (/) AVD
* (x) Win365 - OS12 only
* (/) RDP
* (/) RDP3
* Parallels, Workspot, Evidian,  … need to communicate to 3rd Party vendors (IGEL Ready Apps)



Example of pnlogin%:

{noformat}    <sessioninfo>
        <username>
            value=<.settings.username>
            type=<string>
            runtime=<false>
            displayname[en_us]=<Path to Username parameter >
        </username>
        <password>
            value=<.settings.password>
            type=<string>
            runtime=<false>
            displayname[en_us]=<Path to Password parameter>
        </password>
        <domain>

column1: Poly headsets constantly active (possibly streaming microphone data)
column58:
In previous OS versions, Poly headsets would be inactive unless in a Zoom/Teams call. With 12.4.0.rc5, my Poly BT600 headset dongle flashes all the time, even after a fresh reboot with nothing running. A BT700 headset dongle doesn’t flash in this situation but it reacts to pressing the mute button on the microphone boom (changes from blue to red and back).

This appears to be triggered by a constantly active input stream from the microphone. One indicator is:

{noformat}user@ITCF4A80D5186A1:~$ pactl list | grep -B2 -A3 RUNNING

Sink #0
	State: RUNNING
	Name: alsa_output.usb-Plantronics_Poly_BT600_99ea03eb7e514796a0f47d819bf980b1-00.analog-stereo
	Description: BT600 Analog Stereo
	Driver: module-alsa-card.c{noformat}

Killing igel-system-tray “fixes” the issue. Without further investigation, I would guess the microphone volume level bar graph is constantly active, even if the audio tray app is not visible.

h2. Why is this a problem?

* Headsets are always active, sending microphone data and draining the batteries
* The computer will also have a slightly increased power consumption (more cosmetic than problematic)
* Constantly active microphones are sooner or later going to get noticed by customers, which will lead to questions

If deleting this duplicate wifi-instance  helps in your case, this would point to a problem with the scan for hidden-wifis.
This {{IGEL Technology HB}} is marked as a hidden wifi in your config. The system-tray triggers a scan for such hidden wifis and the network-manager does not like too much scan-requests in a short period of time.
column371:

[https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/network-manager/+bug/2056529|https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/network-manager/+bug/2056529]

column1: Centralized parameter info for identity providers
column58:
All-OR-NOTHING : I assume all three of them a re present and valid. If one is not present, none is present.

NOTE: For AVD / WVD / CPC / RDP3 the user and domain parameter are identical, this is a known flavor of these kind of sessions

{{2024-03-12 15:37:42.672 [auth_only] sessions.wvd2.options.default-user }}
{{2024-03-12 15:37:42.675 [auth_only] sessions.wvd2.options.default-user }}
{{2024-03-12 15:37:42.675 [auth_only] sessions.wvd2.options.crypt_password}}

All clients such as AVD, Citrix .... which are administered by an identity provider such as Evidian or Imprivata must have the following session parameters.
This is to avoid that the providers having to know where to find the parameters for user, PW and domain. 

OS11: 

* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.username   (NAME is the instance of the session, like: avd0) *(value must start with a “.” )*
* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.pw 
* sessions.[NAME].sessioninfo.domain

Example:

* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.username* = .settings.username 
* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.pw* = .settings.password
* sessions.pnlogin0.*sessioninfo.domain* = .settings.domain	

original pathes: 

* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.username	
* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.password	
* sessions.pnlogin%.settings.domain	

ToDo for OS11:

* (/) Horizon
* (/) Citrix
* (/) AVD
* (x) Win365 - OS12 only
* (/) RDP
* (/) RDP3
* Parallels, Workspot, Evidian,  … need to communicate to 3rd Party vendors (IGEL Ready Apps)



Example of pnlogin%:

{noformat}    <sessioninfo>
        <username>
            value=<.settings.username>
            type=<string>
            runtime=<false>
            displayname[en_us]=<Path to Username parameter >
        </username>
        <password>
            value=<.settings.password>
            type=<string>
            runtime=<false>
            displayname[en_us]=<Path to Password parameter>
        </password>
        <domain>
            value=<.settings.domain>
            type=<string>
            runtime=<false>
            displayname[en_us]=<Path to Domain parameter>
        </domain>
    </sessioninfo>{noformat}

column1: Lenovo L14 Gen4 Intel + Universal Docking Station: After Hotplugging one of the active Display shows Black Screen
column58:
Hotplugging one of the 3 external displays from the docking station and then plugging it back in. It can happen that another connected display gets a black screen. The black screen display appears normally on the display tray app and screenshot.

The following two cases can occur when hotplugging for the first time:

Case 2: (fixed with RC7)
When hotplugging for the first time, only 2 of the three remaining displays were shown in the screenshot, even though the third one is on and you can still slide in windows to the not shown display
(pic: after hotplugging uni docking station (only 2 displays shown screenshot) 1)

Case 3: (fixed with RC7)
The first time you hotplug, it may happen that the disconnected display is still shown in the Display Tray app. This display problem sometimes resolves itself after a few more hotplugging attempts.

HowTo:
1. Config the layout for the displays with the docking station
2. Unplug one of the displays
3. After the first hotplugging, check in the Display Tray app whether the disconnected display is still there
>> Result: Separate display still present in the tray app and the same behavior described in case 2
4. Plug the disconnected display back in and repeat the hotplugging
>> Result when disconnecting: Disconnected display disappears when hotplugging
>> Result when plugging in: One of the non-separated displays turns black, but is still active in the display trap and visible on screenshots

Displays:
Internal (Lenovo L14 Gen4 Intel IGEL-0754) 

Universal Docking Station IGEL-0820
3xBenQ EL2870U (HP-Lab)

column1: Circular systemd dependency since last igel-notifyd changes
column58:
After the last igel-notifyd changes we introduced a circular systemd dependency.

Problem is that the {{systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service}} service is started after {{local-fs.target}} which is started very late in igel os because unlocking rw partitions is part of {{local-fs.target}}.
The new {{igel-notifyd.service}} is started after {{systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service}} because it wants the log dir {{/var/log/igel}}.
The solution now is to move the {{igel-rwpart-unlockall.service}} from the {{igel-services-partitions.target}} (which depends of {{local-fs.target}} to the {{igel-apps-ready.target.wants}}.

column1: Serial printing fails due to access rights
column58:
Serial printing not possible because the serial devices /dev/ttyS* which are available at boot time are put into the dialout group and are thus accessible to cups which needs it be group lp to use it.

In OS11 all serial devices are put into group lp by the cups_sys module which isn’t used in OS12’s base_system, so all devices get the dialout group by default.

column1: pcom: should ignore returnvalues
column58:

column1: CLONE - Virtualbox mouse emulation is handled as touch which causes offset issues
column58:
We have serious issues with Virtualbox with multi monitor configuration like in Sinabox cases. There the emulated mouse get handled as Touch and therefore is mapped to one monitor which leads to mouse offsets and so on. This renders the system unusable.

Solution in this case is to filter out the virtualbox device and prevent that it is handled as a touchscreen device.

column1: OS12 Chromium: big delay on node_actions im ms teams pwa installed
column58:
While testing Chromium Browser setup parameters, node actions are triggered with a quite big delay (several seconds). The delay seems to relate to the times, the node actions have been triggered.

The issue only occurs if the MS Teams PWA app is installed and I suspect, that the bind-mount in the mount_pwas function of utils.py might cause the issue.

I already tried to fix it with [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8444|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8444|smart-link], by checking if the chromium-pwa binary is already a mount point before trying to do the bind mount. Sadly it did not fix the issue.

The bind mount was introduced with [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-6641|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-6641|smart-link] by [~accountid:712020:725616c0-4ddd-4ec8-8be6-5dac31847bca]. I suggest giving him this ticket.

Maybe we have to create a separate service for the pwa part. We do not need to trigger this every time a setupd parameter is changed but only at boot.

Also, my check for the bind-mount might not work (pathlib.is_mount: {{On POSIX, the function checks whether path's parent, path/.., is on a different device than path, or whether path/.. and path point to the same i-node on the same device}}). Could be tested with the classic "mountpoint" command, though.

We could rename igel-chromium-clear-shader-cache.service to a more generic service (it is only started on boot and not triggered by any node_action) like igel-chromium-init.service (maybe find a better name?) and also move the prepare pwa command from igel-chromium.service to this service. This way, we make sure, it is only run once at boot.

Tasks:

* igel-cif
** (/) replace pathlib.ismount by subprocess.run(['mountpoint', '/userhome/.config'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) → returncode: 0 is mountpoint in utils.mount_pwas()
* chromium app
** (/) rename igel-chromium-clear-share-cache.service to something more generic → igel-chromium-init.service?
** (/) move cif prepare-pwa command to renamed service

column1: igelpkgd: Check JWT iat timestamp
column58:
IgelPackageDaemon checks the validity of the JWT token ([https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igelpkgd/browse/igelpkgd/src/PackageManager.cpp#3408|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igelpkgd/browse/igelpkgd/src/PackageManager.cpp#3408]). Currently only the exp (The is the expiry date) of the token is checked against the system time.

If the system time is out of sync, e.g. the RTC battery is dead, this could cause problems. Therefore an iat (timestamp when the token was created) against timestamp check should also be implemented.

h3. Tasks

* Implement an iat check. Fail if the system clock is older than the iat timestamp of the jwt token.
* Check if libcpp-jwt-dev ([https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/libcpp-jwt-dev|https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/libcpp-jwt-dev]) could be used for encoding and validation

h3. Hint

When implementing jwt checks in igelpkgd, it was not possible to successfully encode our jwt token with the libcpp-jwt-dev library. We should check this again and if possible change the manual token parsing to the library.

column1: Fix TC build of Pointsharp Net iD app
Rework at multi-stage mechanismus regarding when to start
column58:
*Description:*

Thanks to [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8456|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-8456|smart-link] we found out that the multi-stage  activation of the journal happens during install_partitions and it looks to not happen as desire to be activate at dbus call _activate future config._

*Actual Effects:*

With the actual code, what it is seen, it is that the multi-stage update will _took privileges_ to say that the “future config“ will be the active one in the next reboot although it is not desire, why because the multi-stage will happen right away without any hesitation and not check if that is possible/desire. 

_Possible:_ Means in error case during download process, it was seen that the journal goes written. At this journal should not be active by default in multi-stage update. 

Desire: Means when the activate_future_config is not set, that should not be done in any way. Multi-stage should not have the “privilege“ of overcome the activate future config by default



*That will create a change in multi-stage steps:*

*Until now:*

The multi-stage was running for the very beginning once the calculation of free size was detected that makes that the message of multistage is need comes and the stage 1 was set right away.

*The stage 1 was only downloading the expected sys and bspl*



*In the future:*

So far that the activate future config is done after each reboot, during the multi-stage update will happen the following. Igel-update will detect that it requires a multi-stage update and do nothing more that write the new future config and expect in the next reboot that will process correctly.

*The stage 1 will do the activation of the new journal + the download of the expected sys and bspl.* 



*Expectations:*

* Basically it is a stage 1 delay… from right away when it is detected, to activate future config
* The multi-stage config will be only activate during activate future config and set the (older) flags accordingly. 
* The procedure to “deprecate multistage during uninstall partitions“ needs to still working.



*Task:*

* Create a new journal entrance by configuration to mark that as true or false, 
* The active future config needs to set to prove this new entrance and react accordgly



*Acceptance criteria:*

* Normal update from one nightly without the new configuration of the journal to the newest one. (Topic that was comming always when the journal structure was changed.)
** Check that the update took place correctly.
** Check that the journal could be read in case of not having this entrance in the expected point
* Multistage in good case scenario should work. (Over UMS and over License)
* Multistage in error case should fail without issue. 
** Fail at stage 1: Error flag set and reboot
** Fail at stage 2: Errof flag set and reboot 
* Multistage “deprecation“ should still working. 
* Multistage from version with previous journal configuration to the newer one

column58:
h3. Environment

* Device Model: LG Gram 15ZT90P
* OSVersion: base_system-12.4.0+nightly.20240208.DEV
* State: Unmanaged

h3. Summary

When using the Fn keys to change volume of the speaker on the LG Gram the behaviour of the tray icon is not correct. It shows as muted for as long as the volume is below 2%. The steps after each press on the buttons increase non-linearly the higher the volume is and vice versa.

Additionally pressing the Fn key to mute speakers has no effect.

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Press any of the Fn keys regarding audio (F10, F11, F12)

h3. Current Behaviour

* Fn + F10 does not mute the speaker
* Fn + F11 / F12 (decrease / increase volume) has very small steps in the beginning that get larger the higher the volume is. At low volumes < 2% the tray icon still shows the muted symbol (On the test device 5 presses of the increase volume button are needed to reach 2%).

h3. Expected Behaviour

* Fn + F10 mutes speaker
* Fn + F11/F12 decreases volume in meaningful steps ([~accountid:712020:6a3446d6-af32-4ed2-988e-cc80a93d769d] suggests a constant size of 2%) and doesn’t show as muted below 2%

*Tasks*

* Correctly handle Mute action when set from outside systray
* Only show mute icon if device is actually muted or volume is 0%

column1: Remove obsolete touchrotate script
column58:
As */usr/bin/touchrotate* sets the same Transformation Matrix in the input device as /usr/bin/fix_touchscreen_matrix does we can remove touchrotate. /usr/bin/fix_touchscreen_matrix calls the *xinput map-to-input* command to the x output device. This is completely sufficient for multi monitor setups and also for rotated outputs.

Furthermore we must remove touchrotate as it is not capable to set a matrix for multi monitor setups.

column1: [igelpkgd] igelpkgctl: supply a hint on request for a downgrade if downgrades are inhibited
column58:
There is a feature with [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-7379|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-7379|smart-link] which ensures that the newest app version will activated at boot time.

Igelpkgctl should check this setting and give the user a warning or error if he wants to downgrade an app but downgrade is disabled by update.auto_update_on_boot .

Currently a user gets messages for a successful installation/downgrade, but after reboot the old higher version of the app is active once more. That causes much frustration…

*Tasks*

* Only auto update dependency apps → pin locally installed apps

Your proposal is problematic for all customers using there devices in unmanged mode as autou pdate is the default setting it will prevent manual installation of any app.

09/Apr/24 9:32 AM;712020:eb11546b-6213-4618-8a1d-69eff0c6a0f2;Hello Christian Werner, That approach… “Only updating apps with dependencies“, it is in my opinion dangerous, because the app installed by UMS or manually will bring its version on top (whatever they like to bring as required), but the dependencies part they are not checking which main app version is running, and maybe after 3 automatic updates only with dependencies you break the main app (the one with the requires), because its dependencies are not more compatible with it.

Maybe I am overseeing something but this is my penny about this topic.

09/Feb/24 4:44 PM;712020:df2f0ba2-c813-44fe-9898-d139e77439b8;I tested this with LG Gram Z15T90P - which has the same processor and graphics chip as the Z14T90P - and could not reproduce this problem.

How do I get 1.1.92 unpinned? Or was it wrongly pinned? I’m not sure if I get the point when and why versions are pinned in the repo!
column365:
07/Feb/24 11:42 AM;712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae;There is a command line parameter:

{noformat} -ld, --lock-debian-package-versions
                        Use the debian package versions from checksums{noformat}

This is used for release builds so it will always use the versions specified in the checksums.json which is automatically written when doing a build without this parameter. This is inspired by package-lock.json in npm, it allows to reproduce a previous build.

In order to workwround it without any pipeline process changes you need to either do a RC build which will honor the versions specified in debian.json and update the checksums.json or update the checksums.json manually with the version you want to use.

It might be possible to add a check if the previous version was a release or not and only lock the packages if the previous version was a release. But that might also fail in special cases it is not  that easy to get the previous version because you only are allowd to honor version with the same base.

Why are we building a release without RC and QA testing?

Well we did this since for CloudPC the QA does not have a test environment yet. So there was not point in doing an RC that no one will have a look at. This of course changes in the near future when QA has a test environment.

But still it is quite unexpected that doing a release build without a previous RC build silently uses a wrong package version. Can’t we add a version check here that makes sure we do get a package version that matches the requested one? And if that check fails, fail the build or just do the right thing?

column1: Restart of igel-rmagent-device-connect.service breaks auto reconnect
column58:
Restart of igel-rmagent-device-connect.service breaks auto reconnect - this is caused by the rmagent-check-reenroll command which is called by the igel-auto-renewal.timer. The command rmagent-check-reenroll requires a connected rmagent, so the rmagent is forced to connect before auto connector service what leads to this situation.

Solution: The command rmagent-check-reenroll mustn’t require a connection to the server.

column1: Switching between bluetooth HSP and A2DP does not work in OS12.4

If the Bluetooth headset connects it goes into A2DP mode and only works as Headphone this is the same as in OS12.3 so no surprise. I can also switch to HSP mode which then enables the microphone which is also okay.

But after this I can not choose the A2DP mode again and if I switch to another sound device like speaker or HDMI then I can not choose either HSP or A2DP entry of the bluetooth headset anymore. The entries are shown but you can not select them. Only solution is to disconnect the bluetooth device and reconnect it again to get it working again.

Did the same test with both headsets in OS12.3 and there it worked as expected so it is clearly a new issue in OS12.4.

column1: Soundmixer Test sound in OS12.4 plays testsounds in Mono

Rechecked this with OS12.3 and there it was correct (there the test sound also differs as you can activate it on each side and not in one go).

What I would have expected is that the both sound would play after each other but each only on the side of the headphone as it says so *front left* only on the left side and *front right* only on the right side. Otherwise it also would not make any sense to play both sounds.

column58:
If a connecting is responded with the 401 http code (Unauthorized), then the rmagent must try to reenroll the device certificate. Only if the reenrollment request is also responded with the 401, then the device releasing must be started by the rmagent.

This must avoid device releasing in such cases when the device certificate is expired during off time of the device.

column1: App download does not fallback to other configured portal addresses
column58:
The device uses the fallback addresses for the app download only after an update of the available apps.

Steps I made…

# I connected the OS12 device via an ICG to my UMS.
# Download from UMS for apps enabled.
# Did a ‘igelpkgctl update’.
# Installed an app. The app was downloaded from the UMS AppProxy.
# Switched off my UMS.
# Tried to install another app, but it failed.
# Did a ‘igelpkgctl update’.
# Now the app was installed fron the official AppPortal.

The configuration showed the official AppPortal with priority 100 and 110, the UMS with priority 200.

I would have expected that on a download failure the device automatically tries the next portal in the list.

*Task*

* Always update metadata before installing
* Remove existing check to update only if app is not found in cache
column362:
30/Jan/24 9:02 AM;712020:eb11546b-6213-4618-8a1d-69eff0c6a0f2;The igelpkgctl does not retriger any installation. It tooks the its metadata as it is and try the one with more priority. 

If for some reason this combination app/repo is not reachable… (Imagine UMS as proxy, without no real apps although the SQL/Data Base said other way around…, or the reason that you mention), it will not try with the other repo, why because we do implement it.



[~accountid:712020:ae26aad8-d2cf-440f-adae-bda0606aa3ae] or [~accountid:712020:ee35277e-d3b2-4b5d-8963-7393d33cf7fc] can confirmed to be 100% sure, but It works as expected.

column1: Tray / mobile broadband: no view change when unlocking PIN
column58:
*remarks*

* possible views: Unlocked, Details, SetApn, Locked
* transitions: change-by-user / PIN locked / PIN not-locked

*acceptance criteria*

* when user makes an explicit navigation to Details / SetApn, change view to Details / SetApn
* when data context changes into locked state, then change to Locked view
* when data context changes into not-locked state
** and current view is Locked view, then change to Unlocked view
** and current view is not Locked view, then do not change view
* initially, view should be set to Locked view, if data context is locked, otherwise to Unlocked view



*original ticket description*:

When unlocking the SIM in the UI, the view does never change away from the unlock-view.
I think this broke with this change:
[https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/pull-requests/379/diff#frontend/mobile-broadband/src/state/app/slice.ts?f=73|https://itga-bitbucket.igel.local/projects/LXIG/repos/igel-system-tray/pull-requests/379/diff#frontend/mobile-broadband/src/state/app/slice.ts?f=73]

This was changed to fix the following:

* connected mobile internet, user is currently on the details-view.
* datacontext update from the backend comes in → the view switches away from the details view (FAIL)
* user is surprised of this view-change without interaction, not good.
* happens mostly with signalStrength updates

We need another way to fix this.

Maybe the frontend must ignore signalstrength updates if not currently on the details-view

column1: Remove obsolete touchrotate call in user_display_xrandr
column58:
As */usr/bin/touchrotate* sets the same Transformation Matrix in the input device as /usr/bin/fix_touchscreen_matrix does we can remove touchrotate. /usr/bin/fix_touchscreen_matrix calls the *xinput map-to-input* command to the x output device. This is completely sufficient for multi monitor setups and also for rotated outputs.

Furthermore we must remove touchrotate as it is not capable to set a matrix for multi monitor setups.

column1: Emergency boot access to root shell despite password set
column58:
When a setup password (and optional local user password) is set, one can still achieve full root access to the system via emergency boot.

Steps to reproduce:

* configure root password, optional setup password, optional local user password
* boot in emergency/setup only mode
* login screen appears (either local user or setupw password dialog)
* change to vt11 or vt12 (Ctrl-Alt-F11 or F12)
* → no password required, root shell after pressing enter
** → *root password previously set is ignored!*

Suggested mitigation: disable vt switching in emergency mode completely (check if vtswitch from OSC can be re-used)

*Affects all current OS11 releases.*



Edit: OS12 12.3. and 12.2.1 do not seem to be affected.

column1: igelpkg: ownership of recursively created directories in dirs.json wrong
column58:
When creating a directory with dirs.json, the recursively created parent directories of said directory do not get the same ownership

*Expected Behavior:*

* /dir1 already existing
* create /dir1/dir2/dir3 in dirs.json with owner: 777:100 (user:users)
* dir2 and dir3 should have ownership user:users

*Observed Behavior:*

* /dir1 already existing
* create /dir1/dir2/dir3 in dirs.json with owner: 777:100 (user:users)
* dir2 has ownership root:root
* dir3 has ownership user:users

*Failed workarounds:*

* create /dir1/dir2 with owner: 700:100
* create /dir1/dir2 in input/all
* change ownership of /dir1/dir2 in prepackage_commands.sh (chown 777:100 %root%/userhome/.mozilla)

*Workaround:*

* change ownership after each boot (init service)

*Tasks:*

* change ownership of every recursively created new directory to the defined ownership
